## RWB-E1-020 Allocation and assignment engine v1

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-020 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-07 Run the allocation rule table; FEAT-CWC-08 Run the assignment engine by load and continuity; FEAT-CWC-09 Send a case to the overflow queue when no rule matches |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-007, REQ-CWC-008, REQ-CWC-009, REQ-CWC-016 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, section 5.3 |
| L3 process | 18.3.2 Allocate work to teams, people and partners by rule; 6.1 Take over the case at 90 days past due |
| Decision | D-RCV-36; ADR-011; ADR-012 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-019, RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-056, RWB-E1-072, RWB-E1-073 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **every new recovery case placed in a queue and given an owner by the ALLOCATION and ASSIGNMENT rule packages on the morning it arrives**, so that **each case at 90 days past due has one owner from its first day and nobody allocates cases by hand**.

### 2. Business rationale

Cases are allocated today from team spreadsheets, and ownership is agreed by email, so a case can wait days with no owner. This story places every new case in a queue and gives it an owner by rule before 07:00 on the morning after case creation, with the rule ID and the package version on a decision log entry. It meets REQ-CWC-007, REQ-CWC-008, REQ-CWC-009 and REQ-CWC-016, and serves the business measure "cases inside the service level" (target set with DL22) and control CTL-03.

Under D-RCV-36 (16 November 2026) package ALLOCATION decides the queue and package ASSIGNMENT decides the owner method, both through `RuleEvaluator` (RWB-E1-072), with first-match semantics (T5) and the package version chosen at evaluation time (T7). JOB-03 stays a Quartz job (T2). A rule change is a package version loaded and approved through RWB-E1-073, not a release.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-018 is done: new cases exist with status NEW, product group, region and exposure band.
- RWB-E1-019 is done: queues, queue members and caseload caps are loaded; queue "MTG-BKK-CO" belongs to team "MTG-BKK" and role RW-CASEOWN.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available through its published interface and accepts a rule ID with its rule version.
- RWB-E1-056 is done: JOB-03 has a run book and appears in the job monitor.
- RWB-E1-072 is done: `RuleEvaluator`, `RuleResult` and the package codes exist, and a package with no version in force throws NoPackageInForce.
- RWB-E1-073 is done: package ALLOCATION version "ALLOC-2026.11" is approved by RW-RISK, who is not the author, and is in force from 2026-11-30; package ASSIGNMENT version "ASSIGN-2026.11" is approved and in force from the same date. Each package has at least 50 passing scenarios. The ALLOCATION default row is the last row and its check is at load in RWB-E1-073.
- Every ALLOCATION row holds rule ID, product group, region, exposure band, target queue, valid from, valid to, approver and test case ID. Every ASSIGNMENT row holds queue code, method, cap, named owner and overflow queue.
- Parameters loaded through RWB-E1-042: `allocation.exception.queue.code` = "RWB-EXC" and `allocation.deviation.queue.code` = "DEV-HANDLER" (assumed values; DL23).
- JOB-02 case creation has completed for today's business date after v_ace_batch_status showed the ALS batch COMPLETED.
- The job runs as service identity SY-CASEWF; rules are evaluated as SY-RULES.

### 4. Flow

1. Quartz (D-RCV-36 T2): starts JOB-03 Morning allocation after JOB-02 completes for business date 2026-12-01.
2. AllocationJob: selects every case with status NEW whose last allocation date is before the business date.
3. AllocationService: locks the case row and reads deviation_open; a case with an open deviation goes to the deviation handler queue (R-DEV-01).
4. AllocationService: builds `AllocationFacts` from the case and calls `RuleEvaluator.evaluate("ALLOCATION", facts, businessDate)`; the evaluator returns the first matching rule in row order (T5), its rule ID and package version, and the target queue in `outputs`.
5. AllocationService: fills the target queue code and cap in the same facts object and calls `RuleEvaluator.evaluate("ASSIGNMENT", facts, businessDate)` for that queue; the row returns the assignment method, the cap and, for NAMED_OWNER, the owner. AssignmentEngine counts the open cases of each queue member and picks the first owner below the cap by the method.
6. AllocationService: in one transaction sets queue, team, owner, status ASSIGNED, stage clock start, allocation rule ID and package version, writes the assignment with reason ALLOCATION and the assignment rule ID and package version, sets the last allocation date and writes CaseAllocated (EV-02) to the outbox.
7. AllocationService: as the last step before commit, calls DecisionLogWriter.write with the allocation rule ID, package version, queue, owner and inputs; a failed write rolls the allocation back.
8. AllocationJob: after the last case, builds the allocation summary per team (MSG-P3-011, MSG-P3-012) and sends it to the team manager through the ACE notification path.
9. AllocationJob: records the run result (cases read, assigned, overflow, exception, failed) on the job record for the monitor.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Every owner in the target queue is at or above the cap | Case goes to the overflow queue named by the ASSIGNMENT row; status stays NEW; counted in the summary | MSG-P3-011 | AC4 |
| X2 | No ALLOCATION rule matches the case | Case goes to the exception queue; status stays NEW; rule gap logged; CaseAllocationFailed (EV-03) published | MSG-P3-012 | AC5 |
| X3 | Decision log write fails | Allocation rolled back; case stays NEW with no queue change; retried in the next run | MSG-P3-013 | AC6 |
| X4 | Case has deviation_open = true | Case goes to the deviation handler queue; no case owner is chosen | None | AC7 |
| X5 | The run is repeated for the same business date | Cases already allocated for that date are skipped; no second assignment or log entry | None | AC8 |
| X6 | No case has status NEW | Run completes with zero counts; summary says 0 | MSG-P3-011, MSG-P3-012 with count 0 | AC9 |
| X7 | JOB-02 has not completed for the business date | JOB-03 does not start; job monitor shows it waiting; cases stay NEW | MSG-P1-001 | AC10 |
| X8 | A rerun starts while the first run still holds a case | The case row lock stops the second worker; each case is allocated once | None | AC11 |
| X9 | The ASSIGNMENT row names no overflow queue and every owner is at the cap | Case goes to the exception queue with the reason "no overflow queue" | MSG-P3-012 | AC13 |
| X10 | A user without the right reruns JOB-03 | Refused with 403; nothing runs | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-020-14 |

A package with no version in force is refused by `RuleEvaluator` before any case is touched (NoPackageInForce, MSG-P3-027; RWB-E1-072); it stops the run and is not a per-case exception path.

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the case record (RWB-E1-018), the roles, teams and queues table (RWB-E1-019), the decision log writer (RWB-E1-027), the job monitoring (RWB-E1-056), the Drools evaluator (RWB-E1-072) and the package load (RWB-E1-073), all earlier in Epic 1 |
| Negotiable | The allocation rows, the assignment method per queue, the cap and the queue codes are data values. The story fixes the behavior, not the values |
| Valuable | Ends allocation from spreadsheets for every new case, about 3,110 a month (DL15) |
| Estimable | Two packages, one service, one batch step, no screen |
| Small | Can be finished in two weeks or less with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Allocate a new recovery case to a queue and an owner

  Background:
    Given package ALLOCATION version "ALLOC-2026.11" is in force from 2026-11-30
    Given package ASSIGNMENT version "ASSIGN-2026.11" is in force and gives queue "MTG-BKK-CO" the method "ROUND_ROBIN" with a caseload cap of 150
    Given the queue "MTG-BKK-CO" belongs to team "MTG-BKK" and role RW-CASEOWN
    Given the queue "MTG-BKK-CO" has the overflow queue "MTG-BKK-OVF"
    Given the business date is 2026-12-01

  Scenario: AC1 A new case is placed in the queue its rule names
    Given a new case RW-2026-000201 with status "NEW", product group "MORTGAGE", region "BKK" and exposure band "B2"
    Given allocation rule "ALLOC-014" matches product group "MORTGAGE", region "BKK" and any exposure band, with target queue "MTG-BKK-CO"
    When the morning allocation run starts
    Then the system places the case in queue "MTG-BKK-CO"
    Then the case team is "MTG-BKK" and the region is "BKK"

  Scenario: AC2 The owner is chosen by the assignment rule
    Given queue "MTG-BKK-CO" holds three case owners U-01, U-02 and U-03 with 120, 95 and 140 open cases
    Given the last owner given a case in the queue was U-02
    When case RW-2026-000201 is placed in the queue
    Then the system gives the case to U-03
    Then the case status becomes "ASSIGNED"
    Then the system writes an assignment record with reason "ALLOCATION", allocation rule ID "ALLOC-014" and assignment rule ID "ASSIGN-007"

  Scenario: AC3 An owner at the caseload cap is skipped
    Given the last owner given a case was U-02
    Given U-03, the next owner in turn, holds 150 open cases
    Given U-01 holds 120 open cases
    When case RW-2026-000202 is placed in the queue
    Then the system gives the case to U-01, the following owner below the cap

  Scenario: AC4 Every owner is at the cap
    Given U-01, U-02 and U-03 each hold 150 open cases
    When case RW-2026-000203 is placed in queue "MTG-BKK-CO"
    Then the system places the case in the overflow queue "MTG-BKK-OVF"
    Then the case status stays "NEW" and no owner is set
    Then the team manager of "MTG-BKK" receives the allocation summary with MSG-P3-011 and count 1

  Scenario: AC5 No allocation rule matches
    Given a new case RW-2026-000204 with product group "SSME" and region "NE3" that matches no allocation rule
    When the morning allocation run starts
    Then the system places the case in the exception queue "RWB-EXC"
    Then the case status stays "NEW"
    Then the system writes a decision log entry with final call "RULE_GAP", product group "SSME" and region "NE3"
    Then the system publishes caseAllocationFailed with reason "NO_ROW_MATCHED"
    Then the allocation summary carries MSG-P3-012 with count 1

  Scenario: AC6 Every allocation is logged
    Given case RW-2026-000205 matches rule "ALLOC-014" and owner U-02 is below the cap
    When the case is placed in the queue and given an owner
    Then the system writes one decision log entry with rule ID "ALLOC-014", package version "ALLOC-2026.11", queue "MTG-BKK-CO", owner U-02 and the inputs used
    Then the assignment row carries assignment rule ID "ASSIGN-007" and package version "ASSIGN-2026.11"
    Then if the decision log write fails, the allocation is not made, the case stays "NEW" with no queue and the job record carries MSG-P3-013 for the case

  Scenario: AC7 A case with an open deviation is not allocated to a case owner
    Given a new case RW-2026-000206 with deviation_open = true
    When the morning allocation run starts
    Then the system places the case in the deviation handler queue "DEV-HANDLER" named by rule R-DEV-01
    Then the system sets no case owner and the status stays "NEW"

  Scenario: AC8 A repeated run for the same date has no further effect
    Given the morning allocation run for 2026-12-01 has assigned case RW-2026-000201 to U-03
    When the run for 2026-12-01 is started again from the job monitor
    Then case RW-2026-000201 keeps owner U-03 and its one assignment record
    Then the system writes no second decision log entry for the case
    Then the job record shows 1 case skipped as already allocated

  Scenario: AC9 A run with no new cases
    Given no case has status "NEW" on 2026-12-01
    When the morning allocation run starts
    Then the run completes with 0 cases read
    Then the allocation summary for each team shows 0 in overflow and 0 in the exception queue

  Scenario: AC10 The run waits for case creation
    Given JOB-02 has not completed for 2026-12-01 because v_ace_batch_status holds no COMPLETED ALS row for that date
    When 07:00 passes
    Then JOB-03 has not started for 2026-12-01
    Then the job monitor shows JOB-03 waiting on JOB-02 with MSG-P1-001
    Then every NEW case keeps no queue and no owner

  Scenario: AC11 Two runs at the same time allocate each case once
    Given a first run is allocating case RW-2026-000207
    When a rerun for 2026-12-01 reaches the same case at the same time
    Then the rerun skips the locked case
    Then the case has exactly one assignment record and one decision log entry for 2026-12-01

  Scenario: AC12 An owner one case below the cap gets the case
    Given U-03 is next in turn and holds 149 open cases
    When case RW-2026-000208 is placed in queue "MTG-BKK-CO"
    Then the system gives the case to U-03
    Then U-03 now holds 150 open cases

  Scenario: AC13 A queue with no overflow queue sends the case to the exception queue
    Given the ASSIGNMENT row for queue "HP-CEN-CO" names no overflow queue
    Given every owner in queue "HP-CEN-CO" holds 150 open cases
    When case RW-2026-000209 is placed in queue "HP-CEN-CO"
    Then the system places the case in the exception queue "RWB-EXC" with reason "NO_OVERFLOW_QUEUE"
    Then the case status stays "NEW"
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A case is allocated by the first rule of package ALLOCATION, in row order, whose product group, region and exposure band match the case. First match follows D-RCV-36 T5 and "Any" in a column matches every value | Package ALLOCATION; D-RCV-36 T5; DL24; REQ-CWC-008 |
| BR2 | The owner is chosen by the ASSIGNMENT rule for the queue, whose outputs hold the method: ROUND_ROBIN, LOWEST_LOAD, NAMED_OWNER or SKILL, and the cap | Package ASSIGNMENT; queue.assignment_method (DF-WRK-006), LOV-ASSIGN |
| BR3 | An owner at or above the queue's caseload cap is skipped. Open cases are cases in the queue owned by the person with status other than CLOSED | queue.capacity_cap (DF-WRK-007); values DL23 |
| BR4 | A case that cannot be given an owner goes to the overflow queue named in the ASSIGNMENT row | queue.overflow_queue_id (DF-WRK-008) |
| BR5 | A case that matches no rule goes to the exception queue, and the gap is logged. R-UNI-41 handles the case once a person decides | R-UNI-41; FEAT-CWC-09 |
| BR6 | A case with an open deviation goes to the deviation handler queue | R-DEV-01 |
| BR7 | A decision that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR8 | A case is allocated at most once per business date | R-UNI-40; events.txt rule "Duplicates" |
| BR9 | Each allocation records the ALLOCATION rule ID and package version on the decision log entry, and the ASSIGNMENT rule ID and package version on the assignment row | REQ-CWC-016; CTL-03; D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR10 | The ALLOCATION package always has a default row as its last row; the check is at load in RWB-E1-073 and is not repeated at run time | REQ-CWC-008; D-RCV-36 T5 |

### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| New | Allocation rule matched | ALLOCATION rule matched and the ASSIGNMENT rule gives an owner below the cap | Assigned |
| New | Allocation rule matched | ALLOCATION rule matched and every owner at the cap | New, in the overflow queue |
| New | Allocation rule matched | No ALLOCATION rule matched | New, in the exception queue |
| New | DEVIATION_FLAGGED (R-DEV-01) | deviation_open = true | New, in the deviation handler queue |

### 12. Contract

**Job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Quartz (D-RCV-36 T2), after JOB-02 completes for the business date |
| Job name | JOB-03 Morning allocation |
| Schedule | Daily after JOB-02, complete by 07:00 Asia/Bangkok |
| Input | Cases with status NEW and last_allocation_date before the business date; ALLOCATION and ASSIGNMENT package versions in force on the business date, through `RuleEvaluator` (RWB-E1-072); queues and queue members |
| Output | Case queue, team, owner, status, allocation rule ID and package version; assignment rows with the assignment rule ID and package version; decision log entries; allocation summary per team; job record with counts |
| Events published | CaseAllocated (EV-02: caseId, queueId, ownerId, ruleId, ruleVersion), where ruleVersion is the ALLOCATION package version label; CaseAllocationFailed (EV-03: caseId, reason, ruleGap) |
| Idempotency key | caseId and businessDate. A case with last_allocation_date equal to the business date is skipped |
| Restart | Rerun from the job monitor (POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun). A rerun processes only cases not yet allocated for the date. Chunk commit per case, so a failure in one case does not undo the others |

**Endpoint used to read the result**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Method and path | GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId} |
| Request | Path caseId (uuid) |
| Response | Case: queueId, teamCode, ownerUserId, status, ruleVersion |
| Errors | 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 role lacks Case record R (MSG-P4-002); 404 not found or outside scope (MSG-P4-003); 503 store unavailable |
| Authorization | Case record, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

`ruleVersion` in the response is the ALLOCATION package version label.

**Endpoint used to rerun the job (P1)**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Method and path | POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun |
| Response | Job: id, type, businessDate, status, checks |
| Errors | 401; 403 role lacks Platform administration U (MSG-P4-002); 404 job not found; 409 job already running (MSG-GEN-004) |
| Authorization | Platform administration, right U |
| Idempotency | The rerun follows the job's idempotency key above |

**Published interfaces**

```java
// P3, package recovery.casewf.allocation (published)
public interface AllocationService {
    AllocationOutcome allocate(UUID caseId, LocalDate businessDate);
}
public record AllocationOutcome(UUID caseId, OutcomeType type, UUID queueId,
        UUID ownerUserId, String ruleId, String ruleVersion, String reason) {}
public enum OutcomeType { ASSIGNED, OVERFLOW, EXCEPTION, DEVIATION_QUEUE, SKIPPED, FAILED_LOG }

// P3, package recovery.casewf.rules (published; RWB-E1-072)
public interface RuleEvaluator {
    RuleResult evaluate(String packageCode, Object facts, LocalDate onDate); // throws NoPackageInForce
}
public record RuleResult(String packageCode, String packageVersion, String ruleId, Map<String,Object> outputs) {}

// P7, used by this story (RWB-E1-027)
// package recovery.decision.writer; called inside the caller's transaction as the last step before commit
public interface DecisionLogWriter {
    DecisionLogEntryRef write(DecisionLogRecord record)
        throws DecisionLogRecordInvalidException, DecisionLogUnavailableException;
}

// P3, facts built by this story (not published)
public record AllocationFacts(String caseNo, String productGroup, String regionCode, String exposureBand,
        int daysPastDue, boolean deviationOpen, String queueCode, int capacityCap) {}
```

`AllocationOutcome.ruleId` and `.ruleVersion` are those of the ALLOCATION package; the assignment row carries the ALLOCATION rule ID and the ASSIGNMENT rule ID with its package version. `NoPackageInForce` is a checked exception with messageId MSG-P3-027 and the package code.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `src/main/java/.../recovery/casewf/allocation`, Java package `recovery.casewf.allocation`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AllocationJob | Job | Quartz job for JOB-03; selects NEW cases, calls AllocationService per case, builds the summary, writes job counts |
| AllocationService | Published interface | Implementation AllocationServiceImpl: lock, deviation check, two `RuleEvaluator` calls, owner choice, decision log write, case update, outbox event |
| AllocationFacts | Fact record | The fact object passed to `RuleEvaluator`: case number, product group, region, exposure band, days past due, deviation flag, queue code and cap |
| AssignmentEngine | Service | Applies the method and cap from the ASSIGNMENT row, counts open cases and picks the first owner below the cap |
| OwnerLoadRepository | Repository | Counts open cases per owner in a queue (ix_case_owner_status) |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | Reads and updates recovery_case, queue, queue_member, assignment |
| AllocationSummaryBuilder | Service | Counts overflow and exception cases per team; fills MSG-P3-011 and MSG-P3-012 |
| RuleEvaluator | Published interface | Evaluates ALLOCATION and ASSIGNMENT (RWB-E1-072); no version in force throws NoPackageInForce |

**Database**

- Reads: recovery_case (id, case_no, product_group, region_code, exposure_band, deviation_open, status, last_allocation_date), queue (id, queue_code, team_code, role_code, assignment_method, capacity_cap, overflow_queue_id), queue_member (user_id, capacity).
- Writes: recovery_case (status, owner_user_id, queue_id, team_code, stage_clock_start, rule_version, last_allocation_date, version), queue (rr_cursor_user_id), assignment (all columns), outbox.
- Lock: `SELECT ... FROM recovery_case WHERE id = ? AND status = 'NEW' FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; optimistic version column on update.
- Migration in this story: `V020_1__allocation_columns.sql` adds recovery_case.last_allocation_date (date) and queue.rr_cursor_user_id (uuid). queue_member is created by RWB-E1-019.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Package ALLOCATION version "ALLOC-2026.11" and package ASSIGNMENT version "ASSIGN-2026.11", prepared by RW-REFADM, loaded by RW-COE and approved by RW-RISK through RWB-E1-073; the Shared operations process owner approves the change.
- Queues and members from RWB-E1-019; caps DL23.
- Parameters from RWB-E1-042: `allocation.exception.queue.code`, `allocation.deviation.queue.code`.
- Lists LOV-ASSIGN, LOV-ASSIGN-REASON, LOV-CASE-STATUS (P4 lov_value).

**Build steps**

1. AllocationFacts and the `RuleEvaluator` call for ALLOCATION: given a case snapshot and a package version, return the first matching rule, its rule ID and package version, or none. Unit tests per BR1 with "any" values.
2. The `RuleEvaluator` call for ASSIGNMENT and AssignmentEngine: apply the row's method with cap skipping and the round robin cursor. Unit tests for AC2, AC3, AC12 boundary.
3. OwnerLoadRepository: open case count per owner and queue; integration test on PostgreSQL with Testcontainers.
4. AllocationServiceImpl: lock, deviation branch, two evaluator calls, overflow and exception branches, then case update, assignment and outbox row in one transaction with the decision log write as its last step.
5. Idempotency: skip when last_allocation_date equals the business date; return SKIPPED.
6. AllocationJob: Quartz job with `@DisallowConcurrentExecution`, dependency on JOB-02 completion, per-case transaction, job counts.
7. AllocationSummaryBuilder and the call to the ACE notification path for each team manager.
8. System tests TC-E1-020-01 to TC-E1-020-15 on the synthetic case set. The default row check is not tested here; RWB-E1-073 covers it.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.allocation`. Off: JOB-03 does not run and cases stay NEW.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; TC-E1-020-01 and TC-E1-020-08 are in the regression suite; every decision log entry names the ALLOCATION rule ID and package version; JOB-03 finishes 3,110 synthetic cases inside 15 minutes in SIT (assumed target; DL11).

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-011 | Allocation summary, case in overflow | {count} new cases are waiting in the overflow queue for {team}. Every owner is at the caseload cap. |
| MSG-P3-012 | Allocation summary, no rule matched | {count} new cases matched no allocation rule and are in the exception queue. |
| MSG-P3-013 | Decision log write failed for a case | The case was not allocated because the decision could not be recorded. It will be tried again in the next run. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No ALLOCATION or ASSIGNMENT version is in force at the run | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P1-001 | JOB-03 waiting because the ACE batch has not completed | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right reruns the job | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10. For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value is "package in force" and the {detail} names the package code only.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: product groups, regions, bands, queues, methods, caps and queue codes are data in the packages, the queue table and the parameters.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts. Cases are named by case number only.
- No read of another module's tables; ACE data only through `recovery.v_ace_*` views: rule packages come through `RuleEvaluator` (P3, RWB-E1-072); the decision log through `DecisionLogWriter` (P7).
- One evaluator: ALLOCATION and ASSIGNMENT are evaluated only through `RuleEvaluator`; no code reads `drl_source`, the workbook or a rule_row row directly (D-RCV-36 T3, T6).
- The default row check is not repeated at run time; it is at load in RWB-E1-073 (D-RCV-36 T5).
- The decision log entry is written in the same transaction as the case change; a failed write leaves the case unchanged.
- JOB-03 stays on Quartz in Epic 1 and Epic 2 (D-RCV-36 T2); no case wait moves to Temporal in this story.

## RWB-E1-021 Transfer rules and engine v1

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-021 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-10 Run the transfer rule table and engine |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-010, REQ-CWC-016 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, section 5.3 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | D-RCV-36; ADR-011; ADR-012 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-028, RWB-E1-020, RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-072, RWB-E1-073 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **cases moved between queues and roles by the TRANSFER rule package on stage change, route decided, timer expired, deviation raised or cleared, approval needed, document received, payment missed, or a manual request with a reason**, so that **hand-offs between teams run without email**.

### 2. Business rationale

A case changes hands between the TDR, litigation, NPA and debt sale teams by email today, and the case can wait between teams with nobody holding it. This story moves the case by rule when one of eight triggers fires, picks the owner in the receiving queue, ends the old assignment and records the rule ID and package version, and gives the team manager a programmatic transfer with a coded reason before the Epic 2 screens. It meets REQ-CWC-010 and REQ-CWC-016.

Under D-RCV-36 (16 November 2026) the transfer rules are package TRANSFER, evaluated by `RuleEvaluator` with first-match semantics (T5); the eight triggers arrive as one `TransferTrigger` fact. The manual transfer API does not change; it keeps its endpoint, request, response, errors and authorization. A rule change is a package version loaded and approved through RWB-E1-073, not a release.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-020 is done: AssignmentEngine and the queue structure are in use.
- RWB-E1-028 is done: timers publish TimerDue when a timer other than a service level expires. A service level breach (TimerBreached) never moves the case (R-UNI-30).
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available and accepts a rule ID with its rule version.
- RWB-E1-072 is done: `RuleEvaluator` and `RuleResult` are published, and a package with no version in force throws NoPackageInForce.
- RWB-E1-073 is done: package TRANSFER version "TRF-2026.11" is approved by RW-RISK, who is not the author, and is in force from 2026-11-30, with at least 50 passing scenarios. Each row holds trigger event, condition, target queue code and row order (D-RCV-36 T5).
- The transfer reason list LOV-TRANSFER-REASON holds R01 Capacity, R02 Customer deceased, R03 Skill, R04 Owner absent, R05 Legal referral and R06 Wrong queue (DL23).
- Manual transfer callers hold Queue and allocation U (RW-TEAMMGR, RW-CAPACITY). Hold and release callers hold Case record U (for example RW-LITOFF acting on a Legal instruction).

### 4. Flow

1. Event source: writes a trigger event to the outbox: CaseStateChanged for a stage change or a route decided (rule event ROUTE_APPROVED), TimerDue, DeviationRaised, DeviationCleared, ApprovalRequested, DocumentStored or PaymentMissed.
2. TransferListener: receives the event once per event ID; a repeated event ID is ignored (R-UNI-40), and builds one `TransferTrigger` fact for the event and the case snapshot.
3. RuleEvaluator (SY-RULES): calls `RuleEvaluator.evaluate("TRANSFER", trigger, businessDate)` for the `TransferTrigger` and returns the first matching rule in row order (T5), its rule ID and package version; no match means no transfer and no decision log entry.
4. TransferService: skips an automated transfer when legal_hold is true (R-UNI-20) and logs the skip.
5. TransferService: locks the case by its version, picks the owner in the target queue with AssignmentEngine, and checks the move is allowed from the case status.
6. TransferService: in one transaction ends the open assignment, writes the new assignment (reason TRANSFER and the rule ID), updates queue, team and owner, and writes CaseTransferred (EV-04).
7. TransferService: as the last step before commit, writes the decision log entry with the rule ID, package version, from and to queue and owner, and the trigger.
8. Team manager: calls POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer with reason code MANUAL, transfer reason R03 and a target owner or queue; steps 5 and 6 run with reason MANUAL and step 7 writes the decision log entry with the caller, the reason and the target, and no rule ID. The endpoint, the request, the response, the errors and the authorization are unchanged.
9. Litigation officer: calls POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold with action place or lift; the case goes to On hold or back to the status it paused in.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Two transfers reach the same case in the same second | First commits; second refused on the version check and logged as rejected | MSG-GEN-004 | AC3 |
| X2 | Manual transfer without a transfer reason | Refused with 422; nothing changes | MSG-P3-001 | AC6 |
| X3 | Named target owner at the caseload cap | Refused with 422; nothing changes | MSG-P3-002 | AC7 |
| X4 | Transfer of a closed case | Refused with 409 | MSG-P3-005 | AC8 |
| X5 | Decision log write fails | Refused with 503 for a manual call; event retried for a rule transfer; nothing changes | MSG-P7-003 | AC9 |
| X6 | Rule trigger arrives while legal_hold is true | No automated transfer; skip logged | None | AC10 |
| X7 | The same event arrives twice | Second ignored; one transfer | None | AC11 |
| X8 | No owner below the cap in the target queue | Case placed in the target queue's overflow queue with no owner; team manager told | MSG-P3-011 | AC12 |
| X9 | Hold placed on a case already on hold | Refused with 409 | MSG-P3-005 | AC13 |
| X10 | No TRANSFER rule matches the event | No transfer; nothing logged as a decision | None | AC14 |
| X11 | A role without Queue and allocation U calls the transfer | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-021-15 |

A TRANSFER version not in force is refused by `RuleEvaluator` before the case is touched (NoPackageInForce, MSG-P3-027; RWB-E1-072). The trigger event stays in the outbox and is retried when a version is in force; it is not a per-case exception path.

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on the assignment engine (RWB-E1-020), the timer events (RWB-E1-028), the Drools evaluator (RWB-E1-072) and the package load (RWB-E1-073); no screen |
| Negotiable | Trigger rows, target queues and the reason list are data |
| Valuable | Removes email hand-offs between the six recovery teams |
| Estimable | One listener, one service, one package, two endpoints |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A case moves by the first TRANSFER rule, in row order, whose trigger and condition match. First match follows D-RCV-36 T5 | Package TRANSFER; REQ-CWC-010 |
| BR2 | The eight triggers are stage change, route decided, timer expired, deviation raised, deviation cleared, approval needed, document received and payment missed. They arrive as one TransferTrigger fact with an event code; a manual request is a separate call with a caller-supplied reason | REQ-CWC-010; events EV-05, EV-06, EV-07, EV-09, EV-12, EV-16, EV-18; D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR3 | A manual transfer needs a transfer reason from the list | LOV-TRANSFER-REASON (assumed); REQ-WKM-003; VR-P3-010-1 |
| BR4 | A transfer to an owner at the cap is refused | queue.capacity_cap; VR-P3-010-2 |
| BR5 | A case is in exactly one queue with one open assignment | REQ-CWC-005 |
| BR6 | No automated transfer while a legal hold is in force | R-UNI-20 |
| BR7 | Lifting a hold returns the case to the status it paused in | R-UNI-21; casemodel.txt status transitions |
| BR8 | An event with the same ID is processed once | R-UNI-40 |
| BR9 | Every rule transfer is logged with the rule ID and package version, and every manual transfer with its caller and reason, before it takes effect | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; REQ-CWC-016; D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR10 | A transfer keeps the case status and the clocks | R-UNI-18 (same principle for reallocation) |
| BR11 | The manual transfer API is unchanged: endpoint, request, response, errors and authorization stay as they are | REQ-CWC-010 |
| BR12 | A TRANSFER version not in force leaves the trigger event in the outbox and moves no case; it is never a default transfer | R-UNI-41; D-RCV-36 T5 |

### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| New, Assigned, In progress, any Waiting | LEGAL_HOLD_PLACED (R-UNI-20) | Placed through the legal-hold endpoint | On hold |
| On hold | LEGAL_HOLD_LIFTED (R-UNI-21) | Lifted through the legal-hold endpoint | The status it paused in |

A rule or manual transfer changes the queue, the team and the owner, not the status.

### 12. Contract

**POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/transfer**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | TransferRequest: toOwnerId (uuid) or toQueueId (uuid), reasonCode = "MANUAL", note, and transferReasonCode (new field, LOV-TRANSFER-REASON) |
| Response | 200 Assignment: id, caseId, assigneeUserId, assignedAt, reason, ruleId |
| Errors | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Queue and allocation U (MSG-P4-002); 404 not found or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 409 status does not allow the move (MSG-P3-005) or version changed (MSG-GEN-004); 422 no reason (MSG-P3-001), owner at cap (MSG-P3-002); 503 decision not recorded (MSG-P7-003) |
| Authorization | Queue and allocation, right U, scope Team |
| Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header; a repeat with the same key returns the first response |

The manual transfer request, response, errors and authorization are unchanged by this rewrite.

**POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-hold**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | LegalHoldRequest: action (place, lift), reason (required), reference |
| Response | 200 Case with status and legalHold |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Case record U (MSG-P4-002); 404; 409 already on hold or not on hold (MSG-P3-005); 503 (MSG-P7-003) |
| Authorization | Case record, right U, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header |

**Events.** Consumes CaseStateChanged (EV-05), DeviationRaised (EV-06), DeviationCleared (EV-07), ApprovalRequested (EV-09), PaymentMissed (EV-12), DocumentStored (EV-16), TimerDue (EV-18). Publishes CaseTransferred (EV-04: caseId, fromOwner, toOwner, reasonCode, ruleId) and CaseStateChanged (EV-05) for hold and release.

**Published interface**

```java
// P3, package recovery.casewf.transfer (published)
public interface TransferService {
    TransferResult transferByRule(UUID caseId, String triggerEvent, UUID eventId);
    TransferResult transferManual(UUID caseId, ManualTransfer request, UUID callerId, String idempotencyKey);
    CaseView placeLegalHold(UUID caseId, String reason, String reference, UUID callerId);
    CaseView liftLegalHold(UUID caseId, String reason, UUID callerId);
}

// P3, package recovery.casewf.rules (published; RWB-E1-072)
public interface RuleEvaluator {
    RuleResult evaluate(String packageCode, Object facts, LocalDate onDate); // throws NoPackageInForce
}
public record RuleResult(String packageCode, String packageVersion, String ruleId, Map<String,Object> outputs) {}

// P3, fact built by this story (not published)
public record TransferTrigger(String eventCode, String caseNo, String stageCode, String routeCode,
        String deviationState, boolean legalHold) {}
```

`NoPackageInForce` is a checked exception with messageId MSG-P3-027 and the package code. `TransferResult` carries the rule ID and package version returned by `RuleEvaluator`.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `recovery/casewf/transfer`, Java package `recovery.casewf.transfer`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TransferListener | Listener | Reads the eight trigger events from the outbox, deduplicates by event ID, builds the TransferTrigger fact and calls transferByRule |
| TransferTrigger | Fact record | The fact object for package TRANSFER: event code, case number, stage, route, deviation state and legal hold |
| TransferService | Published interface | Lock, hold check, `RuleEvaluator` call, owner choice, decision log, assignment swap, event |
| RuleEvaluator | Published interface | Evaluates package TRANSFER for a TransferTrigger (RWB-E1-072); no version in force throws NoPackageInForce |
| LegalHoldService | Service | Place and lift with status_before_hold |
| CaseAndWorkflowController | Controller | POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer and POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | recovery_case, assignment, queue, processed event IDs |

**Database**

- Writes recovery_case (queue_id, team_code, owner_user_id, status, legal_hold, status_before_hold, rule_version, version), assignment (end the open row, insert the new row), processed_event (event_id unique), outbox.
- Update with `WHERE id = ? AND version = ?`; zero rows updated means the version changed (MSG-GEN-004).
- Constraint: partial unique index `ux_assignment_open_case ON assignment (case_id) WHERE ended_at IS NULL AND task_id IS NULL`.
- Migration in this story: `V021_1__transfer.sql` adds recovery_case.status_before_hold, assignment.transfer_reason_code, the partial unique index and table processed_event (event_id uuid primary key, consumer varchar(60), processed_at).

**Configuration and reference data**

- Package TRANSFER version "TRF-2026.11", loaded by RW-COE and approved by RW-RISK through RWB-E1-073.
- LOV-TRANSFER-REASON (R01 to R06; DL23) loaded by RW-REFADM through RWB-E1-043.
- Queues from RWB-E1-019.

**Build steps**

1. TransferTrigger and the `RuleEvaluator` call, with unit tests for each trigger (AC4), no match (AC14) and a version not in force (BR12).
2. TransferService.transferByRule with version lock, hold check and assignment swap; tests AC1, AC3, AC10, AC12.
3. TransferListener with processed_event deduplication; test AC11.
4. transferManual with reason and cap validation; tests AC2, AC6, AC7, AC8.
5. LegalHoldService place and lift; tests AC5, AC13.
6. Decision log write as the last step of each transaction, including the rejected transfer; test AC9.
7. Controller endpoints with access checks and Idempotency-Key; access test.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.transfer`. Off: no rule transfers and the two endpoints return 404.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, each of the eight triggers moves a case in SIT, every rule transfer decision log entry names the TRANSFER rule ID and package version, and every manual transfer entry names the caller and reason.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-001 | Manual transfer without a reason | Choose a reason for the transfer. |
| MSG-P3-002 | Target owner at the cap | {owner} is at the caseload cap. Choose another owner or the team queue. |
| MSG-P3-005 | Move not allowed from the status | This case cannot move to {state} from {current}. |
| MSG-P3-011 | Target queue full, case in overflow | {count} new cases are waiting in the overflow queue for {team}. Every owner is at the caseload cap. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No TRANSFER version is in force for a rule trigger | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Second transfer on a changed record | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value is "package in force" and the {detail} names the package code only.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: triggers, target queues and the reason list are data in the TRANSFER package and the list.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts.
- No read of another module's tables; ACE data only through `recovery.v_ace_*` views: trigger events arrive through the outbox; the rule package comes through `RuleEvaluator` (RWB-E1-072).
- One evaluator: TRANSFER is evaluated only through `RuleEvaluator`; no trigger list, row order or target queue is written in code (D-RCV-36 T3, T5).
- The manual transfer API keeps its request, response, errors and authorization.
- A transfer never resets the stage clock or the prescription date.
- JOB-05 and the timer events stay on Quartz in Epic 1 and Epic 2 (D-RCV-36 T2); no case wait moves to Temporal in this story.

### 18. Traceability

| Requirement ID | Requirement (short) | BRD section | Feature | L3 process | Rules | Test cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-CWC-010 | Transfer by rule on eight triggers and manual request with a reason | Epic 1, 3.3; Program, 5.3 | FEAT-CWC-10 | All recovery processes | R-UNI-20, R-UNI-21, R-UNI-40 | TC-E1-021-01 to TC-E1-021-14 |
| REQ-CWC-016 | Every transfer logged with rule ID and version | Epic 1, 3.3; Program, 5.3 | FEAT-CWC-10 | All recovery processes | R-UNI-39 | TC-E1-021-01, TC-E1-021-03, TC-E1-021-09, TC-E1-021-16 |

### 19. Out of scope

- The transfer screen and queue history on the case (RWB-E2-012, RWB-E2-016).
- Reallocation when an owner leaves or passes the cap (Epic 2, R-UNI-18, R-UNI-19).
- Escalation of a breached timer without moving the case (RWB-E1-028).
- The route decision itself (Epic 4).
- From Epic 3 the trigger arrives as a Temporal signal (ADR-011), not from the outbox listener.
- Loading, validating, approving and rolling back the TRANSFER package (RWB-E1-073).

| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-019 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **to sign in to the Workbench once through Entra ID with multi-factor authentication and see only the screens and actions my Workbench roles allow**, so that **access is controlled from the first release and nobody holds a Workbench password or a local account**.

### 2. Business rationale

Access to recovery data today is granted system by system, and the bank cannot show who could see a case on a given date. This story makes Entra ID group membership the only way to hold a Workbench role: one group per role per environment, granted through the bank IAM, read at each sign-in and turned into a session with roles, scope and the permission matrix version in force. It meets REQ-ACA-001, REQ-ACA-002 and REQ-ACA-010 and supports control CTL-09 (access by role and scope). The measure is the access test set in section 16 passing for every role with real users at the release (DL39: administration roles at Epic 1).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-001 is done: the role and permission tables exist in the recovery schema.
- RWB-E1-019 is done: the 54 role rows are loaded, and each environment's role rows carry that environment's Entra ID group name in role.entra_group, for example RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN in SIT (pattern from the Single sign-on sheet; final names DL40).
- Permission matrix version PM-2026.11 is loaded from the Users, roles and permissions workbook (54 roles against 14 capability areas).
- Separation of duty version SOD-2026.11 is loaded into the role conflict table (new, see section 11) from the Separation of duty sheet.
- The ACE common module sign-in is configured for the Workbench application in Entra ID (INT-21), with the bank conditional access policy that requires a second factor.
- The person was added to the Entra ID group for their role through the bank IAM: the line manager requested it, the role owner approved it and the access administrator carried it out (section 10).

### 4. Flow

1. Person: opens the Workbench in the ACE front end.
2. ACE common module: redirects to Entra ID; the person signs in with password and second factor; Entra ID returns an OpenID Connect token with the groups claim and the amr claim.
3. Workbench (SessionResolver): checks that the amr claim contains "mfa".
4. Workbench: maps each group in the groups claim to an active role row by role.entra_group; groups with no active role row are ignored.
5. Workbench: checks the resulting role set against the role conflict table version in force.
6. Workbench: resolves the session: user reference, roles, the permission matrix version in force at that time, and the default scope of each role.
7. Workbench: writes the sign-in event through the AccessEventPublisher (ACE audit log and SOC log through INT-22).
8. ACE front end: calls GET /me/session and shows the first screen with one line naming the roles and the scope, for example "Case owner. Scope: own cases.", and a menu holding only screens whose capability area has R for at least one role.
9. Person: calls any endpoint; AccessCheck evaluates the capability area and right the endpoint declares against the session's matrix version and allows or refuses the call.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A role without the right calls an endpoint, for example the admin API | Refused with 403; the refusal is written to the access event stream with the area and right | MSG-P4-002 | AC2 |
| X2 | The person is in no Workbench group | Session refused with 401; the access request page shows the message and no data | MSG-P4-001 | AC3 |
| X3 | The token has no second factor in the amr claim | Session refused with 401; the refusal is logged | MSG-P4-005 | AC4 |
| X4 | The groups give a role pair listed in the role conflict table | Session refused; an incident is raised to the security administrator; the refusal is logged | MSG-P4-006 | AC6 |
| X5 | A service identity calls an area its role does not hold | Refused with 403, exactly as for a person | MSG-P4-002 | AC7 |
| X6 | A group maps to no active role row | The group is ignored; if no other group maps, X2 applies | MSG-P4-001 | AC8 |
| X7 | A new matrix version takes effect while a session is open | The open session keeps the version it resolved; the next session uses the new one | None | AC9 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the tables (RWB-E1-001) and the role rows (RWB-E1-019). The decision log write of access events is added in RWB-E1-039 |
| Negotiable | Group names, roles, conflicts and permissions are data. The story fixes the behavior, not the values |
| Valuable | Every Epic 1 administration user signs in with one bank identity and sees only what the role allows |
| Estimable | One resolver, one access check, one session endpoint, no business screen |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Sign-on with SSO, MFA and the first roles

  Background:
    Given the environment is SIT
    Given permission matrix version "PM-2026.11" is in force from 30 November 2026
    Given separation of duty version "SOD-2026.11" is in force
    Given role RW-CASEOWN has entra_group "RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN" and default scope "OWN"

  Scenario: AC1 SSO sign-in
    Given test user "U-1001" is in Entra ID group "RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN"
    When the user opens the Workbench and signs in with password and second factor
    Then the session holds roles "RW-CASEOWN", scope "OWN" and matrix version "PM-2026.11"
    Then GET /me/session returns the line "Case owner. Scope: own cases."
    Then the menu shows the screens of the capability areas where RW-CASEOWN holds R, and no Administration menu

  Scenario: AC2 Role denied
    Given test user "U-1002" holds only RW-PHONECOL, whose Platform administration letter is "-"
    When the user calls GET /admin/roles
    Then the system refuses the call with status 403 and message MSG-P4-002 with action "read roles"
    Then the system writes one refusal event with user "U-1002", area "PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION", right "R" and result "REFUSED"

  Scenario: AC3 Not in group
    Given test user "U-1003" has an Entra ID account and no group whose name starts "RWB-SIT-"
    When the user opens the Workbench
    Then the access request page shows MSG-P4-001 and no case, queue or reference data
    Then every recovery endpoint returns status 401 for that token
    Then the system writes one refusal event with reason "NO_ROLE"

  Scenario: AC4 Sign-in without a second factor is refused
    Given test user "U-1004" is in group "RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN"
    Given the token's amr claim holds "pwd" and not "mfa"
    When the token reaches the Workbench
    Then the system refuses the session with status 401 and message MSG-P4-005
    Then the system writes one refusal event with reason "NO_MFA"

  Scenario: AC5 Two roles give the permissions of both
    Given test user "U-1005" is in groups "RWB-SIT-RW-LITOFF" and "RWB-SIT-RW-LEGAL"
    When the user signs in
    Then the session holds roles "RW-LITOFF" and "RW-LEGAL"
    Then the Documents letters are "CRUA", the union of "CRU" and "CRUA"
    Then no permission comes from any role the user does not hold

  Scenario: AC6 A conflicting role pair is refused
    Given test user "U-1006" is in groups "RWB-SIT-RW-SECADM" and "RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN"
    Given the role conflict table says RW-SECADM may not hold any business role
    When the user signs in
    Then the system refuses the session with message MSG-P4-006 naming "RW-SECADM" and "RW-CASEOWN"
    Then the system raises an incident to the security administrator queue
    Then the system writes one refusal event with reason "ROLE_CONFLICT"

  Scenario: AC7 A service identity is checked like a person
    Given managed identity "SY-RULES" is in group "RWB-SIT-SY-RULES"
    When it calls GET /admin/roles
    Then the system refuses the call with status 403 and message MSG-P4-002
    Then the system writes one refusal event with user "SY-RULES"

  Scenario: AC8 An unmapped or inactive group gives no role
    Given test user "U-1008" is in groups "RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN" and "RWB-SIT-LEGACY01"
    Given no active role row has entra_group "RWB-SIT-LEGACY01"
    When the user signs in
    Then the session holds only "RW-CASEOWN"
    Then the system writes the unmapped group name on the sign-in event

  Scenario: AC9 An open session keeps the versions it resolved
    Given test user "U-1009" signed in at 09:00 on 1 December 2026 under matrix version "PM-2026.11"
    Given matrix version "PM-2026.12" takes effect at 10:00 on 1 December 2026 and removes R in Reporting from RW-CASEOWN
    When the user calls GET /reports/measures at 10:30 in the same session
    Then the system checks the call against "PM-2026.11" and allowed
    Then after the user signs in again at 11:00 the same call is refused with MSG-P4-002
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Membership of the Entra ID group mapped to a role is the only way to hold the role. The Workbench holds no password and no local account | role.entra_group (DF-REF-039); DT07; Admin and access model, section 4.2 |
| BR2 | A session is refused unless the token carries a second factor | NFR-049; FEAT-ACA-02 |
| BR3 | No role inherits from another. A person with two roles holds the union of both roles' letters | permission.letters (DF-REF-043) |
| BR4 | A capability area with no letter for any of the session's roles refuses every action in that area | Permission matrix; CTL-09 |
| BR5 | A role pair listed in the role conflict table may not be held in one session | Separation of duty sheet, roles.txt; role conflict table (new) |
| BR6 | A service identity holds a role in the same table and is checked the same way as a person | REQ-ACA-010; NFR-051 |
| BR7 | A session keeps the matrix and conflict versions it resolved at sign-in until it ends | Admin and access model, section 4.2 |
| BR8 | Group names, roles, letters and conflicts are data rows with a version; none is written in code | Principle 1; DT02 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It creates a session with the states Resolved and Refused, and the session ends at sign-out or token expiry.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Line manager (bank IAM, level 4) | Requests a Workbench role for a team member in the bank IAM, naming the person, the role and the reason. May not approve the request they raised |
| Role owner (bank IAM, level 2), the head of the unit whose staff hold the role | Approves or rejects each grant of a role they own after checking the separation of duty table |
| Access administrator (bank IAM, level 3), Chief Debt Recovery Management Office (assumed, DL01) | Adds the person to the Entra ID group of the approved role in each environment requested. Approves no grant |
| Application owner (level 1), Tribe Lead of the Collections and Recovery Tribe (assumed, DL02) | Approves the roles table and each group to role mapping |
| RW-SECADM Security administrator | Maintains the Entra ID groups and the IAM link (DL40); receives the conflict incident in AC6 |
| RW-REFADM Reference data administrator | Loads an approved role or group mapping version. Approves none |
| RW-CASEOWN and every bank role | Signs in and uses the screens of the role |
| RW-PHONECOL Phone collector | Signs in; refused on Platform administration (AC2) |
| SY-RULES and the other service identities | Act under their managed identity and their own role row |
| RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM, RW-SECADM | Read GET /admin/roles (Platform administration R) |

The four administration levels act in the bank IAM, not in the Workbench. If the bank chooses central administration (DL01), level 3 moves to the central IAM team and nothing in this build changes.

### 12. Contract

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/roles** (API-P4-007)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | None |
| Response | Array of Role: id, roleCode, roleName, roleClass, defaultScope, entraGroup |
| Errors | 401 no valid session or no role (MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-005, MSG-P4-006); 403 the session's roles hold no R in Platform administration (MSG-P4-002); 503 the ACE sign-in service is unavailable (MSG-GEN-006) |
| Authorization | Platform administration, right R |
| Idempotency | Not applicable, read only |

**GET /me/session** (new, recorded in the additions file)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | None |
| Response | Session: userRef, roles (roleCode, roleName, defaultScope), matrixVersion, conflictVersion, scopeLine, resolvedAt, breakGlass (active, endsAt; filled by RWB-E1-039) |
| Errors | 401 as above |
| Authorization | Any resolved session; no capability area, because the endpoint returns only the caller's own session |
| Idempotency | Not applicable, read only |

**Published interface AccessCheck** (package recovery.access.signin), called by every module's controller through a Spring method interceptor:

```java
AccessDecision check(SessionContext session, CapabilityArea area, Right right);
SessionContext resolve(VerifiedToken token); // throws SessionRefusedException(reasonCode, messageId)
```

**Published interface AccessEventPublisher** (package recovery.access.signin):

```java
void publish(AccessEvent event); // E1: ACE audit and SOC log through INT-22; RWB-E1-039 adds the decision log
```

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `recovery/access/signin` in the recovery module; Java package `recovery.access.signin`. Front end: `recovery/access` folder in the ACE front end.
- Components:

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AccessAndAdministrationController | Controller | GET /admin/roles and GET /me/session; maps refusals to problem responses with messageCode |
| SessionResolver | Service | Checks the amr claim, maps groups to role rows, applies the conflict check, builds SessionContext |
| AccessCheckService | Published interface | Implements AccessCheck: unions the letters of the session's roles in the area and tests the right |
| AccessCheckInterceptor | Service | Reads the capability area and right declared on each endpoint (x-capability) and calls AccessCheck before the handler |
| AccessEventPublisher | Published interface | Writes sign-in and refusal events to the ACE audit and SOC log |
| AccessAndAdministrationRepository | Repository | Reads role, permission and role_conflict rows in force |
| RoleConflict | Entity | Maps the new role_conflict table |
| SessionBanner | React component | Shows the one-line roles and scope from GET /me/session |
| AccessRequestPage | React component | Shows MSG-P4-001 and no data when the session is refused with NO_ROLE |

- Database: reads role (id, role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope, entra_group, is_active), permission (role_id, capability_area, letters, matrix_version, is_active). Creates table role_conflict (id uuid, role_code varchar(20), conflicts_with varchar(30), reason varchar(200), conflict_version varchar(20), valid_from date, valid_to date, plus the standard columns) with Flyway migration V_E1_022__role_conflict.sql; conflicts_with holds a role code or the class values ANY_BUSINESS_ROLE and ANY_OTHER_ROLE. Index ix_role_entra_group on role (entra_group) where is_active.
- Configuration and reference data: role rows and group names (loaded by RW-REFADM after RWB-E1-019; names DL40); permission matrix PM-2026.11 (loaded by RW-REFADM, approved per RWB-E1-037); role conflict version SOD-2026.11 (loaded by RW-REFADM from the Separation of duty sheet); LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-SCOPE; scope line wording from labels per DL10. Property `rwb.access.required-amr=mfa`.
- Build steps:
  1. Create the role_conflict migration and entity; load SOD-2026.11 into SIT with six rows from the Separation of duty sheet that name Workbench roles.
  2. Build SessionResolver: amr check, group to role mapping on active rows, conflict check, SessionContext with versions; unit tests for AC1, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC8.
  3. Build AccessCheckService with letter union per area; unit tests for every letter and the dash.
  4. Build AccessCheckInterceptor reading the declared area and right; contract test that every operation in api.yaml has one.
  5. Build AccessEventPublisher to the ACE audit and SOC log; refusal reason codes NO_ROLE, NO_MFA, ROLE_CONFLICT, NO_RIGHT.
  6. Build GET /admin/roles and GET /me/session with problem responses.
  7. Build SessionBanner, menu filtering by capability area and AccessRequestPage.
  8. Hold the resolved versions on the session and test AC9 with two matrix versions.
- Feature flag: `rwb.access.sso-roles`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass, a test user per Epic 1 administration role signs in with MFA in SIT, and the contract test finds no endpoint without a declared capability area.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | Sign-in with no Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | An action outside the role's permission | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-005 | Token without a second factor (new) | Sign in again with your second factor. The Workbench needs multi-factor authentication. |
| MSG-P4-006 | Conflicting role pair at sign-in (new) | Your roles {role} and {otherRole} cannot be held together. Access is refused and the security administrator has been told. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | ACE sign-in service unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

Thai text for each message follows DL10; proposed Thai for the new messages is in the additions file.

### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The ACE front end shell shows the session line from GET /me/session at the top of every page and hides menu entries whose capability area the session cannot read. A person with no role sees the access request page with MSG-P4-001 and no data. Epic 1 has no business screens (DL39); RW-CASEOWN test users exist in SIT and UAT only.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: group names, roles, letters, scopes and conflicts are read from tables with their version.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts. Access events carry the Entra ID object reference, never the person's name or e-mail.
- No read of another module's tables.
- No local password, local account or role cache that outlives the session.
- Every endpoint declares its capability area and right; an endpoint without one fails the contract test.

## RWB-E1-023 Case record view v1, read only

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-023 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-ACA-11 Show the case record view read only |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-OCC-007, REQ-RDF-009, REQ-ACA-005, REQ-ACA-006 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.3, 3.4 and 3.6; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.1, 5.4 and 5.6 |
| L3 process | 06 Take over and own the case |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010; DL43 open |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-024, RWB-E1-037, RWB-E1-039, RWB-E1-068, RWB-E1-069 |
| Status | Ready for build, the freshness line behind a flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43) |

### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **one read-only screen per case with the case ID, accounts, arrears, owner, queue, stage, status, contact history and documents, read live from the ACE views by business key with the business date of each**, so that **I stop searching files and systems to understand a case**.

### 2. Business rationale

A case owner opens EFS, ALS, shared drives and team spreadsheets today to answer one question about a case. Under D-RCV-35 the Workbench holds no copy of the account, the customer or the contact point: the screen reads `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_contact` and `v_ace_efs_action` by `account_key` and `person_key`. The identity number is already masked inside `v_ace_customer` (`id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4`) and the contact values are masked at the API by role (RWB-E1-037), so no clear personal value is copied into a Workbench table or a screen cache. This story puts the case, its accounts and arrears, its parties and contacts, its contact history and its documents on SCR-03, each section showing the ACE business date behind it, and writes every view of personal data to the access log. It meets REQ-OCC-007, REQ-RDF-009, REQ-ACA-005 and REQ-ACA-006.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-018 is done: cases exist with `account_key` links on case_account and `person_key` links on case_party.
- RWB-E1-024 is done: the document hub lists documents by case.
- RWB-E1-068 is done: the interaction ledger reads back through its published interface.
- RWB-E1-037 is done: the masking rules by role are in force (DL26) and name the view field IDs.
- RWB-E1-039 is done: access events are published to the access log.
- RWB-E1-069 is done: `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_contact` and `v_ace_efs_action` are Section A views. `v_ace_batch_status` is a Section B view, so the freshness banner stays behind its flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43).
- The account, customer and contact views carry the ACE business date: `v_ace_account.data_as_of` and the ALS, SCBPDM and EFS rows in `v_ace_batch_status`.
- `recovery_svc` holds SELECT on `recovery.v_ace_*` and no privilege on `public`.
- The user holds a role with Case record R and the case is in the user's scope.
- Personal data access is logged through AccessEventPublisher (RWB-E1-039), which also sends the PII access record to PII Kafka through the ACE common module.

### 4. Flow

1. Case owner: opens a case from SCR-02 Case list; SCR-03 shows the Loading state.
2. CaseRecordPage: calls GET /cases/{caseId}, GET /cases/{caseId}/accounts, GET /cases/{caseId}/parties, GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions and GET /cases/{caseId}/documents in parallel.
3. CaseAndWorkflowController: checks Case record R and the scope; out of scope returns 404.
4. CaseRecordQueryService: reads the header from recovery_case and the links from case_account and case_party.
5. CaseRecordQueryService: reads the account facts from `v_ace_account` by `account_key`, the customer facts from `v_ace_customer` by `person_key` and the contact points from `v_ace_contact` by `person_key` and `contact_type`; every row carries the ACE business date from `data_as_of` or from `v_ace_batch_status`.
6. CaseRecordQueryService: reads the collections history from `v_ace_efs_action` by `account_key` and the Workbench entries through InteractionLedgerReader (RWB-E1-068), and merges them into one contact history ordered by time, each row carrying its source system.
7. MaskingApplier: fills each personal field from the masked or the clear view column for the caller's role through FieldMasker, and publishes one AC-READ access event with the field IDs read and their masked flags. A read whose event cannot be written returns nothing.
8. DocumentHub (P5): returns the document list for the case through its endpoint.
9. CaseRecordPage: shows the header (case number, product, status, stage, route, owner, queue, entry date, prescription date, deviation and hold flags), then Accounts, Parties with their contact points, Contact history and Documents, each with its ACE business date (read only state).
10. CaseRecordPage: shows the stale banner with MSG-P1-001 on any section whose ACE batch is not COMPLETE for the latest business date, and no Workbench load or job status anywhere.
11. CaseRecordPage: shows the on hold banner with MSG-P3-004 when the case is on hold.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The ACE batch behind a section is not COMPLETE for the latest business date | Section shows with its business date and the stale banner | MSG-P1-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The case is outside the user's scope | 404; nothing shows | MSG-P4-003 | AC5 |
| X3 | The document hub does not answer | Documents section shows the section message; the rest shows | MSG-P3-023 | AC6 |
| X4 | The access event cannot be written | The read is refused; no case data and no personal field shows | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X5 | The role may not see a personal field in clear | The field shows from the masked view column | None | AC8 |
| X6 | The case is on hold | On hold banner with the prescription date | MSG-P3-004 | AC9 |
| X7 | The case has no documents and no contact history | Each section shows its empty sentence | MSG-P3-024 | AC10 |
| X8 | A role without Case record R opens the view | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-023-11 |
| X9 | A case link holds an `account_key` that `v_ace_account` does not return | The Accounts row shows the key with empty values; REC-05 lists it; the rest shows | None | AC12 |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every section shows the ACE business date behind it, read from `v_ace_account.data_as_of` or from `v_ace_batch_status`; no Workbench load date is used | REQ-RDF-009; VR-P3-001-1 |
| BR2 | A section whose ACE batch is not COMPLETE for the latest business date shows the stale banner | MSG-P1-001; screens.txt Common states "Stale input"; v_ace_batch_status |
| BR3 | A personal field shows from the masked view column unless the masking rule in force lets the role see it in clear; the identity number is never in clear because `v_ace_customer` exposes `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` only | REQ-ACA-005; CTL-11; DL26; DF-ACE-073, DF-ACE-074 |
| BR4 | Every read of personal data is written to the access log; a read whose event cannot be written returns no data | REQ-ACA-006; RWB-E1-039 BR2 |
| BR5 | Only cases in the caller's scope open; others return 404 | CTL-09; REQ-ACA-009 |
| BR6 | The view has no edit control in Epic 1 | SCR-03 "E1 read only" |
| BR7 | The view loads in under 2 seconds with 50 documents | NFR-009 |
| BR8 | Account, customer, contact and collections history data are read live from `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_contact` and `v_ace_efs_action` by business key; the Workbench holds no copy and shows no Workbench load status | D-RCV-35 U1 and U4; ADR-010 |
| BR9 | A case link with no view row shows the business key with empty values and is listed by REC-05; it is never deleted or rewritten | REC-05; Data Tier Map section 5 |
| BR10 | The contact history merges the ACE EFS entries and the Workbench interaction ledger in one time order, each row naming its source system | E1-068; interaction.source_system (DF-INT-013) |

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Back end `recovery/casewf/caserecord` (Java package `recovery.casewf.caserecord`); front end `src/modules/recovery/casewf/caserecord`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseAndWorkflowController | Controller | The four P3 read endpoints with access check and scope |
| CaseRecordQueryService | Service | Composes case, accounts, parties with contacts and contact history; adds the ACE business date per section |
| AceSourceReader | Repository | Reads `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_contact` and `v_ace_efs_action` by business key; SELECT only |
| MaskingApplier | Service | Calls FieldMasker (RWB-E1-037) and publishes AC-READ through AccessEventPublisher; refuses the read when the publish fails |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | recovery_case, case_account, case_party, queue |
| CaseRecordPage | React component | SCR-03 read only layout with Loading, read only and on hold states |
| CaseHeader, AccountsPanel, PartiesPanel, ContactHistoryPanel, DocumentsPanel | React component | One section each, each with an AceDataDateBadge |
| StaleBanner, OnHoldBanner, SectionMessage | React component | MSG-P1-001, MSG-P3-004, MSG-P3-023 and MSG-P3-024 |

**Database**

- Reads recovery_case, case_account, case_party and queue only, plus the four views through AceSourceReader. Uses ix_interaction_case_time in RWB-E1-068 for the ledger part of the contact history.
- No migration.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Masking rules over the view field IDs (RWB-E1-037; DL26), labels (DL10), LOV-ACTION-CODE, LOV-CONTACT-RESULT, LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-CONTACT-TYPE, LOV-PARTY-ROLE.
- Parameter `caserecord.section.timeout.ms` = 3000 (assumed; DL11) from RWB-E1-042.

**Build steps**

1. AceSourceReader with the four view reads by `account_key` and `person_key`; test the join and the business date for AC2, AC3, AC12.
2. CaseRecordQueryService with the section composition and the merged contact history; tests AC2, AC3, AC10.
3. MaskingApplier with the access log call and the refusal path; tests AC7, AC8.
4. Scope check returning 404; test AC5.
5. CaseRecordPage with parallel calls, per-section timeout and section messages; tests AC6, AC10.
6. StaleBanner and OnHoldBanner over `v_ace_batch_status`; tests AC4, AC9.
7. No-copy and performance tests with 50 documents and 120 EFS entries; tests AC1, AC11.
8. Access test.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.caserecordview`. Off: SCR-03 shows the case header only. The stale banner reads a Section B view, so it is on only after RWB-ACE-001 lands and V0003 creates `v_ace_batch_status` (DL43).

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and the view meets NFR-009 in SIT.

SCR-03 Case record. Loading: skeleton rows per section. Read only: fields without edit controls; the header and five sections, each with the ACE business date of its source. On hold: the banner with the deviation or legal hold and the prescription date. Stale input: MSG-P1-001 above the section when the ACE batch is not complete. Error: MSG-P3-023 in the section that failed. The screen shows no Workbench load, job or file status.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: masking rules, labels and timeouts are data.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts; test parties are synthetic and the application log holds case numbers only.
- ACE data only through the `recovery.v_ace_*` views: account, customer, contact and collections history come from `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_contact` and `v_ace_efs_action`, and freshness from `v_ace_batch_status`. The recovery schema holds no foreign key into a `public` table.
- The view holds no copy of a source record and caches no clear personal value; the identity number is masked inside the view and the contact values are masked at the API by role.
- Personal fields are never shown when the access event cannot be written.
