## RWB-E1-024 Document store and index

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-024 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-01 Store documents with a write-once container for legal types; FEAT-DCM-02 Index documents by case, type, date and extracted fields; FEAT-DCM-19 Keep the Workbench document hub as the system of record for documents; FEAT-DCM-20 Version a document and keep its history |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-001, REQ-DCM-002, REQ-DCM-003, REQ-DCM-008 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5; Business Requirements Program, section 5.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence; L2 13.3 Store and retain documents |
| Decision | D7.2 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-025, RWB-TE-012, RWB-E1-001 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **every document stored against its case with its type, date, source and extracted fields, legal types held in a write-once container, and every version kept**, so that **I find a document by case ID, type and date, and a legal document cannot be changed after it is stored**.

### 2. Business rationale

Recovery documents are held today in folders, shared drives and with couriers; originals go missing and evidence is rebuilt for each audit (FSD P5 A1.3). This story builds the store and the index that every other document story writes to: one document record in the Workbench document hub per file, the file in blob storage, legal types write-once (DT06, ADR-007, control CTL-12). It meets REQ-DCM-001, REQ-DCM-002, REQ-DCM-003 and REQ-DCM-008. The module measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.1.1), which can only be counted once every document is indexed against its case.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-001 is done: the tables document and document_field exist in the recovery schema.
- RWB-TE-012 is done: the intake container, rwb-docs (standard), rwb-docs-legal (write-once) and rwb-quarantine exist, reached by managed identity through DocumentStorage.
- RWB-E1-018 is done: cases exist and the P3 published interface CaseDirectory returns a case by ID.
- RWB-E1-025 is done: document type table version DOCTYPE-2026.11 is in force with the six types, the write-once flag and the retention class of each type.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the P7 published interface DecisionLogWriter writes an entry inside the caller's transaction.
- Document hub parameters loaded (this story creates the table): INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES = PDF, JPG, PNG; INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB = 25, assumed (DL11). RWB-E1-053 and RWB-E1-057 read the same table.
- The caller is the upload service (RWB-E1-026, user with Documents C) or the intake (RWB-E1-032, SY-OCR). A reader holds Documents R with the case in scope.
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.store is on.

### 4. Flow

1. Caller: calls DocumentStore.store with the case ID, the document type, the source, the file in the intake container, its SHA-256 hash and any extracted fields.
2. DocumentStoreService: gets the case through CaseDirectory.findById and refuses the call if the case does not exist.
3. DocumentStoreService: reads the type row from the document type table version in force: write_once and retention_class.
4. DocumentStoreService: checks the file type by its content signature and the file size against INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES and INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB.
5. DocumentStoreService: looks for an active document on the case with the same type and hash; if one exists, returns it and stops.
6. DocumentStoreService: in one transaction, writes the decision log entry (decision code DOCATT, final call STORED) through DecisionLogWriter, inserts the document row with doc_version 1 and state COPY_PENDING, inserts the document_field rows and writes DocumentStored (EV-16) to the outbox.
7. DocumentStoreService: after commit, calls DocumentStorage.store (RWB-TE-012), which writes the file to rwb-docs-legal when write_once is true and to rwb-docs otherwise, at {container}/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1; the service sets storage_ref and state STORED.
8. User with Documents R: opens the document from the case documents screen (SCR-30); GET /documents/{documentId} returns the metadata, the extracted fields and the version list; GET /documents/{documentId}/content returns the file. The ACE common module writes each read to the PII access log.
9. User with Documents U: adds a version with POST /documents/{documentId}/versions; the service inserts a new document row with doc_version n+1 and previous_version_id set to the current row, and marks the earlier row is_active = false. The earlier version stays readable.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Delete or content replace of a write-once document, through the service or directly on the container | Refused; the file and the row are unchanged; an audit event DOCUMENT_CHANGE_REFUSED is written | MSG-P5-002 | AC2 |
| X2 | Document type not in the type table in force | Refused with 422; nothing stored | MSG-P5-006 | AC5 |
| X3 | File content is not PDF, JPG or PNG | Refused with 415; nothing stored | MSG-P5-001 | AC6 |
| X4 | File above INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB | Refused with 413; nothing stored | MSG-P5-017 | AC7 |
| X5 | The same file is stored again on the same case with the same type | The existing document is returned; no second row, entry or event | None | AC8 |
| X6 | Two users add a version to the same document at the same time | The first succeeds; the second gets 409; one new version exists | MSG-GEN-004 | AC9 |
| X7 | A version is added to a document that is not the latest version | Refused with 409 | MSG-P5-025 | AC10 |
| X8 | The copy to the container fails after commit | The row stays COPY_PENDING; the copy is retried by the next document intake run (JOB-12); content reads return 503 until it is stored | MSG-GEN-006 | AC11 |
| X9 | The reader's role scope does not include the case | Refused with 403; nothing is returned | MSG-P4-003 | AC12 |
| X10 | The caller's role lacks the Documents right | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-024-13 (Access) |
| X11 | The decision log write fails | Nothing is stored; incident raised (R-UNI-39) | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E1-024-14 (Principle 5) |

| Negotiable | File types, size limit, write-once flag and retention class are data rows; the story fixes the behavior |
| Valuable | Every later document path (upload, OCR intake, generation) stores through this one service |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every document is held against one case, with type, source, stored date and extracted fields | REQ-DCM-001; document.case_id is mandatory |
| BR2 | The document hub is the system of record; the file is held only in the hub containers | DT06; DL27; REQ-DCM-002 |
| BR3 | The write-once flag and the retention class come from the document type table version in force, never from the caller | Document type table (New); principle 1; DT02 |
| BR4 | A write-once document is never deleted or changed; a change is a new version | CTL-12; REQ-DCM-003; NFR-029 |
| BR5 | File types and the size limit are parameters | Document hub parameter table (New); DL11 |
| BR6 | A store with the same case, type and hash returns the existing document | R-UNI-40; events.txt rule Duplicates |
| BR7 | Only the latest version of a document takes a new version | FEAT-DCM-20 |
| BR8 | A store that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR9 | Every read checks role, capability area and scope, and is written to the access log | CTL-09; REQ-ACA-006 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It sets the document record state (standard column state): new row COPY_PENDING; COPY_PENDING to STORED when the copy succeeds; on a new version the earlier row changes is_active from true to false.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-OCR, OCR and extraction pipeline | Stores documents through DocumentStore (Documents C) |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-LITOFF, RW-RESTRUCT and the other roles with Documents C | Store through the upload in RWB-E1-026 |
| Roles with Documents U (for example RW-CASEOWN, RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL, RW-COMPLY) | Add a new version |
| Roles with Documents R (for example RW-TEAMMGR, RW-AUDIT, RW-PHONECOL) | Read metadata and content inside their scope |
| SY-DECLOG, decision log writer | Writes the DOCATT entry |
| Nobody | Deletes or changes a write-once document |

### 12. Contract

**GET /documents/{documentId}**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path documentId (uuid) |
| Response | 200 Document: id, caseId, partyId, documentType, source, storageRef, classificationConfidence, reviewStatus, retentionClass, writeOnce, docVersion. Extended with storedAt, previousVersionId, versions and fields (see additions) |
| Errors | 401 not signed in; 403 no Documents R (MSG-P4-002) or case out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 404 no such document; 503 store unavailable (MSG-GEN-006) |
| Authorization | Documents, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**GET /api/recovery/v1/documents/{documentId}/content**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path documentId (uuid) |
| Response | 200 application/octet-stream, the file of that version |
| Errors | 401; 403 as above; 404; 503 while state is COPY_PENDING (MSG-GEN-006) |
| Authorization | Documents, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**POST /documents/{documentId}/versions**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: file (binary), reason (string, required) |
| Response | 200 Document, the new version |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Documents U (MSG-P4-002) or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 404; 409 not the latest version (MSG-P5-025) or concurrent change (MSG-GEN-004); 413 file above the limit (MSG-P5-017, see additions); 415 file type (MSG-P5-001); 503 decision log write failed (MSG-P7-003) |
| Authorization | Documents, right U, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header; a repeat with the same key returns the first result |

**Published interface (P5, used by RWB-E1-026, RWB-E1-032 and the retention job in RWB-E1-041)**

```java
public interface DocumentStore {
    StoredDocument store(StoreRequest request);          // caseId, documentType, source, intakeBlobRef, sha256, fields, partyId
    StoredDocument addVersion(UUID documentId, BlobRef file, String reason, UUID actor);
    void delete(UUID documentId, String reason, UUID actor);          // throws WriteOnceViolationException when write_once
    void replaceContent(UUID documentId, BlobRef file, UUID actor);   // throws WriteOnceViolationException when write_once
    Optional<StoredDocument> findById(UUID documentId);
}
```

**Event published:** DocumentStored (EV-16), payload documentId, caseId, type, source, written to the outbox in the store transaction.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dochub/store`, Java package `recovery.dochub.store`.

**Components.**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DocumentHubController | Controller | GET document, GET content, POST versions; maps exceptions to problem responses with the message ID |
| DocumentStore | Published interface | The contract in section 12 for other modules and P5 packages |
| DocumentStoreService | Service | Validation, type lookup, duplicate check, decision log write, insert, outbox event, version rules |
| DocumentHubRepository | Repository | Reads and writes document and document_field only |
| DocumentEntity, DocumentFieldEntity | Entity | Map the two tables, with the optimistic lock column version |
| DocumentTypeReader | Repository | Reads the document type table version in force (table from RWB-E1-025) |
| DocumentHubParameters | Rule table | Reads document_hub_parameter rows in force, cached for 5 minutes; used by every P5 package |
| DocumentStorage | Published interface | From RWB-TE-012: writes, opens and refuses overwrite of blobs; called, never reimplemented |
| CopyPendingStep | Job | Step of JOB-12 Document intake that retries copies for rows in COPY_PENDING |
| DocumentDetailPanel | React component | Opens from SCR-30; shows metadata, extracted fields, versions and the download button |

**Database.**
- Reads and writes document (all columns) and document_field (all columns).
- Flyway migration `V1_5_024__document_store.sql`: adds document.previous_version_id uuid null with a foreign key to document(id) and document.content_sha256 char(64) not null; creates document_hub_parameter (id, param_code varchar(40), param_value varchar(200), unit varchar(20), table_version varchar(20), valid_from date, valid_to date, load_id uuid, standard columns) with unique (param_code, table_version).
- Indexes: ix_document_case_type_created on document (case_id, document_type, created_at); unique partial index uk_document_case_type_hash on document (case_id, document_type, content_sha256) where is_active; ix_document_previous_version on document (previous_version_id).

**Configuration and reference data.**
- Document type table (RWB-E1-025), loaded by the reference data administrator.
- Parameters INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES and INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB in document_hub_parameter, loaded by the reference data administrator.
- Container names rwb-docs and rwb-docs-legal from RWB-TE-012, held as properties per environment.
- Decision code DOCATT, assumed; the LOV-DECISION list is loaded by the data steward.

**Build steps.**
1. Write the migration and the entities; test the unique partial index refuses a second active row with the same case, type and hash.
2. Build DocumentHubParameters and DocumentTypeReader with the valid_from and valid_to rule of the type table; unit test the version in force on a boundary date.
3. Build DocumentStoreService.store with validation (case, type, content signature, size) and the duplicate check; unit test AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8.
4. Add the transaction: DecisionLogWriter call, inserts and outbox event; integration test that a forced writer failure leaves no row and no event.
5. Call DocumentStorage after commit and build CopyPendingStep; integration test against the SIT storage account with rwb-docs-legal under its immutability policy for AC1, AC2 and AC11.
6. Build addVersion with the latest-version rule and optimistic locking; test AC4, AC9, AC10.
7. Build delete and replaceContent with the write-once refusal and the audit event; test AC2.
8. Build the controller endpoints with the access check and scope; API tests for AC1, AC12 and the access test.
9. Build DocumentDetailPanel; component test for the version list and the download.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.dochub.store`. Off: the endpoints return 404 and DocumentStore.store refuses with a feature-off error.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the boundary test on module tables passes, and a 1.2 MB PDF is stored and listed within 2 seconds in SIT.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-001 | File content is not an allowed type | This file type cannot be stored. Use PDF, JPG or PNG. |
| MSG-P5-002 | Delete or change of a write-once document | Legal documents cannot be changed. Add a new version instead. |
| MSG-P5-017 | File above the size limit | This file is larger than {size} MB and cannot be stored. |
| MSG-P5-025 | New version on a superseded version | This is not the latest version of the document. Open the latest version to add a new one. |
| MSG-P5-006 | Document type not in the type table in force | {value} is not a document type in force. Choose a type from the list. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Concurrent version | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | Content requested while the copy is pending | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: file types, size limit, write-once flag, retention class and container names are data rows or properties.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts. Test files are synthetic; extracted field values in logs are replaced by the field name.
- No read of another module's tables: the case is read through CaseDirectory, the decision log is written through DecisionLogWriter.
- The service never overwrites a blob; every version is a new blob path.
- The PII access log entry for each read is written by the ACE common module, never by this package.

## RWB-E1-025 Document types and fields agreed

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-025 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-03 Agree the six document types and their fields |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-004 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5; Business Requirements Program, section 5.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence |
| Decision | D7.2 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-069 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the first six document types (demand letter, court notice, appraisal report, title deed, settlement agreement, guarantor notice) with their key fields agreed with Legal and NPA and held as versioned reference data**, so that **the OCR pipeline, classification and extraction have one signed target list**.

### 2. Business rationale

Classification and extraction cannot be built or measured until the bank fixes which types are read and which fields come out of each (REQ-DCM-004, DL19). Today no signed list exists, so the model would train on a list that may change. This story turns the agreed list into a versioned table that the store (RWB-E1-024), classification (RWB-E1-050) and extraction (RWB-E1-053) read, and that changes by a data load without a code release (DT02). The measure it serves is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.3.1).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-069 is done: the 30 ACE views are in place, so the source fields that each document type can carry are known.
- The load file "DOCTYPE-2026.11" is prepared by the reference data administrator with the six types, 26 fields and the sign-offs of a legal counsel user and a Head of NPA user.
- LOV-RETENTION holds the codes LEGAL10Y and GENERAL05Y, assumed until the bank retention schedule arrives (DL26), loaded by the data steward.
- The loader holds RW-REFADM (Reference data C). The approver holds Reference data A (see section 10).
- The P4 endpoint POST /admin/reference-loads exists and calls the P5 ReferenceTableLoader for table code DOCUMENT_TYPE.
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.doctypes is on.

### 4. Flow

1. Center of excellence analyst: prepares the list of six types and 26 fields; legal counsel and the Head of NPA review it and sign with a date.
2. Reference data administrator: uploads the file with POST /admin/reference-loads, table DOCUMENT_TYPE, validFrom 2026-11-30.
3. P4 reference load service: passes the rows to DocumentTypeLoader through the ReferenceTableLoader interface.
4. DocumentTypeLoader: validates every row: type code unique, label present, write-once flag present, retention class in LOV-RETENTION, at least one field, both sign-offs with a user ID and a date.
5. DocumentTypeLoader: on any failure refuses the load whole and returns the row errors; the version in force is unchanged.
6. DocumentTypeLoader: on success writes the rows as table version DOCTYPE-2026.11 with status LOADED, not yet in force.
7. Approver: approves with POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve; a different person from the loader.
8. DocumentTypeLoader: sets the version APPROVED; from validFrom the readers return it as the version in force; the previous version gets valid_to of the day before.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A row has no Legal or no NPA sign-off, or a sign-off without a date | Load refused in full; version in force unchanged | MSG-P3-027 | AC3 |
| X2 | A row has a retention class not in LOV-RETENTION, or repeats a type code | Load refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC4 |
| X3 | The same table version is loaded a second time | Refused with 409; the first load is kept | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X4 | A new version with a future valid from date | The current version stays in force until that date; open work keeps the version it used | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The loader tries to approve their own load | Refused with 409 | MSG-P7-002 | AC7 |
| X6 | A role without Reference data C uploads the file | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-025-08 (Access) |

| Independent | Needs only the ACE view list (RWB-E1-069) and the P4 reference load endpoint |
| Negotiable | The type list and fields are data; the bank list replaces the six proposed types under DL19 |
| Valuable | Gives the OCR, classification and extraction stories one signed target |
| Estimable | One table, one loader, one validation set |
| Small | Under one week with its tests |

### 7. Acceptance criteria


### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The document types and their fields are signed by Legal and NPA before extraction is built | REQ-DCM-004; DL19 |
| BR2 | Each type row carries the write-once flag, the retention class and the field list | Document type table (New); DT02 |
| BR3 | A load with any invalid row is refused in full | refdata.txt change process, step 3; CTL-08 |
| BR4 | A version takes effect on its valid from date; work already done keeps the version it used | refdata.txt change process, step 6; R-UNI-38 |
| BR5 | The person who loads a version does not approve it | roles.txt separation of duty; CTL-08 |
| BR6 | Retention class codes come from LOV-RETENTION | LOV-RETENTION; DL26 |
| BR7 | The six proposed types apply until the bank provides its own list | DL19 |

The initial field lists are assumed until the sign-off (DL19): DEMAND_LETTER case_no, account_no, letter_date, amount_demanded, pay_by_date; COURT_NOTICE court_name, black_case_no, notice_date, hearing_date; APPRAISAL_REPORT appraisal_no, appraisal_date, appraised_value, title_doc_no; TITLE_DEED title_doc_no, land_office, owner_name, area_sq_wa; SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT case_no, agreement_date, settlement_amount, installment_count, borrower_name; GUARANTOR_NOTICE case_no, guarantor_name, notice_date, amount_claimed. Fields account_no, owner_name, borrower_name and guarantor_name are marked personal. Write-once true for every type except APPRAISAL_REPORT; retention LEGAL10Y for the write-once types and GENERAL05Y for APPRAISAL_REPORT (assumed; DL26, DL27).

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the reference load status: LOADED on a valid load; REFUSED on a failed check; APPROVED on approval, in force from valid from.

### 12. Contract

**POST /admin/reference-loads** (P4 endpoint; this story adds the table code DOCUMENT_TYPE)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: file (binary, the load file in the Excel template), table = "DOCUMENT_TYPE", validFrom (date) |
| Response | 201 ReferenceLoad: id, table, validFrom, status (LOADED or REFUSED), rows |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Reference data C (MSG-P4-002); 409 version already loaded (MSG-P3-027); 422 a row fails validation (MSG-P3-027 with row and error); 503 store unavailable (MSG-GEN-006) |
| Authorization | Reference data, right C |
| Idempotency | The table code and the table version; a second load of the same version is refused with 409 |

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path loadId (uuid) |
| Response | 200 ReferenceLoad with status APPROVED |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Reference data A (MSG-P4-002); 404; 409 approver is the loader (MSG-P7-002) or status is not LOADED; 503 |
| Authorization | Reference data, right A |
| Idempotency | Approving an APPROVED load returns it unchanged |

**Published interfaces**

```java
// P5 implements the P4 loader contract for its own tables
public interface ReferenceTableLoader {
    String tableCode();                                           // "DOCUMENT_TYPE"
    LoadResult validateAndStage(UUID loadId, String tableVersion, LocalDate validFrom, List<Map<String, String>> rows);
    void approve(UUID loadId, UUID approverId);
}

// P5 reader used by RWB-E1-024, RWB-E1-050 and RWB-E1-053
public interface DocumentTypeCatalog {
    DocumentTypeVersion inForce(LocalDate businessDate);         // version, types, fields
    Optional<DocumentTypeDef> type(String docTypeCode, LocalDate businessDate);
}
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dochub/types`, Java package `recovery.dochub.types`.

**Components.**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DocumentTypeLoader | Service | Implements ReferenceTableLoader for DOCUMENT_TYPE: parse, validate, stage, approve |
| DocumentTypeCatalog | Published interface | Returns the version in force and a type by code for a business date |
| DocumentTypeCatalogService | Service | Implements DocumentTypeCatalog with a 5-minute cache, cleared on approval |
| DocumentTypeRepository | Repository | Reads and writes document_type only |
| DocumentTypeEntity | Entity | Maps document_type |
| document_type rows | Rule table | The six types as data |

**Database.**
- Flyway migration `V1_5_025__document_type.sql` creates document_type: id uuid, doc_type_code varchar(30), label_en varchar(120), label_th varchar(120), write_once boolean, retention_class varchar(10), field_definitions jsonb, legal_signoff_by uuid, legal_signoff_date date, npa_signoff_by uuid, npa_signoff_date date, table_version varchar(20), valid_from date, valid_to date, load_id uuid, plus the standard columns.
- Constraints: unique (doc_type_code, table_version); not null on both sign-off columns.
- Index ix_document_type_valid on (valid_from, valid_to).

**Configuration and reference data.**
- The load file DOCTYPE-2026.11, prepared by the reference data administrator, signed by legal counsel and the Head of NPA.
- LOV-RETENTION values, loaded by the data steward (DL26).

**Build steps.**
1. Write the migration and the entity; test the constraints.
2. Build the row parser for the Excel template columns; unit test a valid file of 6 rows.
3. Build the validation rules and the refuse-whole behavior; unit test AC3 and AC4.
4. Build staging, the version check and approval with the separation of duty check; test AC1, AC2, AC5 and AC7.
5. Build DocumentTypeCatalogService with the valid from rule; test AC6 on the boundary dates.
6. Add the loader to the table codes of the P4 reference load service; API test through POST /admin/reference-loads and the access test.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.dochub.doctypes`. Off: the table code DOCUMENT_TYPE is refused by the reference load endpoint.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and version DOCTYPE-2026.11 is approved in SIT with both sign-offs.

| MSG-P7-002 | Loader approves their own load | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

## RWB-E1-026 Attach and search screen

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-026 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-04 Attach a document to a case; FEAT-DCM-05 Search documents within a case |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-008, REQ-DCM-001 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5; Business Requirements Program, section 5.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-025, RWB-E1-024, RWB-E1-041, RWB-E1-045, RWB-E1-030 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **to upload, see and search the documents of a case from the case record view**, so that **the case file is complete and I find a document by type and date without leaving the case**.

### 2. Business rationale

Case owners hold documents in shared drives and email today, so the case file is never complete in one place (FSD P5 A1.3). This story puts the case documents screen SCR-30 on the case record view: upload with a type, a list of every document on the case, a search by type and date, and a checklist placeholder showing which of the six agreed types are present. It meets REQ-DCM-008 (search by case, type and date from the case record view) and REQ-DCM-001 (every document stored against its case with type, date and source). The measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.4.1), which needs documents on the case first.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-024 is done: DocumentStore stores, versions and reads documents.
- RWB-E1-025 is done: document type table DOCTYPE-2026.11 is in force.
- RWB-E1-041 is done: the malware scan runs on every file before storage.
- RWB-E1-045 and RWB-E1-030 are done: product parameters and the queue measures used by the case record view exist.
- Parameters INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB = 25 (assumed, DL11) and INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES = PDF, JPG, PNG are in force.
- The user holds a role with Documents C to upload and Documents R to list, with the case in scope.
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.casedocs is on.

### 4. Flow

1. Case owner: opens case RW-2026-000123 on the case record view (SCR-03) and the Documents tab (SCR-30, state Loading then list).
2. Front end: calls GET /cases/{caseId}/documents and GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist and shows the list and the checklist placeholder.
3. Case owner: chooses Upload, picks a file and a document type from the list, and submits; the front end checks the size against INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB before sending and sends an Idempotency-Key.
4. CaseDocumentUploadService: puts the file in the intake container, calls the malware scan (RWB-E1-041) and, if clean, calls DocumentStore.store with source UPLOAD.
5. DocumentStore (RWB-E1-024): writes the decision log entry, the document row and DocumentStored, then copies the file.
6. Front end: on 201 refreshes the list; the new document shows within 5 seconds of submit.
7. Case owner: enters a type and a date range in the search bar; GET /cases/{caseId}/documents with type, dateFrom and dateTo returns only the matching documents, newest first, 20 per page.
8. Case owner: opens a document; DocumentDetailPanel (RWB-E1-024) shows it.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Upload with no document type | Refused with 422; nothing stored | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The file fails the malware scan | Refused with 422; file held in quarantine; nothing stored | MSG-P5-016 | AC5 |
| X3 | The file type is not allowed | Refused with 415; nothing stored | MSG-P5-001 | AC6 |
| X4 | The same file and type is already on the case | The existing document is returned and highlighted; no second document | MSG-P5-024 | AC7 |
| X5 | The submit is sent twice with the same Idempotency-Key | One document; the second call returns the first result | None | AC8 |
| X6 | Date from is after date to | Search not run | MSG-GEN-003 | AC9 |
| X7 | Search matches nothing | Empty state with the sentence and the clear filter action | None | AC10 |
| X8 | Case is outside the user's scope | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-003 | AC11 |
| X9 | Role without Documents C uploads | Refused with 403; Upload button hidden | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-026-12 (Access) |
| X10 | The decision log write fails during the store | Nothing stored; the dialog shows the message | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E1-026-13 (Principle 5) |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the store (RWB-E1-024), the types (RWB-E1-025) and the scan (RWB-E1-041), all earlier in Epic 1; no other screen depends on it |
| Negotiable | Page size, sort order and the placeholder layout can change; the endpoints stay |
| Valuable | Case owners attach and find documents on the case instead of in shared drives |
| Estimable | Two endpoints changed or added, one service, one tab with three parts |
| Small | Fits within two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A user upload carries a document type from the type table in force and source UPLOAD | REQ-DCM-001; LOV-DOC-SOURCE |
| BR2 | Every upload is scanned for malware before it is stored | REQ-DCM-010; FEAT-DCM-18 |
| BR3 | The list and the search show only cases in the user's scope | CTL-09 |
| BR4 | The date filter applies to the stored date of the document in Epic 1 | FSD P5 A2.5; REQ-DCM-008 |
| BR5 | The checklist placeholder lists the types of the type table in force; the required items per case type come in RWB-E1-040 | REQ-DCM-011; FEAT-DCM-16 |
| BR6 | A repeated upload with the same file, type and case returns the existing document | R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | A store that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. A successful upload creates a document record in state COPY_PENDING, then STORED (RWB-E1-024).

### 12. Contract

**POST /cases/{caseId}/documents**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: file (binary), type (doc_type_code, required), source (must be "UPLOAD" for a user call; other values refused with 422) |
| Response | 201 Document for a new document; 200 Document with messageCode MSG-P5-024 for a duplicate |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Documents C (MSG-P4-002) or case out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 404 case not found; 413 above INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB (MSG-P5-017); 415 file type (MSG-P5-001); 422 type missing (MSG-GEN-001), type not in the table (MSG-P5-006) or malware found (MSG-P5-016); 503 decision log write failed (MSG-P7-003) |
| Authorization | Documents, right C, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header, kept 24 hours per user; a repeat returns the first response |

**GET /cases/{caseId}/documents**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query type, page, size (api.yaml) plus dateFrom and dateTo (date, see additions); size default 20, maximum 100 |
| Response | 200 DocumentPage: items (Document), page, size, total; only active versions |
| Errors | 401; 403 (MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003); 404 case not found; 422 dateFrom after dateTo (MSG-GEN-003); 503 |
| Authorization | Documents, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist** (new, see additions)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path caseId |
| Response | 200 DocumentChecklist: caseId, checklistVersion (here the type table version), items [documentType, label, required, presentCount], missingCount, complete |
| Errors | 401; 403 (MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003); 404; 503 |
| Authorization | Documents, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

The placeholder returns required = false for every item, missingCount 0 and complete null until RWB-E1-040 sets the required items.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dochub/casedocs`, Java package `recovery.dochub.casedocs`; front end folder `recovery/documents`.

**Components.**

- Uses the index ix_document_case_type_created from RWB-E1-024. No new table.

**Configuration and reference data.**

## RWB-E1-027 Decision log writer v1

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-027 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P7 Decision center and log |
| Feature | FEAT-DRI-02 Write a decision log entry for every decision; FEAT-DRI-03 Record the rule ID, rule version and inputs on each entry; FEAT-DRI-04 Record the approver and the limit applied; FEAT-DRI-05 Block an action when the decision log write fails; FEAT-DRI-08 Expose the decision service to the workflow |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-004, REQ-DRI-005 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.7; Business Requirements Program, section 5.7 |
| L3 process | 17 Run the decision center |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-008, RWB-E1-056 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As the **case workflow module (SY-CASEWF)**, I want **one writer that validates and records case created, owner assigned, case transferred and document attached, with the rule ID and version used, in the same transaction as the action**, so that **the first decision records exist in Epic 1 and no action proceeds without its record**.

### 2. Business rationale

Without one writer, each module would build its own record and some actions would go unrecorded. This story gives every module one published interface that checks each record against the seven field groups, refuses an incomplete record, writes it in the caller's transaction so that a failed write stops the action, ignores a repeated event and publishes DecisionRecorded. It meets REQ-DRI-004 and REQ-DRI-005 and is the automated part of control CTL-06. The measure is decisions with a log entry: target 100 percent, and no action without one (NFR-034).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-008 is done: the store appends hash-chained entries and holds the columns chain_seq, corrects_entry_id and actor_user_id.
- RWB-E1-056 is done: the writer's failure alert and run book are in the job and service monitoring.
- LOV-DECISION is loaded by RW-DATASTEW with the decision codes, including the access event codes for RWB-E1-039.
- Parameters in the catalog: rwb.decision.code.CASE_CREATED=D6, rwb.decision.code.OWNER_ASSIGNED=D6, rwb.decision.code.CASE_TRANSFERRED=D6, rwb.decision.code.DOCUMENT_ATTACHED=D6 (assumed; D6 is the entry and ownership decision; owner RW-DATASTEW).
- The ACE outbox (RWB-TE-006) is available in the same database transaction.

### 4. Flow

1. Calling module (for example SY-CASEWF in the morning allocation): builds a DecisionLogRecord with the case, the event, the rule ID and version, the inputs reference, the actor and an idempotency key, inside its own transaction.
2. Calling module: calls DecisionLogWriter.write as the last step before commit.
3. Writer (DecisionLogWriterService): checks that a transaction is open; refuses the call if not.
4. Writer: checks the idempotency key; for a key already written, returns the first entry reference and counts the repeat.
5. Writer (DecisionLogRecordValidator): checks the required fields and the version group; refuses an incomplete record with the missing field named.
6. Writer: calls DecisionLogStore.append (RWB-E1-008).
7. Writer: writes the DecisionRecorded event to the outbox in the same transaction.
8. Calling module: commits; the action, the entry and the event are stored together.
9. Writer: on a refused record or a failed append, raises the exception; the caller's transaction rolls back, an incident is raised and the caller shows MSG-P7-003 or its own message.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A record misses the version group, the inputs reference, the final call or the case | Refused; the writer logs the error with the missing field; the caller's action rolls back | MSG-P7-009 | AC2 |
| X2 | A record carries a rule ID with no rule version | Refused as X1 | MSG-P7-009 | AC3 |
| X3 | The store cannot be written | The caller's action rolls back; an incident is raised | MSG-P7-003 | AC4 |
| X4 | The same event arrives twice with the same idempotency key | One entry; the repeat is counted | None | AC5 |
| X5 | The writer is called outside a transaction | Refused with IllegalTransactionStateException; nothing is written | None | AC6 |
| X6 | A record carries a decision code not in LOV-DECISION | Refused as X1 | MSG-P7-009 | AC7 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the store (RWB-E1-008) and the monitoring (RWB-E1-056) |
| Negotiable | Decision codes per event are parameters; the validation rules follow the seven field groups |
| Valuable | Every Epic 1 action has a validated record or does not happen |
| Estimable | One interface, one validator, one outbox write |
| Small | Fits in one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Decision log writer v1

  Background:
    Given the environment is DEV with synthetic data
    Given allocation table version "ALLOC-2026.11" and transfer rule version "TRF-2026.11" are in force

  Scenario: AC1 Record per event
    Given case "RW-2026-000123" is created by JOB-02 and given owner "U-7101" by row "ALLOC-MTG-BKK-01" of "ALLOC-2026.11" in JOB-03
    When the two events are written
    Then two entries exist for the case with final calls "CASE_CREATED" and "OWNER_ASSIGNED"
    Then the second entry carries rule ID "ALLOC-MTG-BKK-01", rule version "ALLOC-2026.11", actor "SY-CASEWF" and an inputs reference
    Then both entries pass the schema check and two DecisionRecorded events are in the outbox

  Scenario: AC2 Schema enforced
    Given a record for case "RW-2026-000123" with final call "CASE_TRANSFERRED" and no rule version, model version or agent version
    When it is written
    Then the system refuses it with message MSG-P7-009 naming "versions"
    Then the writer logs the error with the case ID and the missing field
    Then the system rolls the transfer in the same transaction back

  Scenario: AC3 A rule ID with no rule version is refused
    Given a record with rule ID "R-UNI-14" and an empty rule version
    When it is written
    Then the system refuses it with message MSG-P7-009 naming "ruleVersion"

  Scenario: AC4 A failed write stops the action
    Given the decision log store is unavailable
    When JOB-03 gives case "RW-2026-000124" to owner "U-7102"
    Then the write raises DecisionLogUnavailableException
    Then the case owner stays empty and the case status stays "New"
    Then the system raises an incident to the platform administrator queue

  Scenario: AC5 A repeated event gives one entry
    Given event "EV-7f3a-0001" for document "DOC-2026-0009981" attached to case "RW-2026-000123" was written
    When the same event with idempotency key "EV-7f3a-0001" arrives again
    Then one entry exists for the event
    Then the writer returns the first entry's ID and adds 1 to the repeat count for R-UNI-40

  Scenario: AC6 A write outside a transaction is refused
    Given a caller without an open transaction
    When it calls the writer
    Then the system refuses the call with IllegalTransactionStateException and nothing is written

  Scenario: AC7 An unknown decision code is refused
    Given a record with decision code "D99"
    When it is written
    Then the system refuses it with message MSG-P7-009 naming "decisionCode"
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Epic 1 writes entries for case created, owner assigned, case transferred and document attached | REQ-DRI-004 |
| BR2 | Required on every record: decision code from LOV-DECISION, inputs reference, final call, decided at and the actor; the case unless the decision code is an access event | DF-DEC-002, DF-DEC-003, DF-DEC-008, DF-DEC-012, DF-DEC-016; LOV-DECISION |
| BR3 | The version group needs at least one of rule version, model version and agent version, except for access events; a rule ID needs its rule version | DF-DEC-004 to DF-DEC-007; NFR-034 |
| BR4 | An approver needs an approval level from LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL on the same record | DF-DEC-010, DF-DEC-011; FEAT-DRI-04 |
| BR5 | The record is written in the caller's transaction; if it cannot be written, the action does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06; REQ-DRI-005 |
| BR6 | The same event with the same idempotency key gives one entry, and the repeat is counted | R-UNI-40; events.txt, Duplicates rule |
| BR7 | Decision codes for the Epic 1 events are parameters, not code | Principle 1; parameters rwb.decision.code.* |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It makes a status change made by another module depend on its entry: when the write fails, the case stays in the status it had (for example "New" in AC4).

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-DECLOG Decision log writer | Writes entries (Decision log C) |
| SY-CASEWF Case workflow module | Calls the writer for case created, owner assigned and case transferred (Decision log C) |
| SY-OCR OCR and extraction pipeline | Calls the writer for document attached (Decision log C) |
| SY-RULES, SY-DATALOAD, SY-AGENT | Call the writer for their own decisions (Decision log C) |
| RW-AUDIT, RW-COE and every role holding Decision log R | Read the entries |
| RW-PLATADM Platform administrator | Receives the incident when a write fails |

### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry | all fields | Write |
| DF-DEC-030 | decision_log_entry | actor_user_id | Write |
| DF-DEC-031 | decision_log_entry | idempotency_key | Write, read |
| DF-REF-028 | lov_value | lov_code | Read |
| DF-REF-029 | lov_value | value_code | Read |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

### 12. Contract

**Published interface DecisionLogWriter** (package recovery.decision.writer), the only way any module writes to the decision log:

```java
@Transactional(propagation = Propagation.MANDATORY)
DecisionLogEntryRef write(DecisionLogRecord record)
    throws DecisionLogRecordInvalidException,  // messageId MSG-P7-009, field
           DecisionLogUnavailableException;     // messageId MSG-P7-003
// DecisionLogRecord: idempotencyKey, caseId, decisionCode, ruleId, ruleVersion, modelVersion, agentVersion, inputsRef,
//   recommendation, approverUserId, approvalLevel, finalCall, overrideReason, actions, outcome, decidedAt,
//   actorUserRef, correctsEntryId
// DecisionLogEntryRef: entryId, chainSeq, entryHash, repeated (boolean)
```

**Event published:** EV-08 DecisionRecorded, payload entryId, caseId, decisionCode, approver; written to the outbox in the same transaction; consumers ledger and reporting.

**GET /api/recovery/v1/decision-log/{entryId}** and **GET /api/recovery/v1/decision-log** (API-P7-007, API-P7-006): read the written entries; Decision log R; built in RWB-E1-008.

Idempotency: the record's idempotencyKey (the event ID from the calling module); unique index on decision_log_entry (idempotency_key).

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `recovery/decision/writer` in the recovery module; Java package `recovery.decision.writer`.
- Components:

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DecisionLogWriter | Published interface | The write method above |
| DecisionLogWriterService | Service | Transaction check, idempotency check, validation, append, outbox event |
| DecisionLogRecordValidator | Service | BR2 to BR4 checks, with the decision codes read from LOV-DECISION |
| Epic1DecisionRecords | Service | Builders for the four Epic 1 events, with the decision code from the parameter catalog |
| DecisionRecordedPublisher | Service | Writes EV-08 to the ACE outbox |
| DecisionCenterAndLogRepository | Repository | Idempotency key lookup; append through DecisionLogStore |

- Database: Flyway migration V_E1_027__declog_idempotency.sql adds idempotency_key varchar(80) to decision_log_entry with unique index uk_declog_idempotency. No other table.
- Configuration and reference data: LOV-DECISION (RW-DATASTEW); parameters rwb.decision.code.* (RW-DATASTEW, values assumed); repeat counter exposed as metric decision_log_repeats_total in the job and service monitoring (RWB-E1-056).
- The rule version in a decision log entry is the rule package version label (D-RCV-36).
- Build steps:
  1. Write the migration for idempotency_key.
  2. Build DecisionLogRecordValidator with tests for AC2, AC3 and AC7.
  3. Build DecisionLogWriterService with the mandatory transaction, the idempotency check and the append; tests for AC5 and AC6.
  4. Add the outbox write of DecisionRecorded; test that a rollback leaves no event.
  5. Build the Epic 1 record builders and wire them into JOB-02, JOB-03, the transfer engine (RWB-E1-021) and document attach (RWB-E1-032) through the interface; test AC1.
  6. Test AC4 with the store switched off: the caller's change rolls back and the incident is raised.
- Feature flag: `rwb.decision.log-writer`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass and an architecture test fails the build if any class outside recovery.decision writes to decision_log_entry.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-009 | A record is refused for a missing or invalid field (new; written to the service log and the incident, not shown to customers) | The decision record was refused: {field} is missing or not valid. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The store cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P3-013 | Allocation not made because the write failed (shown by the allocation summary) | The case was not allocated because the decision could not be recorded. It will be tried again in the next run. |

Thai text for each message follows DL10; proposed Thai for MSG-P7-009 is in the additions file.

### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. Entries are read through the decision log endpoints; failed writes appear as incidents in the job and service monitoring (RWB-E1-056).

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: decision codes per event are parameters and list values.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts; a refused record is logged with its case ID and field name only.

## RWB-E1-028 Service levels, timers, escalation and prescription dates

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-028 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-11 Set service levels and stage timers; FEAT-CWC-12 Set and track prescription dates; FEAT-CWC-13 Escalate a breached timer to the named point |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-011, REQ-CWC-012, REQ-CWC-016 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, section 5.3 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes; 06 Take over and own the case; 08 Litigate and enforce |
| Decision | D-RCV-36 (T1, T2); ADR-011 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-045, RWB-E1-020, RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-043 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **a service level per queue and status, a timer on every case, a warning to the owner and a breach raised to the named escalation point by rule, and a prescription date set from the legal periods**, so that **no case waits past its limit unseen and no legal claim expires unnoticed**.

### 2. Business rationale

Deadlines are tracked in personal diaries today, and audit found litigation not filed for debtors meeting the criteria (CTL-18). This story starts a service level timer each time a case enters a queue and status, warns the owner at the warning point, raises a breach to the escalation role without moving the case, and sets the prescription date at case creation from the legal period for the product. It meets REQ-CWC-011, REQ-CWC-012 and REQ-CWC-016 and serves the measure "cases inside the service level" (target set with DL22).

Timers stay rows in the timer table. Every caller schedules, pauses, resumes and cancels a timer through the published TimerScheduler port, and TimerCheckJob (JOB-05, Quartz) is the Epic 1 implementation of that port. Epic 3 therefore replaces the implementation with Temporal durable timers without changing a caller (D-RCV-36 T2; ADR-011).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-020 is done: CaseAllocated is published when a case gets a queue and owner.
- RWB-E1-045 is done: ProductParameterService serves the SERVICE_LEVEL row for a product group and a case status, with limit, unit, warning percent and escalation role.
- RWB-E1-043 is done: ReferenceDataService serves the LEGAL_PERIOD table in force, and the holiday calendar is read from v_ace_holiday over the ACE Bank of Thailand table bot_holiday.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available.
- The published TimerScheduler port exists in the module (package recovery.casewf.timers) and TimerCheckJob (JOB-05, Quartz) implements it (D-RCV-36 T2).
- SERVICE_LEVEL row, values assumed until the business sets them (DL22): product group HIRE_PURCHASE, status ASSIGNED, limit 5 working days, warning percent 80, escalation role RW-TEAMMGR.
- LEGAL_PERIOD row owned by Legal: HIRE_PURCHASE 2 years from the last payment date (assumed value from the current story; other products loaded by Legal). Parameter `legal.prescription.warn.days` = 180 (assumed) from RWB-E1-042.
- v_ace_holiday marks 2026-12-05 to 2026-12-07 as non-working days (synthetic test values).
- JOB-05 runs every 5 minutes as SY-CASEWF through the TimerScheduler port of section 12.

### 4. Flow

1. TimerStarter: on CaseAllocated, CaseTransferred or CaseStateChanged, cancels the running SERVICE_LEVEL timer of the case through TimerScheduler.cancel(timerId).
2. TimerStarter: reads the service level for the new queue and status and calls TimerScheduler.schedule(TimerSpec) with started_at, expires_at in working days and warn_at at the warning percentage; the port writes the timer row.
3. PrescriptionService: on CaseCreated, reads the last payment date of each linked account through the P1 interface and the legal period for the product, and sets the earliest result as the prescription date.
4. PrescriptionService: schedules a PRESCRIPTION timer through TimerScheduler.schedule with expires_at on the prescription date and warn_at 180 days before; a PRESCRIPTION timer never pauses.
5. TimerCheckJob (JOB-05): every 5 minutes finds RUNNING timers whose warn_at or expires_at has passed.
6. TimerCheckJob: for a passed warn_at, writes the decision log entry and sends MSG-P3-003 to the case owner once.
7. TimerCheckJob: for a passed expires_at of a SERVICE_LEVEL timer, writes the decision log entry with rule R-UNI-30, sets the timer EXPIRED with escalation level 1, and publishes TimerBreached with the escalation role; the case keeps its queue and owner.
8. TimerCheckJob: for a passed expires_at of any other timer type, sets it EXPIRED and publishes TimerDue.
9. TimerPauseHandler: on DeviationRaised calls TimerScheduler.pause(timerId); on DeviationCleared calls TimerScheduler.resume(timerId), which moves expires_at and warn_at by the paused time (R-UNI-43).
10. Case owner or team manager: reads the timers through GET /cases/{caseId}/timers and the prescription date through GET /cases/{caseId}.
11. No caller writes or updates the timer table directly: every schedule, cancel, pause and resume goes through TimerScheduler (BR10).

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No SERVICE_LEVEL version is in force on the date | No timer; the case is listed on the exception queue | MSG-P3-026 | AC4 |
| X2 | No legal period for the product | Prescription date not set; the case is listed on the exception queue | MSG-P3-026 | AC5 |
| X3 | An account has no last payment date | The contract date is used | None | AC6 |
| X4 | JOB-05 did not run for 40 minutes | The next run raises every missed warning and breach once | None | AC7 |
| X5 | The timer check runs again after a breach | The breach is not raised twice | None | AC8 |
| X6 | Decision log write fails at a breach | The timer stays RUNNING and the breach is raised by the next run | MSG-P7-003 | AC9 |
| X7 | A deviation is raised on the case | Service level timer paused; prescription timer keeps running | MSG-P3-004 | AC10 |
| X8 | The warning point is 4 of 5 working days | Warning sent once, at the first check after 4 working days have passed | MSG-P3-003 | AC11 |
| X9 | A role without Case record R reads the timers | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-028-12 |
| X10 | A class outside `recovery.casewf.timers` writes or updates the timer table | The build fails on the boundary test; no timer row is changed at run time | None | AC12 |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A SERVICE_LEVEL timer starts each time the case enters a queue or a status, from the SERVICE_LEVEL row for its product group and status | SERVICE_LEVEL table (RWB-E1-045); DL22; VR-P3-011-1 |
| BR2 | The warning is raised at the warning percentage of the service level | SERVICE_LEVEL warning percent, 80 assumed (DL22) |
| BR3 | A breach is raised to the named escalation role. The case does not move | R-UNI-30; REQ-CWC-011; FEAT-CWC-13 |
| BR4 | The prescription date is the earliest of last payment date plus the legal period over the linked accounts; the contract date applies when no payment exists | LEGAL_PERIOD table (RWB-E1-043); REQ-CWC-012 |
| BR5 | The prescription timer never pauses | R-DEV-01; FEAT-DVH-03; Timer.paused description in api.yaml |
| BR6 | A deviation pauses the stage clock; clearing it resumes the clock and recomputes the timers | R-UNI-04, R-UNI-43 |
| BR7 | A legal hold keeps the clocks running and visible | R-UNI-20 |
| BR8 | Service levels count working days from the holiday calendar in v_ace_holiday | v_ace_holiday over public.bot_holiday (RWB-E1-043) |
| BR9 | Each timer start, warning and breach is logged with its rule and version | REQ-CWC-016; Principle 5 |
| BR10 | Timer scheduling goes only through TimerScheduler: every caller schedules, pauses, resumes and cancels a timer through the port, and no caller writes or updates the timer table | D-RCV-36 T2; ADR-011; FEAT-CWC-11 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the timer status (LOV-TIMER-STATUS):

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | CaseAllocated, CaseTransferred, CaseStateChanged | Service level found | RUNNING |
| RUNNING | CaseTransferred or CaseStateChanged | New queue or status | STOPPED |
| RUNNING | DeviationRaised | Timer type SERVICE_LEVEL | PAUSED |
| PAUSED | DeviationCleared | None | RUNNING, expires_at recomputed |
| RUNNING | JOB-05 | expires_at passed | EXPIRED, TimerBreached or TimerDue |

### 12. Contract

**Job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Quartz schedule |
| Job name | JOB-05 Timer check |
| Engine | Quartz; this job is the Epic 1 implementation of the TimerScheduler port (D-RCV-36 T2), with no Temporal schedule |
| Schedule | Every 5 minutes |
| Input | RUNNING timers with warn_at or expires_at before now (index ix_timer_due) |
| Output | Warnings, breaches, expired timers, decision log entries |
| Events published | TimerBreached (EV-19: timerId, caseId, escalateTo); TimerDue (EV-18: timerId, caseId, timerType) |
| Idempotency key | timerId and the point (WARN or EXPIRE); a timer already EXPIRED or already warned is skipped |
| Restart | The next run picks up every missed timer (batch.txt JOB-05) |

**Events consumed.** CaseCreated (EV-01), CaseAllocated (EV-02), CaseTransferred (EV-04), CaseStateChanged (EV-05), DeviationRaised (EV-06), DeviationCleared (EV-07).

**GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path caseId (uuid) |
| Response | Timer[]: id, caseId, timerType, startedAt, expiresAt, warnAt, paused, status, escalationLevel |
| Errors | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Case record R (MSG-P4-002); 404 not found or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 503 |
| Authorization | Case record, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId} returns prescriptionDate (Case schema).

**Published interfaces** (package `recovery.casewf.timers`)

```java
// P3, package recovery.casewf.timers (published)
public interface TimerScheduler { void schedule(TimerSpec t); void cancel(UUID timerId); void pause(UUID timerId); void resume(UUID timerId); }

// P3, package recovery.casewf.timers (published)
public interface TimerService {
    List<TimerView> timersFor(UUID caseId);
    Optional<LocalDate> prescriptionDate(UUID caseId);
}
// P3 (RWB-E1-045) and P3 (RWB-E1-043), used by this story
ServiceLevel serviceLevel(String productGroup, String caseStatus, LocalDate businessDate);   // ProductParameterService
VersionedRows rows(String tableCode, LocalDate businessDate);                                // ReferenceDataService: LEGAL_PERIOD
// P1, used by this story
public interface RecoveryDataQuery {
    List<AccountDates> accountDates(List<UUID> accountIds);   // contract_date, last_payment_date, data_as_of
    List<LocalDate> holidays(LocalDate from, LocalDate to);   // the non-working dates of v_ace_holiday
}
```

Every caller schedules, cancels, pauses and resumes a timer through TimerScheduler and no caller writes a timer row directly. TimerCheckJob (JOB-05, Quartz) is the Epic 1 implementation: schedule, cancel, pause and resume write or change the timer row, and the 5-minute fire runs the warning, breach and expiry check. Epic 3 replaces that implementation with Temporal durable timers and no caller changes (ADR-011).

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `recovery/casewf/timers`, Java package `recovery.casewf.timers`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TimerStarter | Listener | Starts and stops SERVICE_LEVEL timers on case events through TimerScheduler |
| PrescriptionService | Listener | Sets the prescription date and schedules the PRESCRIPTION timer through TimerScheduler on CaseCreated |
| TimerPauseHandler | Listener | Pauses and resumes SERVICE_LEVEL timers through TimerScheduler on deviation events |
| TimerCheckJob | Job | JOB-05 on Quartz; implements TimerScheduler (schedule, cancel, pause, resume) and runs the warning, breach and expiry checks |
| TimerScheduler | Published interface | The port every caller uses to schedule, cancel, pause and resume a timer; the Epic 1 implementation is TimerCheckJob |
| WorkingDayCalculator | Service | Adds working days with the holiday calendar from v_ace_holiday |
| TimerService | Published interface | Reads timers and the prescription date for other modules |
| CaseAndWorkflowController | Controller | GET /cases/{caseId}/timers |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | timer, recovery_case |

**Database**

- Writes timer (all columns) through the TimerScheduler implementation only, recovery_case.prescription_date, outbox.
- Reads with index ix_timer_due (expires_at WHERE status = 'RUNNING'); add `ix_timer_warn ON timer (warn_at) WHERE status = 'RUNNING'` in migration `V028_1__timer_warn_index.sql`, plus column timer.warned_at (New) to record the single warning.
- One running SERVICE_LEVEL timer per case: partial unique index `ux_timer_sl_running ON timer (case_id) WHERE timer_type = 'SERVICE_LEVEL' AND status IN ('RUNNING','PAUSED')`.

**Configuration and reference data**

- SERVICE_LEVEL rows (business lead, DL22) through ProductParameterService (RWB-E1-045).
- LEGAL_PERIOD rows through ReferenceDataService (RWB-E1-043), owned by Legal; the holiday calendar through v_ace_holiday (DF-ACE-155 holiday_date, DF-ACE-159 holiday_weekday).
- Parameter legal.prescription.warn.days = 180 (assumed; owner Legal) through RWB-E1-042.
- LOV-TIMER and LOV-TIMER-STATUS.

**Build steps**

1. Build the TimerScheduler port and its Quartz implementation in TimerCheckJob: schedule, cancel, pause and resume write the timer row; test AC12 with the boundary test.
2. WorkingDayCalculator with the holiday calendar from v_ace_holiday; unit tests for AC1 and AC11.
3. TimerStarter with cancel and schedule on each case event through TimerScheduler; test AC1, AC4, AC12.
4. PrescriptionService with the earliest-date rule and the contract date fallback; tests AC3, AC5, AC6.
5. TimerCheckJob warning branch with warned_at; test AC2 warning, AC11.
6. TimerCheckJob expiry branch: EXPIRED, TimerBreached in the outbox and the decision log write in one transaction; tests AC2, AC8, AC9.
7. Catch-up of missed runs in one pass ordered by expires_at; test AC7.
8. TimerPauseHandler with pause and resume through TimerScheduler and recomputed dates; test AC10.
9. GET /cases/{caseId}/timers with access check.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.timers`. Off: no timers start, the TimerScheduler implementation is not registered and JOB-05 does nothing.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and JOB-05 handles 26,500 open cases' timers inside one 5-minute cycle in SIT (NFR-001 volume).

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: service levels, the warning point, escalation roles, legal periods and holidays are data.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts; cases are named by case number.
- No read of another module's tables; ACE data only through recovery.v_ace_* views: account dates through RecoveryDataQuery (P1).
- A breach never moves the case; the prescription timer never pauses.
- Timer scheduling goes only through TimerScheduler; no class outside recovery.casewf.timers writes or updates the timer table.
- No Temporal schedule and no Temporal durable timer in Epic 1: JOB-05 stays on Quartz behind the port (D-RCV-36 T2).

## RWB-E1-030 Daily rebalancing and queue measures

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-030 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-17 Rebalance queues daily; FEAT-CWC-18 Publish queue measures; FEAT-WKM-11 Reallocate when the caseload cap is breached; FEAT-RPT-02 Publish queue and ageing measures |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-015, REQ-RDF-012 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.1 and 5.3 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes; 15 Manage performance, data and AI |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-020, RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-028 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **a daily job that assigns unassigned cases and moves the newest cases off owners above the cap by the assignment rules, and queue counts, ageing and service level breaches published to Power BI**, so that **queues stay balanced and every team manager sees the same numbers as the case list**.

### 2. Business rationale

Team managers rebalance work by hand today and count queues from spreadsheets that do not match. This story moves cases left in overflow or without an owner each morning, takes owners above the cap back inside it (R-UNI-19), and publishes depth, ageing, owner spread and breaches as one snapshot that reconciles to the case list. It meets REQ-CWC-015 and REQ-RDF-012.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-020 is done: AssignmentEngine and CapacityService answer for the queue version in force.
- RWB-E1-028 is done: timers are EXPIRED on a service level breach.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available.
- Caseload caps are loaded (DL23). If DL23 is late, rebalancing reports and moves nothing.
- JOB-03 has completed for the business date; JOB-06 runs as SY-CASEWF.
- JOB-15 Reporting extract copies the snapshot to the data lake for Power BI nightly (owner RW-BIANAL).

### 4. Flow

1. Quartz: starts JOB-06 at 06:30, or when JOB-03 completes for the business date if that is later.
2. RebalanceJob: lists cases in each queue with no owner and status NEW or ASSIGNED, and owners whose open cases exceed their capacity.
3. RebalanceService: for each owner above the cap, selects the newest cases by assignment time until the owner is inside the cap (R-UNI-19).
4. RebalanceService: skips cases with deviation_open or legal_hold true.
5. AssignmentEngine: picks an owner below the cap in the same queue for each selected or unassigned case.
6. RebalanceService: writes the decision log entry, ends the old assignment, writes the new one with reason REBALANCE and publishes CaseTransferred, case by case.
7. QueueMeasureService: at the end of the run, takes one snapshot per queue at one time: depth, unassigned, age in days from the entry date, owner spread and SERVICE_LEVEL timers EXPIRED.
8. QueueMeasureService: checks each queue depth against the case count for the same queue and time, and publishes the snapshot only when every queue matches.
9. JOB-15: copies the snapshot to the data lake; Power BI shows it from the next morning.
10. TimerBreachNotifier: on TimerBreached from JOB-05, sends the team manager MSG-P3-028 with the queue's breach count.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No member of the queue has capacity | Cases stay where they are; counted in the summary | MSG-P3-011 | AC4 |
| X2 | No caseload cap is loaded for the queue | The queue is reported and nothing is moved | None | AC5 |
| X3 | Decision log write fails for a case | That case is not moved; the run continues | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | JOB-06 runs again the same day | Already balanced queues give no further moves | None | AC7 |
| X5 | A case has an open deviation or a legal hold | Not moved | None | AC8 |
| X6 | The snapshot depth differs from the case count | Snapshot not published; break listed for the data steward | MSG-P3-029 | AC9 |
| X7 | An owner holds exactly the cap | No case is moved off them | None | AC10 |
| X8 | A role without Platform administration U reruns JOB-06 | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-030-11 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reuses the assignment engine (RWB-E1-020) and the timers (RWB-E1-028) |
| Negotiable | Caps and the ordering of moves are data (DL23) |
| Valuable | Removes daily hand rebalancing and gives one set of queue numbers |
| Estimable | One job, one measure snapshot, one notifier |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Cases with no owner are assigned by the queue's method within the cap | queue.assignment_method, queue.capacity_cap; FEAT-CWC-17 |
| BR2 | An owner above the cap loses the newest cases until inside the cap | R-UNI-19 |
| BR3 | Cases with an open deviation or a legal hold are not moved | R-UNI-20; R-DEV-01 |
| BR4 | A queue with no cap is reported and not rebalanced | DL23 |
| BR5 | A move keeps the case status and the clocks | R-UNI-18 |
| BR6 | Measures publish only when queue depths reconcile to the case list with zero difference | DL25; REC-01 |
| BR7 | Every move is logged before it takes effect | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | A breach raises an alert to the escalation role; the case does not move | R-UNI-30 |

### 12. Contract

**Job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Quartz at 06:30, after JOB-03 completes for the business date |
| Job name | JOB-06 Daily rebalancing |
| Schedule | Daily 06:30 |
| Input | Queues in force, members and capacity, open cases per owner, cases with no owner, EXPIRED service level timers |
| Output | Assignments with reason REBALANCE, decision log entries, one queue_measure snapshot per queue |
| Events published | CaseTransferred (EV-04) per move |
| Idempotency key | caseId and businessDate for a move; queueId and snapshot time for a snapshot |
| Restart | Rerun from the job monitor; balanced queues give no moves; managers rebalance by hand if the rerun fails (batch.txt) |

**GET /api/recovery/v1/cases** (used for the reconciliation test)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query queue (uuid), status, page, size |
| Response | CasePage: items, page, size, total |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Case record R (MSG-P4-002); 503 |
| Authorization | Case record, right R, scope applied |

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun** (P1) for JOB-06: Platform administration U; 409 when the job is running.

```java
}
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `recovery/casewf/rebalance`, Java package `recovery.casewf.rebalance`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RebalanceJob | Job | JOB-06; selects cases and owners, calls RebalanceService, writes counts |
| RebalanceService | Service | R-UNI-19 selection, hold checks, owner choice, decision log, assignment swap |
| QueueMeasureService | Published interface | Takes, reconciles and publishes the snapshot |
| TimerBreachNotifier | Listener | Sends MSG-P3-028 to the team manager on TimerBreached |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | recovery_case, assignment, queue, queue_member, timer, queue_measure |

**Database**

- Writes assignment, recovery_case.owner_user_id, queue_measure, outbox.
- Snapshot query in one REPEATABLE READ transaction so depth and the case count are read at the same time.
- Migration in this story: `V030_1__queue_measure.sql` creates queue_measure (id, queue_id, as_of, depth, unassigned, avg_age_days, max_age_days, owner_min, owner_max, breached, status, standard columns; unique (queue_id, as_of)).

**Configuration and reference data**

- Caps and member capacity from RWB-E1-019 (DL23).
- Measure definitions agreed with the Tribe (REQ-RDF-012), owned by RW-COE.

**Build steps**

1. Owner over cap selection by newest assignment; unit tests AC8, AC10.
2. RebalanceService with AssignmentEngine and hold checks; tests AC1, AC4, AC5.
3. One transaction per case with the decision log write as its last step; continue on failure; test AC6.
4. Idempotent rerun; test AC7.
5. QueueMeasureService snapshot and reconciliation; tests AC2, AC9.
6. TimerBreachNotifier; test AC3.
7. P9 hand-off through QueueMeasureService for JOB-15.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.rebalance`. Off: JOB-06 does not move cases; the snapshot still runs.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and the Power BI queue page shows the 2026-12-02 snapshot on 2026-12-03 in SIT.

## RWB-E1-031 Queue and owner on the case list with filters

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-031 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-19 Show queue and owner on the case list |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-007, REQ-ACA-009 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.3 and 3.4; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.3 and 5.4 |
| L3 process | 06 Take over and own the case |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-020, RWB-E1-039 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **the queue and owner columns on the case list, with filters by queue, team and status and an export to Excel**, so that **I see my queues and who owns each case without a new screen**.

### 2. Business rationale

Today a team manager asks each collector for their list to know who holds which case. With allocation by rule (RWB-E1-020), every case has a queue and an owner; this story shows both on the case list, filters by queue, team and status inside the manager's scope, and exports the filtered list with the export written to the access log for PDPA. It meets REQ-CWC-007 (the result of allocation is visible) and REQ-ACA-009 (a user sees only the cases their scope allows).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-020 is done: cases carry queue_id, team_code and owner_user_id.
- RWB-E1-039 is done: the access log interface records exports.
- The user holds a role with Case record R; the team manager's default scope is Team (roles.txt).
- Parameter `caselist.export.maxrows` = 10,000 (assumed; DL11) from RWB-E1-042.
- Owner display names come from the ACE user directory in the common module.

### 4. Flow

1. Team manager: opens SCR-02 Case list; the screen shows the Loading state.
2. CaseListPage: calls GET /cases with page 0 and size 50; the service applies the caller's scope.
3. CaseListPage: shows each row with case number, product, status, stage, queue, owner and entry date (list state).
4. Team manager: picks queue "DIL-BKK-CO", team "DIL-BKK" and status "ASSIGNED"; the page calls GET /cases with the filters (filtered state).
5. CaseQueryService: returns only cases inside the caller's scope that meet every filter, with the total.
6. Team manager: chooses Export.
7. CaseExportService: checks the row count against the limit, publishes the access event AC-EXPT with user, time, filters and row count, then builds the xlsx with masking by role (FieldMasker, RWB-E1-037).
8. Browser: downloads "Case list 20261202 1.xlsx".

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No case meets the filters | Empty state with a plain sentence | MSG-P3-020 | AC3 |
| X2 | The filtered list holds more rows than the export limit | Export refused; the user narrows the filter | MSG-P3-021 | AC4 |
| X3 | The access log cannot be written | Export not made | MSG-P7-003 | AC5 |
| X4 | A filter names a queue outside the caller's scope | Only in-scope cases return; an out-of-scope queue returns none | MSG-P3-020 | AC6 |
| X5 | A case has no owner | Owner cell is blank; the case is still listed | None | AC7 |
| X6 | Exactly 10,000 rows | Export allowed | None | AC8 |
| X7 | A role without Case record R opens the list | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-031-09 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads fields RWB-E1-020 fills; adds columns and filters to an existing screen |
| Negotiable | Column order and the export limit are configurable |
| Valuable | Team managers see ownership on one screen |
| Estimable | Two query parameters, one export endpoint, one screen change |
| Small | Fits under one week |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

| BR6 | A screen responds in under 2 seconds | NFR-008 |

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the export limit and the lists come from data.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts; the export applies masking by role and holds no customer name or ID number.
- No read of another module's tables: the access log is written through AccessEventPublisher (P4); owner names come from the ACE user directory interface.
- The export is never made when its access log entry cannot be written.
