## RWB-E1-060 Extraction evaluation [E1c]

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-060 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P10 Agent runtime |
| Feature | FEAT-AGT-04 Evaluate document extraction quality |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-005, REQ-DCM-006 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.9; Business Requirements Program, section 5.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-053, RWB-E1-058 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **field extraction for the six document types scored against the labeled sample for three approaches (OCR template, model, and OCR checked by the model)**, so that **the extraction approach and the confidence threshold for each document type are chosen on measured precision and recall**.

### 2. Business rationale

Fields read wrongly from a court notice or a title deed send a case down the wrong step, and fields sent to review without need take officer time. This story measures the three approaches on the same reviewed documents, field by field, and proposes for each document type the approach and the confidence threshold below which a field goes to the review queue. It serves REQ-DCM-006 (fields extracted for the agreed types) and REQ-DCM-005 (confidence score and review queue below the threshold).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-053 is done: the P5 pipeline (SY-OCR) writes document_field rows with a confidence per field for the six types in LOV-DOC-TYPE (assumed six types; DL19).
- RWB-E1-058 is done: the gateway, the evaluation harness and the sample loader exist.
- Approved agent_policy "EXTRACT" version "P1" (mode SHADOW, allowed tools read_document_content, read_document_fields) and prompt "PR1".
- Labeled sample "EXTRACT-S1" version 1 is loaded: fields confirmed or corrected by a person (document_field.confirmed_by set), at least 30 documents per type. Personal field values are held as SHA-256 hashes.
- RW-COE holds Rules and parameters C.

### 4. Flow

1. RW-COE: loads sample "EXTRACT-S1" through POST /admin/agent-samples with one row per document and field.
2. RW-COE: starts the evaluation with approaches OCR_TEMPLATE, MODEL and OCR_AND_MODEL through POST /admin/agent-evaluations.
3. System: for OCR_TEMPLATE, reads the stored document_field values through the P5 interface; makes no model call.
4. System: for MODEL, calls agent "EXTRACT" in shadow on the document content and reads the fields from its answer.
5. System: for OCR_AND_MODEL, passes the OCR fields with the content to agent "EXTRACT" and takes its checked values.
6. System: compares each value with the label and stores true positives, false positives, false negatives, precision and recall per field and approach.
7. System: for each document type, picks the approach with the highest F1 and proposes the confidence threshold for the review queue.
8. RW-COE: reads the result through GET /admin/agent-evaluations and exports it; the solution architect records the choice as a proposed architecture decision after ADR-009.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A document type has fewer than 30 labeled documents | The type is scored and marked "insufficient sample"; no approach is proposed for it | None to a user | AC3 |
| X2 | The model times out or fails a guardrail on a document | The MODEL value counts as empty (false negative); the failure is counted on the run | None to a user | AC4 |
| X3 | Two approaches have the same F1 for a type | The approach with fewer model calls is proposed (OCR_TEMPLATE before OCR_AND_MODEL before MODEL) | None to a user | AC5 |
| X4 | A sample row names a document or field that does not exist | The sample load is refused in full | MSG-P10-001 | AC6 |
| X5 | No approach reaches precision 0.95 on a field at any confidence | The field is proposed as review-only | None to a user | AC7 |
| X6 | Evaluation started while the same one is running | Refused with 409 | MSG-P10-003 | AC8 |
| X7 | A role without the right | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-060-09 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the extraction pipeline (RWB-E1-053) and the harness (RWB-E1-058) |
| Negotiable | Thresholds, sample size floor and the tie order are parameters in the policy row |
| Valuable | Sets the review threshold that decides how many documents an officer checks by hand |
| Estimable | Two scorers and one proposal rule on top of the existing harness |
| Small | Under two weeks with one developer |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on a fixture of labeled documents with known counts |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Extraction evaluation [E1c]

  Background:
    Given sample "EXTRACT-S1" version 1 holds 40 court notices of type "COURT_NOTICE" with labels for fields court_name, case_number and hearing_date
    Given the target precision is 0.95 and the minimum labeled documents per type is 30

  Scenario: AC1 Scores per field
    Given the labeled sample
    When the three approaches run
    Then one score row exists per field and approach: 3 fields x 3 approaches for "COURT_NOTICE"
    Then for field hearing_date with approach OCR_TEMPLATE, 34 true positives, 2 false positives and 4 false negatives give precision 0.9444 and recall 0.8947
    Then each score row holds the model version and the prompt version "PR1" where the approach calls the model

  Scenario: AC2 Decision recorded
    Given the scores for "COURT_NOTICE"
    When the proposal is built
    Then the evaluation run names, for "COURT_NOTICE", the approach with the highest mean F1 and its precision and recall per field
    Then it names the proposed confidence threshold: the lowest confidence at which every chosen field reaches precision 0.95
    Then the export lists one row per document type for the solution architect's architecture decision

  Scenario: AC3 A type with too few labels
    Given type "TITLE_DEED" has 12 labeled documents
    When the evaluation runs
    Then the system scores "TITLE_DEED" and marked "insufficient sample"
    Then no approach and no threshold are proposed for "TITLE_DEED"

  Scenario: AC4 A model failure counts against the model approaches
    Given the model stub times out on document 7 of 40
    When the approach MODEL runs
    Then each labeled field of document 7 counts as a false negative for MODEL
    Then the evaluation run holds failure count TIMED_OUT 1

  Scenario: AC5 Equal F1
    Given OCR_TEMPLATE and OCR_AND_MODEL both have mean F1 0.9310 for "COURT_NOTICE"
    When the proposal is built
    Then the system proposes OCR_TEMPLATE

  Scenario: AC6 A sample row for a document that does not exist
    Given the sample file has a row for a document ID that the P5 interface does not return
    When RW-COE loads the file
    Then the system refuses the load with 422 and MSG-P10-001 naming the row number
    Then the system stores no row of the file

  Scenario: AC7 A field that never reaches the target
    Given field case_number reaches at most precision 0.91 for every approach and confidence
    When the proposal is built
    Then the system proposes case_number as review-only for "COURT_NOTICE"

  Scenario: AC8 The same evaluation twice
    Given the evaluation of "EXTRACT" on "EXTRACT-S1" version 1 is running
    When RW-COE starts it again
    Then the system refuses the request with 409 and MSG-P10-003
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A value is a true positive when it equals the label after trim and case folding; dates compare as dates; personal fields compare by SHA-256 hash | agent_sample.expected_value (New); CTL-11 |
| BR2 | Precision = TP / (TP + FP); recall = TP / (TP + FN); F1 = 2PR / (P + R); 4 decimals | agent_evaluation (New) |
| BR3 | A type with fewer labeled documents than the minimum (30, assumed; DL19) gets no proposal | agent_policy row EXTRACT (New) |
| BR4 | The proposed threshold is the lowest confidence where precision reaches the target (0.95, assumed; DL11); a field that never reaches it is review-only | REQ-DCM-005; document_field.confidence |
| BR5 | Ties go to the approach with fewer model calls | agent_policy row EXTRACT (New) |
| BR6 | The OCR_TEMPLATE approach reads stored fields only and makes no model call | DT06 |

None. This story does not change a case status. It writes one evaluation run (RUNNING to DONE) and its score rows. The threshold it proposes takes effect only when P5 loads it as a new reference data version.

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-evaluations** (new): query agent, from, to; 200 AgentEvaluationRun[] with score rows and the proposal per document type; errors 401, 403, 503; Rules and parameters R. Export: Accept text/csv returns the proposal rows.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `src/main/java/.../recovery/agent/eval/extraction/`, Java package `recovery.agent.eval.extraction`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ExtractionApproachRunner | Service | Produces field values per document for each of the three approaches |
| FieldMatchScorer | Service | Applies BR1 and BR2 per field and approach |
| ExtractionProposalBuilder | Service | Applies BR3 to BR5 and writes the proposal JSON on the evaluation run |
| SampleRowValidator | Service | Checks each sample row against P5 before the load is stored |
| prompt EXTRACT PR1 and schema extract-fields-v1 | Rule table | Prompt and output schema loaded through the configuration endpoint |

**Database:** adds column proposal jsonb to agent_evaluation_run in migration `V10_003__evaluation_proposal.sql`; writes agent_sample, agent_run, agent_evaluation_run, agent_evaluation.

**Configuration and reference data:** agent_policy EXTRACT P1 holds the target precision 0.95, the minimum sample 30 and the tie order; loaded by RW-COE, approved by RW-RISK. Document types come from LOV-DOC-TYPE through P4.

**Build steps**
1. Build SampleRowValidator and the hash of personal label values (AC6).
2. Build ExtractionApproachRunner for OCR_TEMPLATE over the P5 interface (AC1).
3. Add the MODEL and OCR_AND_MODEL paths through AgentOrchestrator in shadow (AC1, AC4).
4. Build FieldMatchScorer with a fixture of 40 court notices and known counts (AC1).
5. Build ExtractionProposalBuilder and the CSV export (AC2, AC3, AC5, AC7).
6. Add the running-evaluation check (AC8) and the access test.

**Feature flag:** `rwb.agent.extraction-eval`. Off: the approaches list accepts only AGENT and the extraction approaches are refused with 422.

**Done when:** the tests in section 16 pass and a DEV run over the six types produces one proposal row per type.

## RWB-E1-061 Intake agent evaluation and L1 proposal [E2a]

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-061 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P10 Agent runtime |
| Feature | FEAT-AGT-07 Run the case intake agent at L1 |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-010, REQ-DRI-011 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.9; Business Requirements Program, section 5.7 |
| L3 process | 06 Take over and own the case |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-059 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the evaluation report of the case intake agent and the proposal to run it at autonomy level 1, built from the stored shadow results**, so that **the risk and model risk officer approves the step to L1 on measured results**.

### 2. Business rationale

The step from shadow to L1 puts agent output in front of case owners, so the approver needs the agreement rate, the failure types, the cost and the latency on a stated sample before deciding. This story produces that report from the evaluation run of RWB-E1-059 and holds the L1 proposal as a versioned policy row with its conditions, fallback and measures to watch (REQ-DRI-010), approved and dated like any other reference row (REQ-DRI-011). Nothing goes to L1 until RW-RISK approves the row.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-059 is done: evaluation run of "INTAKE" on sample "INTAKE-S1" version 1 has status DONE with 200 labeled cases.
- Policy "INTAKE" version "P1" (SHADOW) is in force.
- RW-COE holds Rules and parameters C; RW-RISK holds Rules and parameters A.

### 4. Flow

1. RW-COE: requests the report for the evaluation run through GET /admin/agent-evaluations/{evaluationId}/report.
2. System: builds the report from the stored runs and scores: sample size, agreement rate per gap type, failure counts by type, total and per-case cost, median and 95th percentile latency, policy, prompt and model versions.
3. RW-COE: exports the report as CSV and PDF for the steering committee pack.
4. RW-COE: loads policy "INTAKE" version "P2" with autonomy mode L1, the evaluation run ID, the conditions, the fallback and the measures to watch through POST /admin/agent-configs.
5. System: checks that the evaluation run is DONE, that its scores meet every stated condition and that the fallback and measures are present; stores the version as LOADED.
6. RW-RISK: approves version "P2" with a valid from date through POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve after the committee agrees.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The report is requested for an evaluation that is still running | Refused with 409 | MSG-P10-008 | AC3 |
| X2 | The L1 proposal has no conditions, no fallback or no measures | Load refused in full | MSG-P10-001 | AC4 |
| X3 | The evaluation scores do not meet a stated condition | Load refused, naming the gap type and the score | MSG-P10-001 | AC5 |
| X4 | The sample size is below the minimum of 200 cases | Load refused | MSG-P10-001 | AC6 |
| X5 | The loader tries to approve the proposal | Refused with 409 | MSG-P7-002 | AC7 |
| X6 | A role without the right | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-061-08 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads only the stored results of RWB-E1-059 |
| Negotiable | Conditions and measures are values in the proposal row; the story fixes their presence and the check against scores |
| Valuable | Gives the approver one report and one row to approve for the first autonomy step |
| Estimable | One report query, one export, one extra check in the policy loader |
| Small | Three to four days |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on a stored evaluation fixture |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin

  Background:
    Given evaluation run "EV-INTAKE-001" of "INTAKE" on sample "INTAKE-S1" version 1 has status "DONE"
    Given it holds 200 shadow runs: 188 ANSWERED, 7 TIMED_OUT, 3 GUARDRAIL_FAILED and 2 BELOW_FLOOR
    Given the 200 runs cost 412.6000 baht in total with median latency 4,100 ms and 95th percentile 9,800 ms

  Scenario: AC1 Report

    When the report is written

    Then it holds policy "P1", prompt "PR1" and the model version, and no personal field

  Scenario: AC2 Proposal

    Then the system stores version "P2" with status "LOADED" and holds the conditions, the fallback and the measures to watch
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | An L1 proposal names one DONE evaluation run, the conditions, the fallback and the measures to watch | agent_policy.promotion_conditions, watch_measures, evaluation_run_id (New) |
| BR2 | Every stated condition is checked against the scores of the named run before the version is stored | Principle 1; CTL-08 |
| BR3 | The minimum sample for an autonomy step is 200 cases (assumed; set in the policy loader schema) | FEAT-AGT-03 |
| BR4 | Cost per case = total cost / runs, 4 decimals; latency percentiles are computed over all runs including timeouts at 60,000 ms | agent_run.cost_thb, latency_ms (New) |
| BR5 | The fallback of an L1 agent is the rule result | R-UNI-32 |
| BR6 | The loader and the approver are different people | Separation of duty, center of excellence analyst and risk and model risk officer |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. Policy version "P2" moves from no row to LOADED, and to APPROVED when RW-RISK approves it.

| RW-AUDIT | Reads the report and the versions (Rules and parameters R) |

### 12. Contract

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-evaluations/{evaluationId}/report** (new, see additions)
- Request: path runId (uuid); Accept application/json, text/csv or application/pdf.
- Response: 200 AgentEvaluationReport (agent, sampleSize, versions, agreementByLabel[], failureCounts, totalCostThb, costPerCaseThb, latencyP50Ms, latencyP95Ms).
- Errors: 401; 403; 404 unknown run; 409 run not DONE (MSG-P10-008); 503.
- Authorization: Rules and parameters, R. Idempotency: read only; the same run gives the same report.

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-configs** (new, RWB-E1-058): kind POLICY, agent "INTAKE"; this story adds the L1 checks (BR1 to BR3); 201 AgentConfigVersion; errors 401, 403, 409, 422 (MSG-P10-001), 503; Rules and parameters C.

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve** (new): 200; errors 401, 403, 404, 409 (MSG-P7-002, MSG-GEN-004), 503; Rules and parameters A.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `src/main/java/.../recovery/agent/eval/report/`, Java package `recovery.agent.eval.report`; policy checks in `recovery.agent.config`.

| EvaluationReportService | Service | Aggregates runs and scores into the report |
| EvaluationReportExporter | Service | Writes CSV and PDF from the same report object |
| PromotionProposalValidator | Service | BR1 to BR3 checks inside AgentConfigService for mode L1 |

**Database:** migration `V10_004__policy_promotion.sql` adds evaluation_run_id uuid, promotion_conditions jsonb, watch_measures jsonb and fallback_rule varchar(20) to agent_policy. Reads agent_run, agent_evaluation_run and agent_evaluation.

**Configuration and reference data:** the minimum sample 200 is a value in the policy JSON schema version used by the loader.

**Build steps**
1. Build EvaluationReportService over a fixture of 200 runs with the counts in the Background (AC1).
2. Build the CSV and PDF exporter from the same object (AC1).
3. Add the 409 for a run that is not DONE (AC3).
4. Build PromotionProposalValidator and add it to the policy load (AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6).
5. Reuse the approval check from RWB-E1-058 and test it for an L1 version (AC7).

**Feature flag:** `rwb.agent.promotion`. Off: a policy with mode L1 is refused with 422.

**Done when:** the tests in section 16 pass and the report for "EV-INTAKE-001" is attached to the steering committee pack.

## RWB-E1-062 Deviation screening agent in shadow [E2b]

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-062 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P10 Agent runtime |
| Feature | FEAT-DVH-01 Flag a deviation X1 to X7 on the case; FEAT-DVH-04 Route the deviation to the named owner; FEAT-DVH-08 Review a flagged deviation below the confidence threshold; FEAT-AGT-08 Run the deviation screening agent at L1 |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DVH-001, REQ-DVH-003, REQ-DVH-007 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.9; Business Requirements Program, section 5.15 |
| L3 process | 11 Handle customer care and deviations |
| Decision | X1 to X7 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-058, RWB-TE-013 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the deviation screening agent to propose X1 to X7 with reasons from case data, call notes and documents, in shadow on Epic 1 cases**, so that **the Epic 2 and Epic 3 deviation flags start from an agent with measured precision and recall per deviation type**.

### 2. Business rationale

A dispute, a death, a fraud sign or a lost contact found late means contact that should have stopped, or a case worked on the wrong route. The screening agent reads the case, the interaction ledger and the documents at entry and when a document arrives, and proposes deviations with reasons. In Epic 1 the proposals are stored only, scored against the business analysts' review and shown to nobody. The story measures detection from case data, call notes and documents (REQ-DVH-001), the named owner each code would route to (REQ-DVH-003) and the contact that preceded a complaint (REQ-DVH-007).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-058 and RWB-TE-013 are done.
- Approved agent_policy "SCREENING" version "P1": mode SHADOW, timeout 60 seconds, confidence floor 0.80, allowed tools read_case, read_interactions, read_documents, read_document_fields, and output schema "screening-v1" with codes from LOV-DEVIATION (X1 to X7).
- Approved prompt "SCREENING" version "PR1".
- Rule rows R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 are loaded, so the owner role of each code is data.
- Labeled sample "SCREEN-S1" version 1: the business analysts' review of 200 Epic 1 cases, one row per case and code with expected value Y or N.

### 4. Flow

1. SY-CASEWF or P5: writes EV-01 CaseCreated for a new case, or EV-16 DocumentStored for a document on an open case.
2. System (ScreeningShadowListener): calls the orchestrator for agent "SCREENING" with key "SCREENING:<caseId>:<eventId>".
3. System: reads the case, the interaction ledger entries, the documents and their fields as SY-AGENT, masks personal fields and calls the model.
4. System: checks the answer: each proposal has a code in X1 to X7, reasons, source references and a confidence.
5. System: reads the owner role each proposed code routes to from the rule catalog (RuleCatalog, RWB-E1-072) (R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06) and stores it with the proposal.
6. System: marks proposals below the confidence floor as "review"; stores everything on the agent run in mode SHADOW. No deviation record, contact stop or clock change is made.
7. RW-COE: starts the evaluation of "SCREENING" on sample "SCREEN-S1".
8. System: compares proposals at or above the floor with the labels and stores precision and recall per deviation code, with the count of review proposals.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The answer has a code outside X1 to X7 | Check SCHEMA fails; run GUARDRAIL_FAILED; fallback true | None to a user | AC8 |
| X2 | A proposal is below the confidence floor 0.80 | Stored with marker "review"; scored separately | None to a user | AC6 |
| X3 | An X1 proposal names no preceding contact while the ledger holds one in the 30 days before | Check SCHEMA_RULE fails for that proposal | None to a user | AC5 |
| X4 | The same event arrives twice | One run per case and event (R-UNI-40) | None to a user | AC7 |
| X5 | A proposed code has no owner row in R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 | Owner role stored as RW-TEAMMGR and the proposal marked "unmapped" | None to a user | AC4 |
| X6 | The agent times out | Run TIMED_OUT, counted, not retried | None to a user | AC9 |
| X7 | A role without the right | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-062-10 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the platform and client only; no S8 component is called, because nothing is raised in shadow |
| Negotiable | Codes, owner mapping, floor and the 30-day look-back are data values |
| Valuable | Gives the error rate per deviation type that decides the L1 segment in RWB-E2-029 |
| Estimable | Two event listeners, one prompt, one output schema, one scorer |
| Small | Two weeks for one developer and one analyst |
| Testable | Each criterion runs with synthetic cases, call notes and documents |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Deviation screening agent in shadow [E2b]

  Background:
    Given agent "SCREENING" has approved policy "P1" with mode "SHADOW", confidence floor 0.80 and prompt "PR1"
    Given rule rows R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 are in force

  Scenario: AC1 Shadow flags
    Given 200 cases with their call notes and documents
    When the agent runs
    Then each run stores its proposed codes with reasons and source references in mode "SHADOW"
    Then no deviation record exists, deviation_open stays false on every case and no contact stop is set
    Then no user-facing endpoint returns a proposal

  Scenario: AC2 Compared
    Given the business analysts' flags for the same 200 cases in sample "SCREEN-S1" version 1
    When the comparison runs
    Then one score row per code X1 to X7 holds precision, recall and sample size 200
    Then for X6 with 18 true positives, 2 false positives and 6 false negatives precision is 0.9000 and recall is 0.7500

  Scenario: AC3 A new document starts a run
    Given open case "RW-2026-000401" receives a document of type "DEATH_CERTIFICATE"
    When EV-16 DocumentStored is processed
    Then one shadow run exists with key "SCREENING:<caseId>:<eventId>" and trigger "DocumentStored"

  Scenario: AC4 The owner role comes from the rule rows
    Given the agent proposes X4 for case "RW-2026-000402"
    When the proposal is stored
    Then it holds owner role "RW-FRAUD" from rule R-DEV-04
    Then the system stores a proposed code with no owner row with owner role "RW-TEAMMGR" and marker "unmapped"

  Scenario: AC5 A complaint names the contact before it
    Given case "RW-2026-000403" has an outbound call on 2026-11-25 and a complaint note on 2026-11-27
    When the agent proposes X1
    Then the proposal names the interaction of 2026-11-25 as the preceding contact
    Then an X1 proposal without a preceding contact, when one exists in the 30 days before, fails check "SCHEMA_RULE"

  Scenario: AC6 A low-confidence proposal is marked for review
    Given the agent proposes X2 with confidence 0.72
    When the proposal is stored
    Then it holds marker "review"
    Then the evaluation counts it under "review" and not in precision or recall

  Scenario: AC7 A repeated event
    Given EV-16 for document "D-1001" on case "RW-2026-000401" was processed
    When the same event ID arrives again
    Then one run exists for the case and event and the repeat is counted (R-UNI-40)

  Scenario: AC8 A code outside the list
    Given the model stub returns code "X9"
    When the guardrail runs
    Then the run holds status "GUARDRAIL_FAILED", check "SCHEMA" and fallback true

  Scenario: AC9 Timeout
    Given the model stub does not answer for 61 seconds
    When the agent runs for case "RW-2026-000404"
    Then the run holds status "TIMED_OUT" and is not retried for that event
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | In SHADOW mode the screening agent raises nothing: no deviation record, no clock pause, no contact stop | agent_policy.autonomy_mode (New); R-DEV-01 is not fired |
| BR2 | A proposal carries a code from LOV-DEVIATION, reasons, source references and a confidence | LOV-DEVIATION; deviation.deviation_code |
| BR3 | The owner role of a code is read from R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06; a code with no row maps to the team manager and is marked unmapped | R-DEV-02, R-DEV-03, R-DEV-04, R-DEV-05, R-DEV-06; REQ-DVH-003 |
| BR4 | An X1 proposal names the latest interaction in the 30 days before the complaint (30, assumed; held in the policy) | REQ-DVH-007; interaction.occurred_at |
| BR5 | Proposals below the floor are marked review and scored separately | agent_policy.confidence_floor (New); FEAT-DVH-08 |
| BR6 | Precision and recall per code use proposals at or above the floor against Y and N labels | agent_evaluation (New) |
| BR7 | One run per case per triggering event | R-UNI-40 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status and raises no deviation. In shadow, the rule R-DEV-01 (ANY_STATE, DEVIATION_FLAGGED, to DEV_FLAGGED) is never fired. It writes agent runs and one evaluation run (RUNNING to DONE).

### 12. Contract

**Events consumed:** EV-01 CaseCreated and EV-16 DocumentStored (documentId, caseId, type, source); idempotent on event ID.

**Event published:** EV-28 AgentRunCompleted (runId, agent "SCREENING", caseId, outcome, fallback).

**Output schema "screening-v1":** proposals (array of {code in X1..X7, reasons (array of strings, masked), sourceRefs (interaction or document IDs), precedingContactId (X1 only), confidence}).

**Interfaces called:** P3 CaseQueryService.getCase, P7 InteractionLedgerReader.list(caseId, from, to), P5 DocumentQueryService.listByCase and getFields, P3 RuleEvaluator.ownerFor(routeSet "Deviations", event "OWNER_ASSIGNED", deviationCode); all as SY-AGENT or SY-RULES.

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-evaluations** and **GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-evaluations** (new, RWB-E1-058): agent "SCREENING", sample "SCREEN-S1"; Rules and parameters C and R; errors 401, 403, 409 (MSG-P10-003), 422 (MSG-P10-002), 503.

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-runs** (api.yaml): metadata only; Platform administration R.

**Configuration and reference data:** policy SCREENING P1 (floor 0.80, look-back 30 days, ledger window 180 days) loaded by RW-COE and approved by RW-RISK; LOV-DEVIATION and rule rows R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 maintained by the center of excellence.

## RWB-E1-063 Agent monitoring dashboard v1 [E2c]

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-063 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P10 Agent runtime |
| Feature | FEAT-AGT-06 Publish the agent monitoring dashboard |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-009 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.9; Business Requirements Program, section 5.7 |
| L3 process | 15 Manage performance, data and AI |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Should |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-061, RWB-E1-007, RWB-E1-014, RWB-E1-058 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **risk and model risk officer (RW-RISK)**, I want **a dashboard with runs, acceptance, override, fallback, latency, cost and evaluation score per agent and version, and an alert when an agent's daily cost passes its limit**, so that **every agent is watched from its first shadow run**.

### 2. Business rationale

An agent in shadow that times out on one case in five, or that spends twice its budget, must be seen in the first week, not at the L1 review. This story copies daily agent run figures to the data lake with the nightly reporting extract, matched by row count (REQ-DRI-009), so the Power BI dashboard reads the copy and not the live tables. A daily check sends an alert when the cost of an agent on a business date is above its policy limit.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-058 is done: agent_run and agent_policy exist with cost, latency and status per run.
- RWB-E1-014 is done: the nightly copy path to the data lake exists.
- RWB-E1-007 is done: outbound files and the exception queue use the integration adapters.
- JOB-15 Reporting extract runs nightly at 01:30.
- Each approved agent policy holds daily_cost_cap_thb (assumed 2,000 baht for INTAKE and SCREENING; DL33) and alert_role (assumed RW-COE).
- RW-BIANAL builds the Power BI report on the data lake table; RW-RISK and RW-COE hold Reporting R.

### 4. Flow

1. JOB-15 Reporting extract: at 01:30 calls the P10 step AgentRunExtractStep for the previous business date.
2. System: groups the agent runs of that date by agent, policy version, prompt version and model version: runs, answered, fallback, median and 95th percentile latency, tokens and cost.
3. System: adds the latest DONE evaluation score per agent and version.
4. System: writes the rows to the data lake table agent_run_daily and checks that the row count and the sum of runs match the source.
5. System: compares each agent's cost for the date with daily_cost_cap_thb of its policy; for each breach writes one agent alert and sends MSG-P10-004 through the P6 notification interface to the alert role and to RW-RISK.
6. RW-RISK: opens the Power BI report "Agent monitor v1" and reads each agent by version and date.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Row count or run sum in the data lake does not match the source | The publish is held; the previous day stays visible; the data steward and RW-PLATADM are alerted; JOB-15 reports failed for the step | None to a user | AC3 |
| X2 | JOB-15 runs again for the same business date | Rows for the date are replaced, not added; no second alert is sent | None to a user | AC4 |
| X3 | An agent has no runs on the date | One row with runs 0; no cost alert | None to a user | AC5 |
| X4 | Cost equals the cap exactly | No alert; an alert is sent only when cost is above the cap | None to a user | AC6 |
| X5 | The notification interface is unavailable | The alert row is kept with sent_at empty and retried by JOB-11 Outbox sender (R-UNI-33) | None to a user | AC7 |
| X6 | A role without Reporting R opens the report | The workspace refuses access | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-063-08 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads only P10 tables and writes through the existing copy path and notification interface |
| Negotiable | Caps, alert role and the measures shown are data; the Power BI layout is the analyst's choice |
| Valuable | Shows fallbacks and spend per agent from the first shadow run |
| Estimable | One extract step, one data lake table, one check, one Power BI page |
| Small | One developer and one BI analyst for one week |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on fixed runs for one business date |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Agent monitoring dashboard v1 [E2c]

  Background:
    Given agents "INTAKE" (policy "P1", prompt "PR1") and "SCREENING" (policy "P1", prompt "PR1") run in shadow
    Given on business date 2026-12-01 "INTAKE" has 120 runs, 9 with fallback, cost 1,840.0000 baht
    Given on 2026-12-01 "SCREENING" has 150 runs, 21 with fallback, cost 2,310.5000 baht
    Given both policies have daily_cost_cap_thb 2,000 and alert_role "RW-COE"

  Scenario: AC1 Per agent
    Given two agents in shadow
    When the dashboard opens for 2026-12-01
    Then each agent shows runs, fallback rate, median and 95th percentile latency, cost and the latest evaluation score by policy and prompt version
    Then "INTAKE" shows 120 runs and fallback rate 0.0750
    Then acceptance and override show "no L1 runs" for both agents, because no agent runs at L1 in Epic 1

  Scenario: AC2 Alert
    Given cost above the daily parameter for "SCREENING"
    When JOB-15 completes for 2026-12-01
    Then one agent alert row exists for "SCREENING", type "COST_CAP", date 2026-12-01, measured 2,310.5000 and threshold 2,000
    Then the system sends MSG-P10-004 to the holders of RW-COE and RW-RISK through the notification path
    Then no alert exists for "INTAKE"

  Scenario: AC3 A copy that does not match is held
    Given the data lake write for 2026-12-01 stores 1 row for 2 agent and version groups
    When the count check runs
    Then the system holds the publish for 2026-12-01 and the report shows 2026-11-30
    Then the step reports failed in GET /admin/jobs and the data steward is alerted

  Scenario: AC4 A rerun for the same date
    Given JOB-15 completed for 2026-12-01 and sent the "SCREENING" alert
    When RW-PLATADM reruns JOB-15 for 2026-12-01
    Then agent_run_daily holds the same 2 rows for 2026-12-01
    Then no second alert row or notification exists

  Scenario: AC5 An agent with no runs
    Given agent "EXTRACT" has an approved policy and no runs on 2026-12-01
    When JOB-15 completes for 2026-12-01
    Then "EXTRACT" shows runs 0 and cost 0.0000 for 2026-12-01 and no alert

  Scenario: AC6 Cost equal to the cap
    Given "INTAKE" cost is 2,000.0000 baht on 2026-12-02
    When JOB-15 completes for 2026-12-02
    Then no cost alert exists for "INTAKE" on 2026-12-02

  Scenario: AC7 The notification path is down
    Given the P6 notification interface is unavailable at 01:40
    When the "SCREENING" alert is raised
    Then the system keeps the alert row with sent_at empty
    Then the system sends it when the outbox sender succeeds (R-UNI-33, R-UNI-35)
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The dashboard reads the data lake copy, never the live tables | REQ-DRI-009; integration INT-20 pattern |
| BR2 | A copy is published only when its row count and run sum match the source | REQ-DRI-009; DL25 (zero tolerance) |
| BR3 | A cost alert is raised when the cost of an agent on a business date is above agent_policy.daily_cost_cap_thb (2,000 baht, assumed; DL33) | agent_policy.daily_cost_cap_thb (New) |
| BR4 | One alert per agent, type and business date | agent_alert unique key (New); R-UNI-40 |
| BR5 | Fallback rate = runs with fallback / runs, 4 decimals | agent_run.fallback (New) |
| BR6 | Alerts go to the policy alert role and to RW-RISK within 15 minutes of the end of the step (target, DL11) | agent_policy.alert_role (New); NFR-068 |

### 12. Contract

**Job:** JOB-15 Reporting extract (batch.txt), nightly 01:30 Asia/Bangkok. This story adds step "agentRunDaily" after the existing steps.
- Trigger: Quartz schedule of JOB-15; manual rerun through POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun.
- Input: agent_run rows with run_at on the business date; agent_policy in force; latest DONE agent_evaluation per agent and version.
- Output: data lake table agent_run_daily (business_date, agent_code, policy_version, prompt_version, model_version, runs, answered, fallback, latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, tokens, cost_thb, eval_score); agent_alert rows.
- Events published: none from events.txt; alerts go through the P6 notification interface and the outbox (JOB-11 Outbox sender).
- Idempotency key: business_date for the data lake rows (replace); agent_code, alert_type, segment and business_date for alerts.
- Restart: the step restarts from the start for the date; earlier rows for the date are deleted in the same transaction as the new write.

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs** and **POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun** (api.yaml, P1): show and rerun JOB-15; Platform administration R and U.

**Published interface used by JOB-15:**

```java
package recovery.agent.api;
public interface AgentRunExtractSource {
    List<AgentRunDailyRow> dailyRows(LocalDate businessDate);
    List<AgentAlert> raiseCostAlerts(LocalDate businessDate);
}
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `src/main/java/.../recovery/agent/monitor/`, Java package `recovery.agent.monitor`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AgentRunExtractSource | Published interface | Daily rows and cost alerts for JOB-15 |
| AgentMonitorService | Service | Aggregates runs; joins the latest evaluation score |
| AgentRunExtractStep | Job | Spring Batch step in JOB-15: write, count check, publish or hold |
| CostAlertService | Service | Compares cost with the cap; writes agent_alert; calls the P6 notification interface |
| AgentAlertRepository | Repository | agent_alert reads and writes |
| Agent monitor v1 | Power BI report | One page per agent with version filters, built by RW-BIANAL on agent_run_daily |

**Database:** migration `V10_006__agent_alert.sql` creates agent_alert with the standard record columns and unique (agent_code, alert_type, segment, business_date). Index agent_run (run_at).

**Configuration and reference data:** daily_cost_cap_thb and alert_role in agent_policy (RW-COE loads, RW-RISK approves). Notification template "agent cost alert" for MSG-P10-004 in the P6 template set.

**Build steps**
1. Write the agent_alert migration and entity.
2. Build AgentMonitorService aggregates on a fixture of 270 runs (AC1, AC5).
3. Build AgentRunExtractStep with the replace-by-date write and the count check (AC3, AC4).
4. Build CostAlertService with the strict greater-than rule and the unique key (AC2, AC6).
5. Send through the P6 interface with the outbox retry (AC7).
6. RW-BIANAL builds the Power BI page on agent_run_daily; check the figures against the fixture.

**Feature flag:** `rwb.agent.monitor`. Off: JOB-15 skips the step.

**Done when:** the tests in section 16 pass and the Power BI page shows the fixture figures for 2026-12-01.

## RWB-E1-064 Data dictionary for the 14 data products

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-064 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | None |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-001, REQ-RDF-011 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story), section 4 (REQ-RDF-001, REQ-RDF-011) and section 5 (data dictionary sources and owners) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010; DL43 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-043, RWB-E1-069 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)**, I want **all 122 objects and 1,366 fields of the 14 data products typed, sourced and owned, including the 30 ACE views and the four extension tables, with a data contract for the ACE read path that the ACE team confirms**, so that **every read has one published definition and a change to an ACE column reaches the dictionary through one governed load**.

### 2. Business rationale

The dictionary is the only place that says what a field is, where it comes from and who owns it. It now covers 122 objects and 1,366 fields: the 92 Workbench tables hold 1,062 fields, 49 of them on the four extension tables, and the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views hold 304 fields, 177 in Section A and 127 in Section B. The Workbench loads no source data (D-RCV-35 U1), so every source is either ACE, whose columns are recorded as `public.table.column` on the view fields where the view reads one column, or the Workbench itself.

V0001 creates `sys_objects`, `sys_fields`, `sys_field_version`, `data_product` and `data_contract` and seeds the 122 objects and 1,366 fields. This story does not create a table or a column. It publishes the governance attributes on every field, records the change history, and takes the ACE team's confirmation of the read contract before it is published. A new ACE column is added to the dictionary by a reference load through RWB-E1-043, never by editing an applied migration; the view conformance test of RWB-E1-069 blocks the merge until the row exists. Serves REQ-RDF-001 (one system of record and one owner per product) and REQ-RDF-011 (catalog entry content). The measure is that 100 percent of the 1,366 fields return a source, an owner, a refresh cycle and a late behavior.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-001 is done: V0001 created the 92 tables, the 30 view objects in the dictionary, the 122 `sys_objects` rows, the 1,366 `sys_fields` rows, `sys_field_version`, `data_product` and `data_contract`.
- RWB-E1-069 is done: the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views exist and the view conformance test CHK-01 compares every view column with `sys_fields`.
- The reference data service (RWB-E1-043) accepts a load for table code `sys_fields` and hands approved rows to P1.
- The data steward holds RW-DATASTEW (Reference data U); the reference data administrator holds RW-REFADM (Reference data C).
- The ACE team lead is named as the confirming role for the ACE read contract; the confirmation is stored outside the Workbench as a document reference.
- `v_data_dictionary` returns the 122 objects and 1,366 fields of V0001.

### 4. Flow

1. Data steward: prepares the governance load for all 1,366 fields with owner role, refresh cycle, late behavior and interface, and checks the source system and source field of each view field against the view definition.
2. Reference data administrator: loads the file through POST /admin/reference-loads with table `sys_fields` and valid from 2026-11-30.
3. DataDictionaryLoader: refuses the whole load if any field is unknown, if a view field's source system is not "ACE", if a Workbench field's source system is not "Workbench", if a view field's source field is not a column of that view and is not one of the 7 derived fields, or if any of the required attributes is empty; otherwise writes the attributes and version 1 of each field to `sys_field_version`.
4. Data steward: records the ACE team lead's confirmation of contract DC-ACE, which lists the 304 ACE fields and the read interfaces V0002 and V0003, with the confirming role, the date and the stored document reference.
5. Data steward: publishes DC-ACE with POST /admin/data-contracts/{contractId}/publish; the service refuses a contract without a confirmation.
6. DataContractService: sets the contract PUBLISHED. The published version stays in force until a later version is confirmed and published.
7. Developer or analyst: calls GET /admin/data-dictionary/fields and reads a field's type, source system, source field, refresh, owner and behavior when late.
8. Data steward: changes a field definition with PATCH /admin/data-dictionary/fields/{fieldId}, a reason and an If-Match version; the service writes a new `sys_field_version` row with its date and reason.
9. DataContractService: when a changed field belongs to the published DC-ACE, opens a new DRAFT contract version; the published version stays in force.
10. ACE team and recovery developer: a new ACE column is added to a view by a Flyway migration and to the dictionary by a load through RWB-E1-043; no applied migration is edited, and CHK-01 passes only when both exist.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Publish of a contract without the ACE team's confirmation | 409; contract stays DRAFT | MSG-P1-021 | AC6 |
| X2 | A field change without a reason | 422; no version written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |
| X3 | A dictionary load with an unknown field, a missing attribute, a source system outside ACE and Workbench, or an ACE source field that is not a column of the view and not one of the 7 derived fields | Load refused in full; the dictionary in force stays | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X4 | Two stewards change the same field from the same version | The second change is refused with 409 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC7 |
| X5 | A field of a published contract changes | A new DRAFT contract version; the published version stays in force | None | AC8 |
| X6 | A view column exists with no `sys_fields` row | CHK-01 fails and the merge is blocked | v_ace_account.legacy_bucket has no data dictionary entry | AC4 |
| X7 | A field definition is changed with no If-Match version | 428; no version written | MSG-GEN-004 | AC7 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the tables and seed of RWB-E1-001, the reference load of RWB-E1-043 and the views and conformance test of RWB-E1-069; it publishes the definition every later read uses |
| Negotiable | Owners, refresh cycles, late behavior and contract content are data values; the story fixes the completeness, source and version rules |
| Valuable | Every read has one published definition, and a source change is governed in one place |
| Estimable | No DDL, five endpoints, two services, one loader |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is one API test against the seeded metadata tables |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every field carries its data type, physical type, source system, owner role, refresh cycle and behavior when late, and every view field names its ACE column as `public.table.column`, or, for the 7 derived view fields, states that the view derives it | REQ-RDF-001; sys_fields |
| BR2 | The dictionary holds 122 objects and 1,366 fields: 92 tables with 1,062 fields, 49 of them on the four extension tables, and 30 views with 304 fields, 177 in Section A and 127 in Section B | D-RCV-35; Data Tier Map v1 section 8 |
| BR3 | Each data product has exactly one system of record and one owner role; a source is either an ACE column recorded on a view field or the Workbench itself | REQ-RDF-001; data_product; D-RCV-35 U1 |
| BR4 | A data contract is published only after its confirming role is recorded with a date and a stored document reference | DL12; data_contract |
| BR5 | A field change creates a new `sys_field_version` row with a date and a reason; earlier versions stay readable | Reference data change process; DT02; Principle 1 |
| BR6 | A dictionary load with an exception is refused in full; an ACE source field that is not a column of the view is an exception unless the view derives it | Reference data change process, step 3; CTL-08 |
| BR7 | A change to a field of a published contract opens a new contract version; the published version stays in force until the new one is confirmed and published | R-UNI-38 |
| BR8 | V0001 owns `sys_objects`, `sys_fields`, `sys_field_version`, `data_product` and `data_contract`; this story adds no table, column, index or constraint and publishes rows only through RWB-E1-043 and the endpoints | RWB-E1-001; D-RCV-28 |
| BR9 | A new ACE column reaches the dictionary as a reference load after its view column exists; an applied migration is never edited, and CHK-01 blocks the merge until the row exists | RWB-E1-069; BR-P1-001 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the data contract status: DRAFT to PUBLISHED after the confirming role is recorded, and a new DRAFT version when a field of a published contract changes. Each field change adds a version; earlier versions stay readable.

### 12. Contract

**Endpoints**

| Method and path | Request | Response | Errors | Authorization | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET /admin/data-dictionary/fields | Query: product, entity, field, sourceSystem, page, size | DataDictionaryFieldPage: items of DataDictionaryField (fieldId, entity, fieldName, dataType, physicalType, mandatory, listCode, sourceSystem, sourceField, refreshCycle, ownerRole, lateBehavior, interfaceId, isPersonal, version, versionDate) and the object and field counts | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 (MSG-P4-002); 503 (MSG-GEN-006) | Reference data, R | Not applicable |
| PATCH /admin/data-dictionary/fields/{fieldCode} | Header If-Match: version; body DataDictionaryFieldChange (changed attributes, reason) | DataDictionaryField | 403; 404 unknown field (MSG-P4-003); 409 stale version (MSG-GEN-004); 422 reason empty (MSG-GEN-001); 428 no If-Match (MSG-GEN-004) | Reference data, U | If-Match version |
| GET /admin/data-contracts | Query: sourceSystem, status | DataContract[] (id, contractCode, sourceSystem, interfaceId, contractVersion, status, fieldCount, confirmedByRole, confirmedOn, confirmationDocumentRef, publishedAt) | 401; 403; 503 | Reference data, R | Not applicable |
| PATCH /admin/data-contracts/{contractId} | Header If-Match; body DataContractConfirmation (confirmedByRole, confirmedOn, confirmationDocumentRef) | DataContract | 403; 404; 409 (MSG-GEN-004); 422 field empty (MSG-GEN-001) | Reference data, U | If-Match version |
| POST /admin/data-contracts/{contractId}/publish | Header Idempotency-Key | DataContract | 403; 404; 409 no confirmation (MSG-P1-021) | Reference data, U | Idempotency-Key header |

The dictionary load uses POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads with table `sys_fields` (Reference data, C), approved through POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve (Reference data, A).

**Published interface (P1, called by the reference data service and by RWB-E1-016)**

```java
package recovery.dataengine.dictionary.api;

public interface DataDictionaryLoader {
    LoadResult apply(String loadVersion, LocalDate validFrom, List<DictionaryFieldRow> rows);
}

public interface DataDictionaryQuery {
    Optional<DataDictionaryField> field(String fieldId);
    List<DataDictionaryField> fieldsOf(String objectName);
    DataProductDefinition product(String productCode);
    DictionaryCounts counts(); // 122 objects, 1,366 fields, 304 view fields, 49 extension fields
}
```

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `recovery/dataengine/dictionary`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.dictionary`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DataDictionaryController | Controller | The five endpoints in section 12 |
| DataDictionaryService | Service | Field reads, versioned changes with reason, optimistic lock, object and field counts |
| DataContractService | Service | The ACE read contract; confirmation; publish rule; new version on change |
| DataDictionaryLoader | Published interface | Whole-load validation and apply; source and view column checks |
| DataDictionaryQuery | Published interface | Field and product definitions for other packages and modules |
| SysFieldRepository, SysFieldVersionRepository, DataContractRepository, DataProductRepository | Repository | Read and write the five tables |
| SysField, SysFieldVersion, DataContract, DataProduct | Entity | One per table |

- Database: no DDL. V0001 created `sys_objects`, `sys_fields`, `sys_field_version`, `data_product` and `data_contract` with the 122 and 1,366 seed rows. This story writes only rows, through the reference load and the endpoints.
- Configuration and reference data: the governance load prepared by the data steward from `v_data_dictionary` and the 30 view definitions; data_product owners confirmed by each product owner (BRD Epic 1 section 5); expected_by times assumed 08:00 for daily ACE products and Monday 08:00 for weekly ACE products (DL11).
- Build steps:
  1. Read the 122 objects and 1,366 fields from `v_data_dictionary`; confirm the counts and the 30 view rows. No migration.
  2. DataDictionaryLoader with whole-load validation of the six attributes, the source system and the view column; refusal with MSG-P1-002 and the first failing check.
  3. DataDictionaryService change with If-Match and a mandatory reason; one `sys_field_version` row per change.
  4. DataContractService: DC-ACE from the 304 ACE fields; confirmation record; publish rule with MSG-P1-021; new DRAFT on a field change.
  5. DataDictionaryController and the contract tests for the endpoints (RWB-TE-003).
  6. Prepare and load the governance file through RWB-E1-043; confirm the ACE team's confirmation and publish DC-ACE.
  7. Tests for AC1 to AC8 and the access test.
- Feature flag: `rwb.dataengine.data-dictionary`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass, all 30 views have dictionary rows in SIT, and DC-ACE is PUBLISHED.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-021 | Publish of a contract with no confirmation | The data contract for {system} cannot be published until its confirming role records the confirmation. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Reason or confirmation field empty | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Change from an old version, or no If-Match version | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P1-002 | Dictionary load refused at a check | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The store or a view is unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without Reference data U | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. Developers and analysts read the dictionary through GET /admin/data-dictionary/fields; SCR-40 Reference data shows versioned tables from Epic 8, and until then changes go by file load or the endpoints.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: owners, cycles, late behavior and contract content are data rows.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts: the dictionary holds definitions, not values; the confirmation names a role, not a person.
- No read of another module's tables: other modules use DataDictionaryQuery. The only public schema names in the story are the ACE column names recorded in the dictionary, which no recovery class reads directly.
- A published contract is never edited in place; a change makes a new version.
- No DDL: V0001 owns the five tables; this story never adds or alters a column.

| REQ-RDF-011 | Catalog entry per data product with definition, owner, system of record and refresh | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.1 and 4 | None | All recovery processes | R-UNI-38 | TC-E1-064-04, TC-E1-064-05, TC-E1-064-07, TC-E1-064-08 |

| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010; DL43 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-069 |
| Status | Ready for build, Section B views behind the RWB-ACE-001 DDL (DL43) |

### 1. Story

As a **Tribe lead and squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a sandbox database that stands up the ACE schema and the recovery schema from the same DDL as SIT, with synthetic ACE-shaped source rows and synthetic Workbench rows**, so that **I can build and test every view read before the ACE interfaces are available and without production data**.

### 2. Business rationale

SIT reads the real ACE database; DEV has none. Without a local ACE schema the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views cannot compile, so no squad can test a source read, the case list, a notice or a report before SIT is connected. The sandbox applies the ACE schema for the 22 Tier 1 tables, the RWB-ACE-001 DDL for the 14 Tier 2 tables, Physical Schema v6 for the 92 recovery tables and the four extension tables, and V0002 and V0003 for the 30 views. It fills the source tables with synthetic rows and the Workbench tables with synthetic cases across Mortgage, Hire Purchase and SSME, and the exception shapes the rules must handle.

There is no copy and no load table: `loan_account`, `account_payment`, `party`, `contact_point`, `collateral`, `account_collateral`, `collections_history`, `party_product`, `valuation`, `score`, `asset`, `load_run`, `dq_exception`, `dq_rule`, `source_field_map`, `source_code_map`, `interface_run`, `interface_signoff`, `tracker_inventory` and `tracker_row` do not exist. The generator reads the data dictionary, so a schema change reaches the sandbox with no manual rebuild, and the verifier allows a clear identity number only in the ACE-shaped tables, where ACE itself holds it; the recovery schema sees `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` only. Serves REQ-RDF-001 (the 14 data products in one schema) and REQ-RDF-010 (no personal data outside its permitted use).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-001 is done: V0001 creates the 92 tables, `data_product`, the 122 `sys_objects` rows, the 1,366 `sys_fields` rows and the four extension tables.
- RWB-E1-069 is done: V0002 and V0003 create the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views and their grants, and CHK-01 compares them with the dictionary.
- The ACE schema DDL `15 ACE DB Alignment/ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql` is in the repository. It holds the 22 Tier 1 tables, among them `account`, `payment`, `customer`, `efs_action` and `iam_user`.
- The RWB-ACE-001 DDL for the 14 Tier 2 tables is available in DEV (DL43); until it lands, the 14 Section B views and the features that read them stay behind their flags.
- A PostgreSQL 17 database `rwb_sandbox` exists in DEV, reachable from the pipeline.
- The Entra ID group RWB-DEV-RW-TRIBE exists and maps to the sandbox read-only database role.
- The role to permission matrix rows (roles.txt, Permissions) are available as a seed file for the sandbox.
- The ACE service can be deployed in DEV against the sandbox database.

### 4. Flow

1. Pipeline: on a merge to main that changes the ACE schema DDL, a recovery Flyway migration or the dictionary, or on a manual start, runs the sandbox build stage in DEV.
2. Pipeline: creates database `rwb_sandbox_next` and two empty schemas, `public` and `recovery`.
3. Pipeline: applies `ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql` (22 Tier 1 tables), then the RWB-ACE-001 DDL (14 Tier 2 tables), then V0001 (92 tables and the dictionary), V0002 (16 Section A views) and V0003 (14 Section B views).
4. SandboxGenerator: reads `sys_objects`, `sys_fields` and `lov_value` to learn every table, column, type and list.
5. SandboxGenerator: seeds the 22 Tier 1 tables and the 14 Tier 2 tables with synthetic rows, including one `ace_batch_run` row per source and business date.
6. SandboxGenerator: creates synthetic cases with seed 20261128: 1,226 Mortgage, 1,296 Hire purchase and 290 SSME (10 percent of the 30 June 2026 inventory; DL15), with their accounts, parties, contact points, collateral, valuations, payments and interactions, linked by business key to the ACE-shaped rows.
7. SandboxGenerator: adds 10 cases for each exception shape in section 8, BR4.
8. SandboxGenerator: loads the 54 roles, the permission matrix and one named test user per role.
9. SandboxVerifier: checks that the 30 views compile and each returns a row, that every seeded table has rows, that every LOV column holds list values, that every foreign key resolves, that no clear personal value sits in schema `recovery`, and that the boundary accounts exist.
10. Pipeline: renames `rwb_sandbox_next` to `rwb_sandbox`, grants SELECT on schema `recovery` to role `rwb_sandbox_read`, and publishes the build result with the row count per table.
11. Developer or analyst: queries the sandbox with SQL or the export script, or calls the DEV service, without a request to another team.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A table column has no `sys_fields` row | Build fails naming the table and column; previous sandbox kept | None (pipeline result) | AC4 |
| X2 | The reset runs twice for the same commit and seed | The schemas are dropped and recreated; the same seed gives the same rows and counts | None | AC5 |
| X3 | A generated value breaks a constraint | Build fails naming the table and constraint; previous sandbox kept | None (pipeline result) | AC6 |
| X4 | A generated value in schema recovery matches a personal data pattern | Build fails naming the table and column | None (pipeline result) | AC7 |
| X5 | Accounts sit at the 90 days past due boundary | Accounts at 89 and at 90 days past due are both generated | None | AC8 |
| X6 | A second build starts while one runs | The second build waits on the pipeline lock and runs after the first | None | AC9 |
| X7 | The RWB-ACE-001 DDL is not yet in DEV | The build stops before V0003; the 16 Section A views and the Workbench tables are still built and published | None (pipeline result) | AC1 |

| Independent | Needs the DDL from RWB-E1-001 and RWB-E1-069 and, for Section B, the Tier 2 DDL of RWB-ACE-001; it publishes the environment every squad tests in |
| Negotiable | Volumes, seed and exception shapes are properties; the story fixes the generator, the checks and the access |
| Valuable | Every squad builds and tests every view read from the first day with no production data |
| Estimable | One generator tool, one verifier, one pipeline stage, one database role |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is a pipeline test or a query against the built sandbox |

```gherkin

    Then case "RW-2026-000001" has its accounts, parties, interactions and documents linked
    Then none of the 20 tables that left the schema exists in schema recovery: loan_account, account_payment, party, contact_point, collateral, account_collateral, collections_history, party_product, valuation, score, asset, load_run, dq_exception, dq_rule, source_field_map, source_code_map, interface_run, interface_signoff, tracker_inventory and tracker_row

  Scenario: AC2 It is readable and extractable

    Then the result shows MORTGAGE, HIRE_PURCHASE and SSME with their counts
    Then the export script writes recovery_case to a CSV file without a request to another team
    Then the system refuses an UPDATE by the same database role

  Scenario: AC3 It scales with the schema
    Given a test migration, never shipped, adds column "risk_tier varchar(10)" to recovery_case with its sys_fields row and list LOV-RISK-TIER
    When it is applied
    Then the sandbox rebuild fills risk_tier with values from LOV-RISK-TIER on every case

  Scenario: AC4 A column with no dictionary entry
    Given a dictionary fixture in which the sys_fields row for recovery_case.closure_reason is removed
    When the sandbox build runs

  Scenario: AC5 The reset is idempotent
    Given the sandbox was built for commit "a1b2c3d" with seed 20261128
    When the build runs again for commit "a1b2c3d" and seed 20261128
    Then a fresh schema public and a fresh schema recovery are built in rwb_sandbox_next and swapped in
    Then every seeded table holds the same row count
    Then case "RW-2026-000001" holds the same total_outstanding_at_entry of 1,845,200.00
    Then no row from the first build remains

  Scenario: AC6 A generated value breaks a constraint
    Given list LOV-PRODUCT is empty in the seed data
    When the sandbox build runs
    Then the build fails naming table "recovery_case" and column "product_group"
    Then the previous sandbox stays in use

  Scenario: AC7 No clear personal value outside the ACE tables
    Given the verifier scans every column of schema recovery tagged is_personal
    When a generated value in recovery.document_field.extracted_value matches the 13-digit national ID pattern with a valid check digit
    Then the build fails naming recovery.document_field.extracted_value
    Then a clear identity number in public.customer is not a failure, because ACE holds it and v_ace_customer exposes id_no_masked and id_no_last4 only
    Then the system publishes no sandbox from that build

  Scenario: AC8 Accounts at the entry boundary
    Given the exception shapes include the entry boundary
    When the sandbox is provisioned
    Then 10 accounts in v_ace_account have days_past_due 89 and no case
    Then 10 accounts in v_ace_account have days_past_due 90 and one open case each

  Scenario: AC9 Two builds at once
    Given a sandbox build is running for commit "a1b2c3d"
    When a second build starts for commit "e4f5a6b"
    Then the second build waits until the first ends
    Then the sandbox after both holds the data for commit "e4f5a6b"
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | No production data in DEV; the sandbox holds synthetic data only | NFR-045; CTL-11 |
| BR2 | The sandbox is built from the same DDL as SIT: the ACE schema for the 22 Tier 1 tables, the RWB-ACE-001 DDL for the 14 Tier 2 tables, and V0001 to V0003 for the 92 recovery tables and the 30 views | RWB-E1-001; RWB-E1-069; ADR-001 |
| BR3 | Generated values come from the data dictionary and the lists of values, not from code | sys_fields; lov_value; Principle 1 |
| BR4 | Exception shapes generated: duplicate case for one customer and product (R-UNI-17), deceased customer (R-UNI-05), bankruptcy (R-UNI-07), open deviation, legal hold (R-UNI-20), unmapped product code, collateral with no account, case with three accounts, accounts at 89 and 90 days past due (DL16), withdrawn consent (R-UNI-10) | rules.txt; DL16 |
| BR5 | Case volumes follow the product split of the 30 June 2026 inventory at 10 percent | DL15 |
| BR6 | Every role has a named test user before it has real users | DL39 |
| BR7 | The ACE-shaped tables (22 Tier 1 and 14 Tier 2) are a DEV test double for ACE, not a copy of source data: they hold synthetic rows only, they are never deployed to SIT, UAT or production, and no recovery table is loaded from them by a batch job | D-RCV-35 U1; NFR-045 |
| BR8 | No copy and no load table exists in the sandbox; the 20 tables that left the schema are absent, and the Workbench reads source data only through `recovery.v_ace_*` | D-RCV-35; ADR-010 |
| BR9 | A clear identity number is allowed only in the ACE-shaped tables; schema recovery holds masked or synthetic values only | D-RCV-35 U4; CTL-11 |

### 12. Contract

**Pipeline stage**

| Item | Value |

| Trigger | Merge to main that changes the ACE schema DDL, a file under the recovery Flyway migration folder or the dictionary; manual start by RW-TRIBE or RW-PLATADM |

| Schedule | On trigger only |
| Input | `ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql`; the RWB-ACE-001 Tier 2 DDL; V0001, V0002 and V0003; `sys_objects`, `sys_fields` and `lov_value` after migration; the role and permission seed file; properties in section 13 |
| Output | Database `rwb_sandbox` with schema `public` (the ACE schema, including the 22 Tier 1 and 14 Tier 2 tables) and schema `recovery` (92 tables and 30 views) holding synthetic rows; build report with row count per table and the verifier result |
| Events published | None |
| Idempotency key | Commit hash and seed. The same pair produces the same rows |
| Restart behavior | The build works on `rwb_sandbox_next` and renames it to `rwb_sandbox` only after the verifier passes; a failed build leaves the previous sandbox |

| Method and path | Use | Authorization | Errors |

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `tools/sandbox-generator`, Java package `recovery.tools.sandbox`, built as a separate build module that is not packaged into the ACE service.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AceSchemaLoader | Service | Applies the 22 Tier 1 tables, the 14 Tier 2 tables, V0001, V0002 and V0003 to `rwb_sandbox_next` |
| SandboxGenerator | Service | Reads the metadata and writes synthetic rows table by table in foreign key order, in schema public first and then schema recovery |
| ValueFactory | Service | Produces a value per data type and list, seeded; synthetic names as "SYN-FIRST-000123"; tokens as random 64-character hex |
| ExceptionShapeBuilder | Service | Adds the shapes in BR4, 10 cases each |
| SandboxVerifier | Service | View compile and row checks, list, key, personal data pattern and boundary checks |
| AccessSeedLoader | Service | Loads 54 roles, the permission matrix and one test user per role |
| SandboxExport | Service | Writes a table to CSV for the read-only role |
| Sandbox build stage | Job | Pipeline stage: create database, apply the ACE schema, the Tier 2 DDL and V0001 to V0003, generate, verify, rename, grant |

- Database: no new recovery table. The stage creates `rwb_sandbox_next`, applies the ACE schema and the recovery migrations, fills both schemas, verifies, then renames the database to `rwb_sandbox` from the maintenance connection and grants SELECT to role `rwb_sandbox_read` mapped to RWB-DEV-RW-TRIBE. The pipeline holds a PostgreSQL advisory lock for the whole build.
- Configuration and reference data: properties `rwb.sandbox.seed=20261128`, `rwb.sandbox.cases.mortgage=1226`, `rwb.sandbox.cases.hire-purchase=1296`, `rwb.sandbox.cases.ssme=290`, `rwb.sandbox.shape-count=10`, `rwb.sandbox.ace-schema=15 ACE DB Alignment/ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql`, owned by the tech lead; lists of values from the seed migration; roles and permissions from the roles.txt seed file.
- Build steps:
  1. AceSchemaLoader for the 22 Tier 1 tables and the 14 Tier 2 tables; stop before V0003 when the Tier 2 DDL is absent.
  2. Metadata reader over `sys_objects`, `sys_fields` and `lov_value` with foreign key order from the relationships.
  3. ValueFactory per data type and list, seeded; a column with no `sys_fields` row fails the build.
  4. SandboxGenerator for the 22 Tier 1 and 14 Tier 2 tables, then the case volumes with linked accounts, parties, contact points, collateral, valuations, payments and interactions.
  5. ExceptionShapeBuilder for the shapes in BR4.
  6. AccessSeedLoader with a test user per role.
  7. SandboxVerifier: 30 views compile and return rows, rows per table, list values, foreign keys, personal data patterns in schema recovery (national ID with check digit, mobile number, email), and the 89 and 90 days past due boundary.
  8. Pipeline stage with `rwb_sandbox_next`, the rename, the grant and the lock.
  9. Tests for AC1 to AC9 and the access test in the pipeline.
- Feature flag: `rwb.dataengine.sandbox` (enables the DEV profile that points the service at `rwb_sandbox`).
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass and squads use the sandbox in DEV.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: volumes, seed and shape counts are properties; values come from the dictionary and the lists.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts: every name, identifier and contact value is synthetic, and the verifier blocks a value that looks real in schema recovery.
- No read of another module's tables at runtime: the generator is a build tool outside the ACE service and is never deployed to SIT, UAT or production.
- The sandbox is in DEV only; no copy goes to another environment. The ACE-shaped tables are a test double, not a data copy.
- No copy and no load table is created: the Workbench reads source data only through `recovery.v_ace_*`.

## RWB-E1-066 Interaction ledger store and writer

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-066 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-ILG-01 Write every Workbench event to the ledger; FEAT-ILG-02 Hold the ledger beside the decision log; FEAT-ILG-05 Raise an incident when the ledger cannot be written |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-ILG-001, REQ-ILG-002, REQ-ILG-004, REQ-ILG-008 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story) and section 4 (REQ-ILG-001, REQ-ILG-002, REQ-ILG-004, REQ-ILG-008) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-027 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **every contact, letter, promise, payment and hand-over on the case written to one ledger when it is recorded**, so that **the history of the case is never assembled after the fact**.

### 2. Business rationale

Today the history of a recovery case is spread across EFS, LIT, letters and team spreadsheets, and an officer rebuilds it by hand before each decision. One append-only ledger per case, written in the same transaction as the action it records, gives one ordered history with no gap. The ledger records what happened with the customer; the decision log records why the system acted; each ledger entry for a decision points to its decision log entry. A ledger write that fails stops the action and raises an incident, so the history never has a silent gap. Serves REQ-ILG-001, REQ-ILG-002, REQ-ILG-004 and REQ-ILG-008; NFR-070 and NFR-077.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-018 is done: recovery_case exists with case numbers RW-YYYY-NNNNNN.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer and its incident path (incident record and operations alert) exist.
- The interaction table from RWB-E1-001 exists with its append-only trigger tr_interaction_append_only.
- The list LOV-LEDGER-EVENT is loaded by the reference data administrator (values in section 13).
- The caller of the writer holds Case record C: a person through POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions, or a service identity (SY-CASEWF, SY-DATALOAD).

### 4. Flow

1. Case owner: records a call with POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions (channel CALL, direction OUTBOUND, result RIGHT_PARTY, summary, promise amount and date).
2. P3 interactions handler: checks Case record C and the case scope, opens a transaction and calls InteractionLedgerWriter.append().
3. InteractionLedgerWriter: validates the command (case, event code in LOV-LEDGER-EVENT, occurred time, actor, source, idempotency key).
4. InteractionLedgerWriter: takes a transaction-level advisory lock on the case ID and assigns case_seq as the case's highest case_seq plus 1.
5. InteractionLedgerWriter: inserts the entry with event code, actor type and reference, source system and source reference, channel and direction where they apply, and the decision log entry ID for a decision.
6. P3 handler: commits the action and the entry in one transaction and returns 201 with the Interaction.
7. Other recording paths (EFS history load, ALS payment load, notice dispatch): call append() in their own transactions with source system EFS or WORKBENCH.
8. On a write failure: the transaction rolls back, the caller receives MSG-P1-022, and the writer raises an incident with incident code LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED, the case ID and the cause.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The ledger cannot be written | Action and entry roll back; 503 to the caller; incident raised; nothing discarded silently | MSG-P1-022 | AC4 |
| X2 | A required value is missing (event code, occurred time, actor) | 422; nothing written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |
| X3 | Two entries for one case at the same moment | Both written with consecutive case_seq; no gap and no repeat | None | AC6 |
| X4 | The case does not exist or is out of scope | 404; nothing written | MSG-P4-003 | AC7 |
| X5 | Any change or delete of an entry | Refused by the append-only trigger; a correction is a new entry naming the original | None | AC8 |

| Valuable | The case history exists as it happens and is never rebuilt by hand |

| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is a writer or API test on synthetic cases |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One ledger holds every interaction on a case; no other record is the authoritative history | REQ-ILG-001; case file item "Interaction ledger" (casemodel.txt) |
| BR2 | Every entry carries case, event, time, actor and source | REQ-ILG-002 |
| BR3 | An offer, promise, payment or hand-over is recorded on the interaction it was made in | REQ-ILG-004; interaction.promise_amount |
| BR4 | Entries are append only; a correction is a new entry naming the original | tr_interaction_append_only (Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql); R-UNI-24 |
| BR5 | A ledger write that fails stops the action and raises an incident; no entry is discarded | REQ-ILG-008; CTL-06 |
| BR6 | The ledger records what happened; the decision log records why; a decision entry links the two | FEAT-ILG-02; ADR-009 |
| BR7 | Entries of one case carry a gap-free sequence | REQ-ILG-001; interaction.case_seq |
