### 12. Contract

**Endpoint used (P3, API-P3-015)**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Method and path | POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions |
| Request | InteractionRequest: channel, direction, result, summary |
| Response | 201 Interaction: id, caseId, partyId, occurredAt, channel, direction, actionCode, contactResult, promiseAmount, promiseDate, summary, conductCheck, sourceSystem |
| Errors | 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Case record C (MSG-P4-002); 404 case missing or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 422 field invalid (MSG-GEN-001); 503 ledger write failed (MSG-P1-022) |
| Authorization | Case record, C, scope applied |
| Idempotency | The handler builds the idempotency key from the request ID header; a repeat returns the first entry (RWB-E1-067) |

**Published interface (P1)**

```java
package recovery.dataengine.ledger.api;

public interface InteractionLedgerWriter {
    /** Must run inside the caller's transaction (Propagation.MANDATORY). */
    LedgerEntryRef append(LedgerEntryCommand command);
}

public record LedgerEntryCommand(UUID caseId, UUID partyId, String eventCode,
        OffsetDateTime occurredAt, ActorType actorType, String actorRef,
        String sourceSystem, String sourceRef, String channel, String direction,
        String actionCode, String contactResult, BigDecimal promiseAmount,
        LocalDate promiseDate, String summary, UUID decisionLogEntryId,
        UUID correctsEntryId, String idempotencyKey) {}

public record LedgerEntryRef(UUID entryId, long caseSeq) {}
```

**Incident path (RWB-E1-027)**: `IncidentRecorder.raise(String incidentCode, UUID caseId, String detail)` with incident code LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED; detail holds the error class and no personal data.

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `recovery/dataengine/ledger`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.ledger`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| InteractionLedgerWriter | Published interface | append() for every recording path |
| LedgerWriteService | Service | Validation, advisory lock, case_seq, insert, incident on failure |
| InteractionRepository | Repository | Inserts and reads interaction rows; no update or delete method |
| Interaction | Entity | Immutable mapping of the interaction table |
| InteractionsHandler (P3, API-P3-015) | Controller | Existing P3 endpoint; delegates the write to InteractionLedgerWriter |

- Database: Flyway migration in this story adds to interaction the columns event_code varchar(40) not null, actor_type varchar(10) not null, actor_ref varchar(64) not null, source_ref varchar(60) not null, idempotency_key varchar(120), case_seq bigint not null, decision_log_id uuid, corrects_entry_id uuid; drops NOT NULL on channel and direction (Workbench events such as CASE_CREATED have no channel); adds unique (case_id, case_seq) and unique (idempotency_key). The append-only trigger stays. Index ix_interaction_case_time (case_id, occurred_at) from Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql serves the read.
- Configuration and reference data: list LOV-LEDGER-EVENT with values CONTACT, LETTER, PROMISE, PAYMENT, HANDOVER, CASE_CREATED, CASE_ALLOCATED, CASE_TRANSFERRED, CASE_ESCALATED, DOCUMENT_ATTACHED, DECISION_TAKEN, CORRECTION, loaded by the reference data administrator; Thai labels per DL10.
- Build steps:
  1. Flyway migration for the new columns, the nullable channel and direction, and the two unique keys.
  2. LedgerWriteService validation against LOV-LEDGER-EVENT and the required fields; MSG-GEN-001 on a missing value.
  3. Case sequence with pg_advisory_xact_lock on the case ID and max(case_seq) plus 1; retry once on a unique key clash.
  4. Insert with Propagation.MANDATORY so the entry commits with the action.
  5. Failure handling: translate the database error to LedgerWriteException, raise LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED, return MSG-P1-022 with 503 at the API.
  6. P3 InteractionsHandler delegation for POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions.
  7. Architecture test: no class outside `recovery.dataengine.ledger` uses InteractionRepository.
  8. Tests for AC1 to AC8 and the access test.
- Feature flag: `rwb.dataengine.ledger-writer`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass and the ACE collections history read through `v_ace_efs_action` writes through append().

## RWB-E1-067 Every Workbench action into the interaction ledger

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-067 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-ILG-01 Write every Workbench event to the ledger; FEAT-ILG-04 Reject a duplicate ledger entry |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-ILG-005, REQ-ILG-002, REQ-ILG-007 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story) and section 4 (REQ-ILG-002, REQ-ILG-005, REQ-ILG-007) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-066 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **every action the Workbench takes on my case written to the ledger when it is taken**, so that **I can read the history without assembling it from four systems**.

### 2. Business rationale

The Workbench creates, allocates, transfers and escalates cases, attaches documents and records decisions by rule, often with no person involved. If these actions are not in the ledger, the case owner sees the customer contacts but not what the Workbench did between them. Each action already publishes an application event to the outbox in the same transaction as the change (events.txt); a ledger listener turns each event into one entry with its source and actor. Events are delivered at least once, so the listener rejects a repeat by its idempotency key and counts it. Serves REQ-ILG-005, REQ-ILG-002 and REQ-ILG-007.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-066 is done: InteractionLedgerWriter, the case sequence and LOV-LEDGER-EVENT exist.
- RWB-TE-006 is done: the outbox delivers events at least once, per case in written order, with event ID, idempotency key, schema version, occurred time and actor in the event header, and moves an event to the exception queue after the retry limit.
- The publishing stories exist for EV-01 CaseCreated and EV-02 CaseAllocated (RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-020), EV-04 CaseTransferred (RWB-E1-021), EV-16 DocumentStored (RWB-E1-024), EV-08 DecisionRecorded (RWB-E1-027) and EV-19 TimerBreached.
- The listener runs as service identity SY-CASEWF (Case record C).

### 4. Flow

1. Publishing module: commits its change and writes the event to the outbox in the same transaction.
2. Outbox: delivers the event to LedgerEventListener, in order per case.
3. LedgerEventListener: checks the schema version is the current or the previous version for the event.
4. LedgerEventMapper: maps the event to a LedgerEntryCommand: EV-01 to CASE_CREATED, EV-02 to CASE_ALLOCATED, EV-04 to CASE_TRANSFERRED, EV-19 to CASE_ESCALATED, EV-16 to DOCUMENT_ATTACHED, EV-08 to DECISION_TAKEN with the decision log entry ID.
5. LedgerEventMapper: sets actor from the event header (user ID or service identity), source system WORKBENCH, source reference as the owning module and event ID, and the event's idempotency key.
6. InteractionLedgerWriter: appends the entry with the next case_seq.
7. LedgerDuplicateService: when the idempotency key already exists, writes no entry and adds 1 to the hit count for that key (R-UNI-40).
8. Outbox: marks the event processed for the ledger consumer.
9. On failure: the outbox retries; after three retries the event goes to the exception queue with owner RW-PLATADM and incident LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED is raised.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The same event arrives twice with the same key | One entry; the repeat is counted | None | AC3 |
| X2 | An event with a schema version that is neither current nor previous | Not written; moved to the exception queue with owner RW-PLATADM | None (exception queue item) | AC4 |
| X3 | The ledger write fails | Retried three times, then the exception queue and an incident; the event is not discarded | MSG-P1-022 (incident detail) | AC5 |
| X4 | Events for one case arrive in written order | Entries follow that order in case_seq | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The same event reaches two consumer threads at once | One entry; one hit counted | None | AC7 |
| X6 | An event names a case that does not exist | Not written; moved to the exception queue | None (exception queue item) | AC8 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the ledger writer (RWB-E1-066) and the outbox (RWB-TE-006); the events come from stories earlier in Epic 1 |
| Negotiable | The event to entry map is configuration; the story fixes the listener, the duplicate rule and the failure path |
| Valuable | The case owner sees every Workbench action in the case history |
| Estimable | One listener, one mapper, one duplicate table |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion publishes synthetic events and reads the ledger |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Case creation, allocation, transfer, escalation, document attachment and each decision write a ledger entry as they happen | REQ-ILG-005; EV-01, EV-02, EV-04, EV-19, EV-16, EV-08 (events.txt) |
| BR2 | Every entry names the system or person that produced it | REQ-ILG-002 |
| BR3 | The same event with the same key produces one entry, and the repeat is counted | R-UNI-40; REQ-ILG-007 |
| BR4 | Events for one case are processed in the order they were written | Events rule "Ordering" (events.txt) |
| BR5 | A consumer failure retries, then goes to the exception queue with its owner | Events rule "Failure" (events.txt); R-UNI-36 |
| BR6 | A consumer accepts the current and the previous schema version | Events rule "Versioning" (events.txt) |
| BR7 | Event payloads carry references and codes, no personal data | Events rule "Payload" (events.txt) |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It adds ledger entries and moves failed events to the exception queue state EXCEPTION_QUEUE for the platform team (R-UNI-36).

| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Runs the ledger listener and appends entries (Case record C) |
| SY-RULES, SY-OCR, SY-DECLOG | Appear as actors on entries; do not call the writer |
| SY-AGENT, agent platform | May not append (Case record R) |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Owns exception queue items from the listener; receives the incident |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the entries through RWB-E1-068 |

### 12. Contract

**Listener**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Outbox delivery of EV-01 CaseCreated, EV-02 CaseAllocated, EV-04 CaseTransferred, EV-08 DecisionRecorded, EV-16 DocumentStored, EV-19 TimerBreached |
| Job name | None in batch.txt; the outbox consumer runs in the service, not as a scheduled job |
| Input | Event header (event ID, idempotency key, schema version, occurred time, actor) and payload as in events.txt |
| Output | One interaction row per event, or one hit on processed_event |
| Events published | None |
| Idempotency key | The event's idempotency key, unique on interaction.idempotency_key |
| Restart behavior | At-least-once delivery; an unprocessed event is delivered again after a restart; three retries, then the exception queue (NFR-026) |

**Published interface used (P1, from RWB-E1-066)**

```java
LedgerEntryRef InteractionLedgerWriter.append(LedgerEntryCommand command);
```

The writer checks that the calling identity holds Case record C; a call from an identity without it throws AccessDeniedException mapped to MSG-P4-002.

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `recovery/dataengine/ledger/events`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.ledger.events`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| LedgerEventListener | Listener | Outbox consumer for the six events; version check; calls the mapper and the writer |
| LedgerEventMapper | Service | Event to LedgerEntryCommand per the map in the flow, read from configuration |
| LedgerDuplicateService | Service | Catches the unique key clash on idempotency_key and adds a hit |
| InteractionDuplicateRepository | Repository | Upserts processed_event |
| InteractionDuplicate | Entity | One row per repeated idempotency key |

- Database: table processed_event (new, Flyway migration in this story) with idempotency_key varchar(120) primary key, first_interaction_id uuid not null, hit_count integer not null, last_hit_at timestamptz not null, plus the standard columns. Uses the interaction columns added by RWB-E1-066.
- Configuration and reference data: event to ledger event map in `rwb.dataengine.ledger.event-map` (EV-01=CASE_CREATED, EV-02=CASE_ALLOCATED, EV-04=CASE_TRANSFERRED, EV-08=DECISION_TAKEN, EV-16=DOCUMENT_ATTACHED, EV-19=CASE_ESCALATED); retry limit 3 from the outbox settings (NFR-026; DL11).
- Build steps:
  1. Flyway migration for processed_event.
  2. LedgerEventMapper with the configured map and the source reference "<owning module>, <event ID> <event name>".
  3. LedgerEventListener subscribed to the six events with the schema version check.
  4. LedgerDuplicateService on the unique key clash, inside a new transaction so the hit is recorded.
  5. Identity check in InteractionLedgerWriter for Case record C.
  6. Failure path through the outbox retry and exception queue, with LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED.
  7. Tests for AC1 to AC8 and the access test, publishing synthetic events through the outbox test fixture.
- Feature flag: `rwb.dataengine.ledger-events`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass and each of the six events has the ledger as a consumer in SIT.

| MSG-P4-002 | An identity without Case record C calls the writer | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

## RWB-E1-068 Interaction ledger read interface

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-068 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-ILG-03 Read the ledger in one ordered sequence |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-ILG-006, REQ-ILG-003, REQ-ILG-014 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story) and section 4 (REQ-ILG-003, REQ-ILG-006, REQ-ILG-014) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-066 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **to read a case's ledger in one ordered sequence, filtered by channel, actor or date range**, so that **I can see what has happened to it before I decide anything**.

### 2. Business rationale

A case owner who decides a route, a settlement or a legal step must first know what was said, promised, sent and done on the case. One read interface returns the ledger in order with the source of each entry, filters it by channel, actor and date range, and masks personal content by role on the same rules as the case record. The case record view and every other consumer read through this interface, so there is one ordering and one masking rule for the history. Serves REQ-ILG-006, REQ-ILG-003 and REQ-ILG-014; NFR-070 (one case history read in under 2 seconds at its 2031 size; DL11).

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-066 is done: the interaction table carries event_code, actor, source, case_seq and the decision link.
- RWB-E1-037 is done: P4 publishes the masking interface; masking rules may be empty (DL26), in which case every personal field is masked.
- P3 publishes CaseScopeQuery (RWB-E1-016) to check that the caller may see the case.
- The reader holds Case record R.

### 4. Flow

1. Case owner: opens SCR-03 Case record; the history panel calls GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions?page=0&size=50.
2. P3 interactions handler (API-P3-014): checks Case record R and calls InteractionLedgerReader.read() with the caller's context.
3. InteractionLedgerReader: checks the case is in the caller's scope through CaseScopeQuery.
4. InteractionLedgerReader: validates the filter (channel in LOV-CHANNEL, from not after to, size 1 to 200).
5. InteractionLedgerReader: reads the case's entries matching the filter, ordered by occurred_at, then case_seq.
6. InteractionLedgerReader: masks the summary field (is_personal) through the P4 masking interface for the caller's roles.
7. InteractionLedgerReader: writes the read to the PII access log when a personal field is returned unmasked.
8. P3 handler: returns InteractionPage with each entry's event, time, actor, channel, outcome, promise and source.
9. Case owner: filters by channel, actor or date range; the panel calls the same endpoint with the filter.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | from is after to | 422; nothing returned | MSG-GEN-003 | AC4 |
| X2 | The case is outside the caller's scope | 404 | MSG-P4-003 | AC5 |
| X3 | No masking rule allows the caller to see the summary | Summary returned as "MASKED" | None | AC6 |
| X4 | Page size above 200 | 422 | MSG-GEN-002 | AC7 |
| X5 | The case has no entries | 200 with an empty page; the panel shows the Empty state | None | AC8 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the ledger store (RWB-E1-066); masking and scope come from published interfaces of P4 and P3 |
| Negotiable | Page size limits are properties; the story fixes the order, the filters and the masking |
| Valuable | The case owner reads the full history before deciding |
| Estimable | One reader, one endpoint change, one panel |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is one API call on a synthetic ledger |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Interaction ledger read interface

  Background:
    Given case "RW-2026-000401" has 9 ledger entries from 2026-08-04 to 2026-12-06
    Given 3 entries come from EFS with channel CALL between 2026-08-04 and 2026-10-15
    Given 2 entries come from user "u-owner-04" with channel VISIT on 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-20
    Given 4 entries come from the Workbench with no channel between 2026-12-01 and 2026-12-06
    Given user "u-owner-04" holds RW-CASEOWN and owns the case

  Scenario: AC1 The ledger reads in order
    Given a case with entries from several sources
    When user "u-owner-04" calls GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions for case "RW-2026-000401"
    Then 9 entries come back ordered by occurred time, earliest first
    Then each entry names its source system and source reference, for example "EFS, INT-07" or "WORKBENCH, P3 case and workflow"

  Scenario: AC2 It can be filtered
    Given the 9-entry ledger
    When it is read three times: filtered by channel "CALL", by actor "u-owner-04", and from 2026-12-01 to 2026-12-06
    Then the first read returns only the 3 EFS call entries
    Then the second read returns only the 2 VISIT entries
    Then the third read returns only the 4 Workbench entries

  Scenario: AC3 It is available to the case record
    Given the case record view SCR-03 for case "RW-2026-000401"
    When it loads
    Then its history panel shows the 9 entries from GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions
    Then the architecture test finds no class outside the ledger package that queries the interaction table

  Scenario: AC4 A date range in the wrong order
    When the case owner filters from 2026-12-06 to 2026-12-01
    Then the system refuses the call with status 422 and MSG-GEN-003 for "to" and "from"

  Scenario: AC5 A case outside the caller's scope
    Given user "u-owner-05" holds RW-CASEOWN and does not own case "RW-2026-000401"
    When the user reads its ledger
    Then the system refuses the call with status 404 and MSG-P4-003

  Scenario: AC6 Summary masked when no masking rule allows it
    Given no masking rule from Compliance is loaded for interaction.summary
    When user "u-owner-04" reads the ledger
    Then the system returns the summary of each entry as "MASKED"
    Then the channel, result, promise amount and promise date are returned in full

  Scenario: AC7 Page size at and above the limit
    When the case owner reads once with size 200 and once with size 201
    Then the read with size 200 returns the 9 entries with size 200
    Then the system refuses the read with size 201 with status 422 and MSG-GEN-002 for "size" between 1 and 200

  Scenario: AC8 A case with no entries
    Given case "RW-2026-000402" has no ledger entries
    When its owner reads the ledger
    Then the response holds 0 items and total 0
    Then the history panel shows the Empty state
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The ledger reads back in one ordered sequence, by occurred time and then case sequence | REQ-ILG-006; interaction.occurred_at; interaction.case_seq |
| BR2 | The ledger can be filtered by channel, actor and date range through one interface | REQ-ILG-006 |
| BR3 | Entries carry channel, who or what was reached, and the outcome where the interaction had one | REQ-ILG-003; interaction.contact_result |
| BR4 | Personal data in the ledger is masked by role on the same rules as the case record | REQ-ILG-014; CTL-11; DL26 |
| BR5 | A case outside the caller's scope is refused | CTL-09 |
| BR6 | No consumer queries the interaction table directly | ADR-002; DT08 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It reads the ledger and changes nothing.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the ledger of own cases (Case record R, scope Own) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads the ledger of team cases (Case record R, scope Team) |
| RW-CONDUCT, RW-AUDIT and other roles with Case record R | Read the ledger of cases in their scope |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | May not read (no Case record right) |
| RW-COMPLY, Compliance and PDPA officer | Owns the masking rules that decide who sees the summary (DL26) |

### 12. Contract

**Endpoint (P3, API-P3-014, extended; see additions)**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Method and path | GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions |
| Request | Path: caseId; query: channel, from, to, page, size as in api.yaml, plus actor (new) |
| Response | InteractionPage: items of Interaction, page, size, total. Interaction gains eventCode, caseSeq, actorType, actorRef, sourceRef and decisionLogEntryId (new); summary is masked by role |
| Errors | 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Case record R (MSG-P4-002); 404 case missing or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 422 filter invalid (MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002, MSG-GEN-003); 503 store down (MSG-GEN-006) |
| Authorization | Case record, R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**Published interface (P1)**

```java
package recovery.dataengine.ledger.api;

public interface InteractionLedgerReader {
    LedgerPage read(UUID caseId, LedgerFilter filter, int page, int size, UserContext caller)
            throws CaseNotInScopeException;
}

public record LedgerFilter(String channel, String actorRef, LocalDate from, LocalDate to) {}
public record LedgerPage(List<LedgerEntryView> items, int page, int size, long total) {}
```

### 13. Solution plan

- Package: folder `recovery/dataengine/ledger/read`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.ledger.read`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| InteractionLedgerReader | Published interface | The one read path for the ledger |
| LedgerReadService | Service | Scope check, filter validation, ordered query, masking, PII log |
| InteractionRepository | Repository | Read query by case and filter, ordered by occurred_at, case_seq |
| InteractionsHandler (P3, API-P3-014) | Controller | Existing P3 endpoint; adds the actor parameter and delegates to the reader |
| CaseHistoryPanel | React component | History panel on SCR-03 with channel, actor and date filters, paging and the Empty state |

- Database: no new table. Query on interaction by case_id with optional channel, actor_ref and occurred_at range, ordered by occurred_at, case_seq; uses ix_interaction_case_time (Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql). Add index (case_id, actor_ref) in a Flyway migration for the actor filter.
- Configuration and reference data: properties `rwb.dataengine.ledger.page-size-default=50` and `rwb.dataengine.ledger.page-size-max=200`; LOV-CHANNEL for the channel filter; masking rules from Compliance through RWB-E1-037 (DL26).
- Build steps:
  1. LedgerFilter validation: channel in LOV-CHANNEL, from not after to, size 1 to 200.
  2. Ordered, filtered, paged query in InteractionRepository and the actor index migration.
  3. Scope check through CaseScopeQuery before the query.
  4. Masking of summary through MaskingPolicy; PII access log write when a personal field is returned unmasked.
  5. P3 InteractionsHandler: actor parameter, new response fields, delegation to the reader.
  6. CaseHistoryPanel on SCR-03 with filters, paging, Loading and Empty states.
  7. Architecture test that no class outside `recovery.dataengine.ledger` queries interaction.
  8. Tests for AC1 to AC8 and the access test; a timed read of one case with 5,000 entries against the 2 second target (NFR-070).
- Feature flag: `rwb.dataengine.ledger-read`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass and SCR-03 shows the ledger in SIT.

## RWB-E1-069 Read-only ACE source views, grants and boundary rule

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-069 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-01 Create the recovery tables, extension tables and read-only ACE views |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-002, REQ-DRI-006 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story) and section 4 (REQ-RDF-002); Business Requirements Program, sections 5.2 and 7 (REQ-DRI-006) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010; DL43 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001 (V0001); RWB-ACE-001 for the 14 Section B views (DL43) |
| Blocks | RWB-E1-002, RWB-E1-016, RWB-E1-018 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **recovery developer (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **the recovery module to read ACE source data only through SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views, with the database grants and the build-time rule that enforce the boundary**, so that **there is one copy of source data, the Workbench cannot alter or copy it, and a direct read of an ACE table fails in the database and in the build**.

### 2. Business rationale

The Workbench takes no inbound source data. ACE ingests every source, and the recovery module reads it through 30 SELECT-only views: 16 over the ACE tables that exist today, 177 fields, and 14 over the tables RWB-ACE-001 adds, 127 fields. The views are owned by a dedicated role that holds SELECT on the ACE tables; the recovery service role holds SELECT on the views and no privilege on anything in `public`. PUBLIC holds no privilege, and no write is granted on a view. The Workbench keeps its own decisions about an ACE record in four extension tables keyed by the ACE business key, never in a copy of an ACE column.

The boundary is enforced twice: by the catalog, where a direct `public` read is refused, and by boundary rule BND-6 in RWB-TE-001, which fails the build when a recovery class names a `public` table. Serves REQ-RDF-002 (account balance, arrears, payments and classification read from ACE through `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_payment`) and REQ-DRI-006 (no component calls a system of record directly); applies D-RCV-35 U1 and U4 and ADR-010. The measure is 100 percent of pipeline runs in which every view compiles and the conformance test passes.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-001 is done: V0001 created the recovery tables, the three helper functions `recovery.ace_to_date`, `recovery.ace_to_boolean` and `recovery.ace_mask_value`, the dictionary rows and the view `v_data_dictionary`.
- RWB-E1-044 is done: Flyway runs in the ACE pipeline and takes the schema name from the parameter `recoverySchema`, fixed to `recovery` in every environment (D-RCV-28).
- The ACE schema in DEV and SIT is at the head that holds the 21 Tier 1 tables of section 11, among them `account`, `payment`, `customer` and `efs_action` (ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql).
- The roles `ace_view_owner` and `recovery_svc` exist in DEV and SIT, with the names fixed in the Environment and Deployment Design. The recovery migration account holds the ACE DBA role for the release window, so it can grant on schema `public` and set a view owner (RWB-E1-044).
- The module map of RWB-TE-001 is in the repository, with `recovery-modules.yaml` read by `RecoveryBoundaryTest`.
- For the 14 Section B views only: RWB-ACE-001 is deployed in DEV and SIT and its 14 Tier 2 tables exist (DL43). Until then the features that read a Section B view stay behind their flags.

### 4. Flow

1. Recovery developer: takes Section A of `15 ACE DB Alignment/Recovery Workbench ACE Source Views v1.sql` into `V0002__rwb_e1_069_ace_source_views.sql`: the 16 views, the three helper functions and the grant block. The four extension tables ship in V0001 with RWB-E1-001, which runs first; this story verifies them rather than creating them.
2. Recovery developer: writes no environment name in the file. The schema is `${recoverySchema}` and the two role names come from the Environment and Deployment Design (D-RCV-28; RWB-E1-044).
3. Pipeline: applies V0001 then V0002 in DEV, then in SIT.
4. Pipeline: runs the conformance test: 16 of 16 views compile, no constraint in `recovery` references `public`, every view has dictionary rows, and `recovery_svc` has no privilege in `public` and no write on a view.
5. Recovery developer: adds boundary rule BND-6 to `RecoveryBoundaryTest` in RWB-TE-001 and the 30 view names to `recovery-modules.yaml` as the only allowed source objects.
6. ACE team: applies RWB-ACE-001 with the 14 Tier 2 tables, and its migration grants SELECT on those tables to `ace_view_owner` (DL43).
7. Recovery developer: writes `V0003__rwb_e1_069_ace_tier2_views.sql` with the 14 Section B views and one SELECT grant per view to `recovery_svc`. The dictionary rows for the 14 views ship with V0001, as the 16 Section A rows do.
8. Pipeline: applies V0003 in DEV and SIT; 30 of 30 views compile and the features that read a Section B view come out from behind their flags.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A Section A view does not compile | The V0002 stage rolls back; no view from that run exists; the extension tables from V0001 are unchanged; the stage names the view and the ACE column | Pipeline log: v_ace_account does not compile: column a.core_banking_system_date does not exist | AC1 |
| X2 | V0003 is applied before RWB-ACE-001 | The stage fails; no Section B view is created; the 16 Section A views and their features are unchanged | Pipeline log: relation public.valuation does not exist | AC3 |
| X3 | A recovery constraint references a table in `public` | The conformance test fails and the merge is blocked | fk_case_account_account_key references public.account; no constraint in recovery may reference another schema | AC4 |
| X4 | A view has no `sys_objects` row or a column has no `sys_fields` row | The conformance test fails and names the view and the column | v_ace_account.legacy_bucket has no data dictionary entry | AC5 |
| X5 | `recovery_svc` holds a privilege in `public`, or a write on a view | The conformance test fails and names the privilege and the object | recovery_svc holds SELECT on public.account; the recovery role reads the views only | AC2 |
| X6 | A recovery class names a table in `public` | The build fails with boundary rule BND-6 and the class is named | Boundary rule BND-6 broken: AccountReader reads public.account. Read recovery.v_ace_account instead. | AC8 |
| X7 | A second row is written for an ACE key already in an extension table | The write is refused; the first row is unchanged | SQLSTATE 23505 duplicate key value violates unique constraint party_ext_pkey | AC7 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs V0001 and, for Section B, the ACE tables RWB-ACE-001 adds; it publishes the read path every later story uses |
| Negotiable | The view names and fields are frozen in the ACE Data Tier Map v1 and the ACE Source Views file; the migration order and the test harness are the squad's choice |
| Valuable | One copy of source data, a boundary the database enforces, and no load estate to build |
| Estimable | Two migrations, four extension tables, one conformance test class, one boundary rule |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is one pipeline run or one catalog query |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The recovery module reads ACE source data only through the 30 SELECT-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views: 16 now over tables ACE holds, 14 when RWB-ACE-001 lands. It loads, copies and transforms nothing | D-RCV-35 U1, U4; ADR-010 |
| BR2 | A view is owned by `ace_view_owner`, which holds SELECT on the ACE tables it reads and writes nothing. It holds no right in schema `recovery` other than the views it owns | D-RCV-35 U4; CTL-02 |
| BR3 | On ACE source data `recovery_svc` holds SELECT on the views and no privilege of any kind in `public`; PUBLIC holds nothing; no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE is granted on a view. Its DML on the Workbench's own tables is granted by V0001 and is outside this story | D-RCV-35 U4; BR-P1-001-4; CTL-02 |
| BR4 | No constraint in schema `recovery` references a table or a type outside it. A link to an ACE record is a `varchar(255)` business-key column with no foreign key, because ACE cascades deletes on `account` | D-RCV-35 U4; BR-P1-001-3; ADR-010 |
| BR5 | Every view carries one `sys_objects` row and one `sys_fields` row per column, with the ACE source field and the data product | BR-P1-001; RWB-E1-064 |
| BR6 | A text date in ACE becomes a date through `recovery.ace_to_date`, and a Y/N flag becomes a boolean through `recovery.ace_to_boolean`; both return NULL rather than fail a read | BR-P1-001-7 |
| BR7 | An extension table holds a Workbench decision about an ACE record and never a copy of an ACE column. It is 1:1 with the ACE record on the ACE business key and carries the seven standard record columns | BR-P1-001-5 |
| BR8 | Boundary rule BND-6: no recovery class names a table in schema `public`; the only source objects it may name are the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views, read from the module map | REQ-DRI-006; RWB-TE-001 |
| BR9 | A Section B view is created only after its ACE table exists. Until then the feature that reads it stays behind its flag, and V0003 is a later Flyway sequence | ADR-010; DL43 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It moves schema `recovery` through two Flyway versions (V0002 now, V0003 with RWB-ACE-001), changes the privileges of two database roles and owns no business row.

### 12. Contract

No endpoint and no event. The contract is the migration set and the grant.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Migration V0002 | `V0002__rwb_e1_069_ace_source_views.sql`: the four extension tables, the 16 Section A views, the Section A grant |
| Migration V0003 | `V0003__rwb_e1_069_ace_tier2_views.sql`: the 14 Section B views, the Section B grant |
| Published interface | The 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views: one row per ACE object, no primary key, no foreign key. Every module reads source data here and nowhere else |
| Grantees | `ace_view_owner` owns the views and holds SELECT on the ACE tables; `recovery_svc` holds SELECT on the views only; PUBLIC holds nothing |
| Trigger | The pipeline step `migrate` at deployment (RWB-E1-044) |
| Idempotency | The Flyway version. An applied version is never applied again; a repeated GRANT changes nothing |
| Restart | A failed migration rolls back. A fix is merged as a new version; V0003 waits until RWB-ACE-001 is deployed |
| Output | Applied objects in schema `recovery`; rows in `flyway_schema_history_recovery`; a pass or a named failure from the conformance test |

**Grant block in V0002** (run as the ACE schema owner; the 16 ALTER VIEW OWNER statements are one per view)

```sql
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO ace_view_owner;
GRANT SELECT ON public.account, public.payment, public.customer, public.phone, public.email,
     public.address, public.ca_relation, public.aa_relation, public.collateral, public.asset,
     public.efs_action, public.efs_action_code, public.efs_assignment,
     public.bucket_log_snapshot, public.product, public.branch, public.bot_holiday,
     public.ace_case, public.cfsc_mg_ssme_tdr_case, public.tdr_calculation,
     public.ai_recommended_plan
     TO ace_view_owner;

ALTER VIEW recovery.v_ace_account OWNER TO ace_view_owner;
-- one ALTER VIEW OWNER statement for each of the 16 views

GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA recovery TO recovery_svc;
GRANT SELECT ON recovery.v_ace_account TO recovery_svc;
-- one GRANT per view, 16 in V0002 and 30 in all; never GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA recovery

REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA recovery FROM PUBLIC;
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Packages and files.** Migration files in `ace-service/src/main/resources/db/migration/recovery` (RWB-E1-044). Boundary rule in the test source of the recovery module, beside `RecoveryBoundaryTest` (RWB-TE-001). The view definitions are taken verbatim from `15 ACE DB Alignment/Recovery Workbench ACE Source Views v1.sql`; the four extension tables verbatim from `06 Data/Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| V0002__rwb_e1_069_ace_source_views.sql | Migration | Four extension tables, 16 Section A views, Section A grant |
| V0003__rwb_e1_069_ace_tier2_views.sql | Migration | 14 Section B views and their SELECT grant |
| ViewConformanceTest | Test | Four checks: every view compiles, no constraint references `public`, every view has dictionary rows, `recovery_svc` has no privilege in `public` and no write on a view |
| SourceViewBoundaryRule | ArchUnit rule in RecoveryBoundaryTest | Boundary rule BND-6: a recovery class names no table in schema `public` |
| recovery-modules.yaml | Rule table | Gains `sourceViews`, the 30 view names that BND-6 allows |
| recovery.v_ace_* | Published read interface | The only source read for every module |

**Database.** V0002 creates four tables and 16 views; V0003 creates 14 views. No table in schema `recovery` gains a foreign key into `public`, and no ACE table is altered. The extension tables are:

- `party_ext`: person_key varchar(255) primary key, vulnerable, deceased_override, bankruptcy, fraud_flag boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, is_active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true, state varchar(40), version integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at and updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), created_by and updated_by uuid.
- `contact_point_ext`: contact_key varchar(255) primary key, contact_type varchar(10) NOT NULL, consent_given boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, consent_at and verified_at timestamptz, failed_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, source varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'WORKBENCH', is_active, state, version, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by, and the check `ck_contact_point_ext_type` that contact_type is PHONE, EMAIL or ADDRESS.
- `account_ext`: account_key varchar(255) primary key, dispute_open boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, is_active, state, version, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by.
- `valuation_ext`: valuation_key varchar(255) primary key, accepted boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, accepted_at timestamptz, accepted_by and valuer_partner_id uuid, stale_flag boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, age_days integer, is_active, state, version, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by.

**Configuration and reference data.** The roles `ace_view_owner` and `recovery_svc` and their names are fixed in the Environment and Deployment Design. The schema is `${recoverySchema}`, fixed to `recovery` (D-RCV-28). The 30-view list is frozen in the ACE Data Tier Map v1 and copied into `recovery-modules.yaml`; a change needs the data architect and the recovery tech lead. Section B features keep their own flags.

**Build steps**

1. V0002: the four extension tables, copied from Physical Schema v6 with their primary keys and the contact type check (AC7).
2. V0002: the 16 Section A views, copied from the ACE Source Views file, using the V0001 helper functions (AC1).
3. V0002: the grant block of section 12, with one GRANT and one ALTER VIEW OWNER per view and no `ALL TABLES` grant (AC2).
4. ViewConformanceTest with its four checks and a failing fixture for each (AC1 to AC5).
5. Boundary rule BND-6 in RecoveryBoundaryTest, reading `sourceViews` from the module map, with a fixture class on `public.account` and the same class on `recovery.v_ace_account` (AC8).
6. V0003: the 14 Section B views, copied from the ACE Source Views file, and one SELECT grant per view (AC3).
7. A pipeline stage for V0003 that runs only after RWB-ACE-001 is reported deployed; before that the stage is skipped and the Section B features stay behind their flags (AC3).
8. Tests for AC1 to AC8, including the access test on `recovery_svc` and a test role with no grant.

**Feature flag.** None for the views; they are the read path, not a feature. Each Section B feature keeps the flag it already has until V0003 is applied.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, SIT holds 30 compiling views and four extension tables, and the pipeline of main shows the conformance test and boundary rule BND-6 in its report.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| Conformance check 1 | A view does not compile | v_ace_account does not compile: column a.core_banking_system_date does not exist |
| Conformance check 2 | A constraint references `public` | fk_case_account_account_key references public.account; no constraint in recovery may reference another schema |
| Conformance check 3 | A view has no dictionary row | v_ace_account.legacy_bucket has no data dictionary entry |
| Conformance check 4 | `recovery_svc` holds a privilege in `public` or can write a view | recovery_svc holds SELECT on public.account; the recovery role reads the views only |
| Build log | A recovery class names a `public` table | Boundary rule BND-6 broken: AccountReader reads public.account. Read recovery.v_ace_account instead. |
| SQLSTATE 42501 | `recovery_svc` selects a public table or writes a view | permission denied for schema public |
| SQLSTATE 23505 | A second row for one ACE key in an extension table | duplicate key value violates unique constraint party_ext_pkey |

No `MSG-` ID applies: this story has no user-facing message. Pipeline and build log text is for developers and is not part of the message standard.

No screen in this story. A developer reads the conformance test and boundary rule BND-6 in the pull request checks.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the view list and the role names are configuration and data, not constants in a service.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts: test rows are synthetic; the customer view returns `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` only and never the clear identity number.
- No read of a `public` table and no write to an ACE table: the database grants and boundary rule BND-6 enforce it, and a breach is a defect.
- The views are forward only in PROD; a wrong view is corrected by a new migration, never by editing an applied one.

| REQ-DRI-006 | No component calls a system of record directly | Business Requirements Program, sections 5.2 and 7 | FEAT-RDF-01 | All recovery processes | ADR-010; DL43 | TC-E1-069-04, TC-E1-069-08 |
| D-RCV-35 U4 | The Workbench reads ACE only through the views and holds no copy | Decision log, D-RCV-35 section 6.1; ADR-010 | FEAT-RDF-01 | All recovery processes | ADR-010; CTL-02 | TC-E1-069-01 to TC-E1-069-08 |

### 19. Out of scope

- The 14 Tier 2 tables and the 12 columns that RWB-ACE-001 adds to `account`, `customer` and `efs_action`: the ACE team owns them, and this story neither creates nor alters them.
- The features that read a Section B view: their own stories, behind their flags until V0003 is applied.
- Masking at the API and the PII access log: RWB-E1-037 and RWB-E1-016.
- The data dictionary content and its maintenance: RWB-E1-001 for the metadata rows and RWB-E1-064 for the dictionary of the 14 data products.
- The rest of RWB-TE-001: this story adds boundary rule BND-6 and the `sourceViews` list only.
- Any change to the 30-view list: the data architect and the recovery tech lead, with a new version of the ACE Data Tier Map v1.

| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **a Temporal cluster per environment on the ACE AKS clusters, with its own persistence databases, the rwb-recovery namespace, mTLS and the Web UI behind Entra SSO**, so that **case workflows from Epic 3 have a durable engine that SCB IT runs like the rest of ACE**.

### 2. Business rationale

Case workflow begins in Epic 3, and a durable engine must exist before the first case workflow is written. ADR-011 replaces ADR-003 (DT09, DT10): Temporal runs the case lifecycle, while case data remains the system of record in the ACE DB recovery schema. If the engine is installed without its own database, identity, certificates and run book, Epic 3 builds on a shared service that nobody owns and a restart becomes a developer task.

This story provides the platform only: one Temporal cluster per environment on the ACE AKS clusters, the databases temporal and temporal_visibility owned by temporal_svc, the rwb-recovery namespace with 30-day retention and four search attributes, mTLS between the services, the Web UI behind Entra ID OIDC, metrics to the ACE monitoring stack and a run book with the eight sections of RWB-E1-056. It meets REQ-DRI-007 (a named owner and a tested way back for every failure) and REQ-DRI-010 (environment values come from parameters, not code). The measure is that DEV and SIT pass every check in section 16 and that operations restarts a stopped frontend in SIT from the run book alone.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-044 is done: migrations run with parameterized schema names, and the ACE database exists in each environment.
- RWB-E1-056 is done: job_catalog, the run book catalog and RunbookCompletenessTest exist and accept a new run book with the eight sections.
- RWB-E1-022 is done: Entra ID SSO, MFA and the application roles exist, including RW-PLATADM and RW-AUDIT.
- The ACE AKS clusters for DEV, SIT, UAT and PROD exist with the ACE namespace, a zone-redundant PostgreSQL flexible server, Azure Key Vault and the ACE monitoring namespace.
- SCB IT approved the Temporal server and Java SDK release on 16 November 2026; the approved version is recorded in Environment and Deployment Design v4 and is not selected by the build.
- An internal DNS name and ingress exist for the Web UI; the frontend gRPC port 7233 is reachable only from the cluster network and the worker subnets.
- The ACE internal certificate authority issues the mTLS certificates, and the platform administrator may read the certificate from Key Vault.
- The platform administrator holds RW-PLATADM through the environment group; RW-AUDIT holds RW-AUDIT through the environment group.

### 4. Flow

1. Platform administrator: deploys Helm release rwb-temporal into the ACE namespace of DEV, then SIT, from the values file; the chart runs frontend, history, matching, internal-worker and web.
2. TemporalSchemaJob: creates the databases temporal and temporal_visibility owned by temporal_svc, then runs the Temporal schema tool at the pinned server version; a second run changes nothing.
3. NamespaceBootstrapJob: registers the namespace rwb-recovery with retention 30 days and the Keyword search attributes CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup and QueueCode; a second run changes nothing.
4. Platform administrator: binds the mTLS certificate and key from Key Vault to the frontend and the workers through the CSI driver; the certificate is issued by the ACE internal CA and names the namespace.
5. Platform administrator: configures the Web UI with Entra ID OIDC; the app roles map RW-PLATADM to operate and RW-AUDIT to read; any other role is refused.
6. Platform administrator: turns on the metrics scrape to the ACE monitoring stack and imports the platform dashboard.
7. Platform administrator: runs every check in section 16 and records the pinned server and SDK version in Environment and Deployment Design v4.
8. Platform administrator: writes the run book with the eight sections and asks operations to restart the frontend in SIT from the run book alone.
9. System: a frontend pod restart or reschedule keeps every workflow; history and visibility are durable in PostgreSQL, and the workers reconnect to the new pod.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A client connects to the frontend with no certificate, an expired certificate or a certificate for another namespace | The TLS handshake fails or the call is refused; no workflow call is served and the event is in the frontend log with the client identity only | None (TLS) | AC3 |
| X2 | A user with a Workbench role other than RW-PLATADM or RW-AUDIT signs in to the Web UI | The sign-in is refused; no namespace is listed and no workflow is shown | MSG-P4-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | A grant joins the two databases, for example temporal_svc on the recovery schema or recovery_svc on temporal | The access review check fails, the release is held and the grant is removed before the next environment | None (access review) | AC2 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Stands alone as infrastructure; it needs the ACE cluster, the schema of RWB-E1-044, the roles of RWB-E1-022 and the run book catalog of RWB-E1-056 |
| Negotiable | Pod sizes, storage class, replica count, certificate life and dashboard panels are Helm values; the separation of databases and the namespace settings are fixed |
| Valuable | Epic 3 starts on an engine that SCB IT can run, restart and review like the rest of ACE |
| Estimable | One Helm release, two databases, one namespace bootstrap, one OIDC app, one certificate binding, one dashboard and one run book |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its checks |
| Testable | Each criterion in section 7 is one check in section 16 |

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One Temporal cluster per environment, on the ACE AKS clusters, deployed by the official Temporal Helm chart; the server and Java SDK version are pinned to the SCB IT approved release and recorded in Environment and Deployment Design v4 | D-RCV-36 T1; ADR-011 |
| BR2 | Temporal persistence is separate from the ACE database: databases temporal and temporal_visibility are owned by temporal_svc; temporal_svc has no grant on the ACE database and recovery_svc has no grant on the Temporal databases | D-RCV-36 T1 |
| BR3 | The frontend requires mTLS from every client; certificates come from the ACE internal CA through Key Vault and are renewed before expiry | D-RCV-36 T1 |
| BR4 | The Web UI is behind Entra ID OIDC: RW-PLATADM operates, RW-AUDIT reads, every other role is refused; decode is not in this story | D-RCV-36 T1; RWB-E1-022 |
| BR5 | One namespace per environment, rwb-recovery; retention is 30 days and the only search attributes are CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup and QueueCode as Keyword | D-RCV-36 T1 |
| BR6 | A frontend pod restart loses no workflow; history and visibility are durable in PostgreSQL | D-RCV-36 T1; AC6 |
| BR7 | The run book has the eight sections of RWB-E1-056 and is tested by RunbookCompletenessTest | RWB-E1-056 |
| BR8 | Server and SDK versions, replica counts, retention and node sizes are Helm values or parameters, never code | REQ-DRI-010 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status. It establishes the namespace and the cluster; a workflow created in Epic 3 moves through its own states. A namespace has one state, REGISTERED, and a server has one state, RUNNING; a server upgrade stays RUNNING and is checked by AC1 after the change.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-PLATADM | Installs and upgrades the release, runs the namespace bootstrap, reads the database grants, operates the Web UI and restarts a service (Platform administration, U) |
| RW-AUDIT | Reads the namespace and workflow history in the Web UI (Platform administration, R) |
| RW-SECADM | Reads the certificate and OIDC configuration; decode through the codec server is RWB-E2-038, not this story |
| RW-CASEOWN and every other Workbench role | No Web UI access; a sign-in is refused with MSG-P4-002 |
| SY-CASEWF | Connects to the frontend as the worker with its own client certificate; no Web UI account |
| SY-RULES | Runs the Drools evaluator inside the recovery module and does not connect to Temporal directly |
| RW-TRIBE | Maintains the Helm values and the run book through the change process; may not deploy to PROD |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A platform deployment is not a credit decision |

### 11. Data

Temporal persistence is outside the recovery schema. This story reads and writes no table in the recovery schema, and no DF-REF, DF-CAS or DF-DEC field is added or changed.

| Store | What it holds | Owner | In the Physical Schema |
|---|---|---|---|
| temporal | Workflow histories, mutable state, timers, tasks | temporal_svc | No |
| temporal_visibility | Workflow visibility records and search attributes | temporal_svc | No |
| ACE database recovery schema | Case data, the system of record | recovery_svc | Yes, unchanged by this story |

The Physical Schema v6 counts 93 tables and does not include the Temporal tables. The databases are created by TemporalSchemaJob; no Flyway migration in the recovery module touches them.

### 12. Contract

No Workbench endpoint. This story adds no path under /api/recovery/v1. The platform interfaces are internal to the ACE network.

| Interface | Method | Request | Response | Errors | Authorization | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Temporal frontend | gRPC over mTLS, port 7233: StartWorkflowExecution, SignalWorkflowExecution, DescribeWorkflowExecution | namespace rwb-recovery, workflow type, workflow ID, task queue, encrypted input | workflow ID and run ID | TLS handshake failure; NOT_FOUND namespace; PERMISSION_DENIED; FAILED_PRECONDITION | Client certificate from the ACE internal CA with the namespace claim | Workflow ID is the idempotency key; a repeated start with the same ID returns the running execution |
| Temporal Web UI | HTTPS 443: HTTP GET and POST through the internal ingress (OIDC sign-in and UI pages) | Entra ID OIDC authorization code flow | namespace and workflow pages | 401 MSG-P4-001 when the user has no Workbench role; 403 MSG-P4-002 when the role is not RW-PLATADM or RW-AUDIT | Entra app role RW-PLATADM (operate) or RW-AUDIT (read) | Read only; sign-in is safe to repeat |
| Metrics endpoint | HTTPS GET /metrics, port 9090 | Prometheus scrape of the Temporal SDK metrics | OpenMetrics text | None | Network policy from the ACE monitoring namespace only | Read only |
| Health endpoint | HTTP GET /health, port 8080 | None | 200 when the service is ready, 503 when it is not | 503 | Cluster probe only | Read only |

The frontend never accepts a Workbench JWT. The Workbench API does not proxy case workflow calls in Epic 1; the smoke endpoint of RWB-E1-071 is the only Workbench path that starts a workflow, and the worker connects to the frontend directly.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** No Java package. The deployment assets live in `deploy/temporal/`; the run book lives in `docs/operations/runbooks/RWB-E1-070.md`; the dashboard lives in `ops/monitoring/`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-temporal-values.yaml | Helm values | Images, replica counts, resources, persistence, mTLS, metrics and ingress per environment |
| TemporalSchemaJob | Pipeline job | Creates temporal and temporal_visibility and runs the Temporal schema tool at the pinned version; idempotent |
| NamespaceBootstrapJob | Pipeline job | Registers rwb-recovery with retention 30 days and the four Keyword search attributes; idempotent |
| OidcConfig | Configuration | Entra ID app registration, redirect URI, role claims and the mapping to RW-PLATADM and RW-AUDIT |
| KeyVaultCertificateBinding | Configuration | CSI driver binding of the mTLS certificate and key; renewal before expiry |
| TemporalPlatformDashboard | Dashboard | Grafana JSON for service readiness, request rate, errors and persistence latency |
| TemporalPlatformRunBook | Document | The eight sections of RWB-E1-056, with the restart steps for each service |

**Database and namespace**

- Create the databases temporal and temporal_visibility with owner temporal_svc on the zone-redundant PostgreSQL flexible server.
- Create the roles temporal_svc and recovery_svc with no membership in each other; revoke PUBLIC on both databases.
- Register rwb-recovery with retention 720 hours and the search attributes CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup and QueueCode as Keyword.
- Keep ace-collection unregistered; it belongs to the ACE team.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Parameters through RWB-E1-042: temporal.target, temporal.namespace, temporal.taskqueue.platform, temporal.retention.days = 30.
- Helm values per environment: replica counts, resources, storage class, ingress host, certificate secret name, metrics scrape and log level.
- No business parameter and no reference table in this story.

**Build steps**

1. Write the values file for DEV and SIT and run helm lint and helm template in the pipeline.
2. Build TemporalSchemaJob with the schema tool; prove a second run changes nothing.
3. Build NamespaceBootstrapJob with retention and the four search attributes; prove a second run changes nothing.
4. Bind the certificate from Key Vault; test AC3 with no certificate, an expired certificate and a foreign certificate.
5. Configure the OIDC app roles; test AC4 with RW-CASEOWN, RW-AUDIT and RW-PLATADM.
6. Add the metrics scrape and import the dashboard; check that every service reports.
7. Run the database grant checks for AC2 and add them to the access review.
8. Write the run book and pass RunbookCompletenessTest; run the frontend restart in SIT for AC6.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.temporal`. The flag controls the worker of RWB-E1-071, not the cluster. With the flag off, the cluster and namespace stay in place and nothing else changes.

**Done when.** The checks in section 16 pass in DEV and SIT, the database grants are in the access review, and operations restarts the frontend in SIT from the run book alone.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | A Workbench role other than RW-PLATADM or RW-AUDIT signs in to the Web UI | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

A certificate failure shows in the frontend log and the TLS alert only; no Workbench message is shown because no Workbench screen is involved. The run book names the alert text and the check.

### 15. Screens and states

No Workbench screen in this story. The operational view is the Temporal Web UI behind Entra ID, with two states: operate for RW-PLATADM and read-only for RW-AUDIT. A refused sign-in shows MSG-P4-002. The Grafana dashboard "Temporal platform" shows the five services, request rate, errors and persistence latency. The Workbench admin screens for platform settings come in Epic 8.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: replica counts, retention, node sizes and versions are Helm values or parameters.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts: search attributes hold case codes and queue codes only; the smoke payload is synthetic.
- No read of another module's tables; ACE data only through recovery.v_ace_* views: this story reads no recovery or ACE table.
- Temporal persistence is never placed in the ACE database, and the recovery schema is never granted to temporal_svc.
- No Web UI account for a role other than RW-PLATADM and RW-AUDIT; no shared operator account.
- No clear personal data in the Temporal payload; the codec is RWB-E1-071.
- No mTLS bypass in DEV or SIT; a test that needs a certificate uses a certificate from the test CA.

## RWB-E1-071 Temporal worker and SDK in the recovery module

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-071 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | None (platform enabler) |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-005, REQ-DRI-007, REQ-DRI-010 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.2; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.1 and 5.2 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | D-RCV-36 (T1, T2, T7); ADR-011 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-070, RWB-E1-042, RWB-E1-047, RWB-TE-001 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **the recovery module to run a Temporal worker through the Spring Boot starter, with fixed task-queue and workflow-ID conventions, a PDPA payload codec and a smoke workflow**, so that **Epic 3 workflows plug into a worker that is already secure and observable**.

### 2. Business rationale

The Temporal cluster of RWB-E1-070 is only useful when a worker connects to it from the recovery module. Without one worker pattern, each Epic 3 squad would choose its own task queue, workflow ID, payload handling and start-up checks, and the first clear personal data in a workflow history would be found in production. This story gives the module one worker, one codec, one gateway and one smoke workflow, and it proves the path end to end before the first case workflow exists.

It meets REQ-DRI-005 (an action does not proceed when its decision record cannot be written), REQ-DRI-007 (a failed start reaches a named owner) and REQ-DRI-010 (the target, namespace and task queue are parameters, not code). It follows D-RCV-36 T1 (hybrid, case data stays in the ACE DB), T2 (Quartz stays for Epic 1 and 2 jobs; the smoke job is Quartz) and T7 (workflow code is deterministic and calls Drools only inside an activity). The measure is a daily smoke workflow that completes with one decision log entry and a history that holds no clear personal data.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-070 is done: the Temporal cluster, the rwb-recovery namespace, mTLS and the Web UI exist in DEV and SIT.
- RWB-E1-042 is done: ParameterService serves temporal.target, temporal.namespace, temporal.taskqueue.platform and temporal.retention.days = 30; the values are in the catalog as at 16 November 2026.
- RWB-E1-047 is done: the feature flag service serves rwb.p3.temporal, and a flag change is a logged data change.
- RWB-TE-001 is done: the module boundaries and the architecture tests run in the pipeline.
- The Temporal Java SDK version is pinned with the server version approved for RWB-E1-070; the build reads the version from the dependency lock and not from a property.
- A Key Vault key for the payload codec exists, and the SY-CASEWF managed identity has wrap and unwrap rights on that key only.
- LOV-DECISION carries PLATFORM_SMOKE as a system event code with no case, loaded by RW-DATASTEW through the versioned reference load (RWB-E1-043). The decision log writer accepts it under the system event exception, as it accepts the access event codes.
- The clustered ACE Quartz scheduler is available for the daily smoke job (T2); no Temporal Schedule is created.

### 4. Flow

1. Application start: TemporalConfig reads temporal.target, temporal.namespace and temporal.taskqueue.platform through ParameterService; a missing value stops start-up with MSG-P3-032.
2. Application start: TemporalWorkerLifecycle reads rwb.p3.temporal; when it is on, it creates one worker on rwb-platform with the workflow and activity classes and the build ID from the pipeline.
3. Worker: connects to the frontend with its mTLS certificate and polls rwb-platform; when the flag is off, no worker and no poller are created.
4. PdpaPayloadCodec: registers as the data converter on the client and the worker; it encrypts every payload with AES-GCM and the Key Vault key, and it decrypts only inside the worker.
5. WorkflowGateway: starts and signals workflows by workflow ID; a start with an existing workflow ID returns the running execution and does not start a second run.
6. SmokeScheduleJob: Quartz runs daily at 06:00 and calls WorkflowGateway.start("PlatformSmokeWorkflow", "platform-smoke-{yyyymmdd}", input).
7. PlatformSmokeWorkflow: runs one activity; PlatformSmokeActivity writes a decision log entry with decision code PLATFORM_SMOKE through DecisionLogWriter, then returns the worker build ID.
8. Workflow: completes when the activity commits; a failed decision log write fails the activity and the workflow, and the incident reaches RW-PLATADM.
9. Platform administrator: may call POST /admin/workflows/smoke to run the same workflow on demand; the response gives the workflow ID, run ID and status.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The Temporal frontend is unreachable or refuses the connection | WorkflowGateway.start fails; the endpoint returns 503; no workflow, no history and no decision log entry are written | MSG-P3-036 | AC3 |
| X2 | A start uses a workflow ID that is already RUNNING | The running execution is returned; no second run and no second activity | None | AC4 |
| X3 | rwb.p3.temporal is off | No worker is registered and the admin smoke endpoint is not registered; the call returns 404 | None | AC5 |
| X4 | temporal.target has no value for the environment at start-up | The service does not start; the missing parameter and environment are named | MSG-P3-032 | AC6 |
| X5 | A workflow class is placed outside recovery.casewf.workflow | The build fails naming the class and the package rule; the merge is blocked | Build log | AC7 |
| X6 | A role without Platform administration U calls the smoke endpoint | The call is refused with 403; nothing starts | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-071-08 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the cluster of RWB-E1-070, the parameters of RWB-E1-042, the flag of RWB-E1-047 and the module rules of RWB-TE-001; the smoke workflow is self-contained |
| Negotiable | The smoke schedule, build ID format and retry policy are configuration; the codec, the package boundary and the ID conventions are fixed |
| Valuable | Epic 3 starts from a worker that already encrypts payloads, records a decision and survives a restart |
| Estimable | One worker, one codec, one gateway, one smoke workflow and one endpoint |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion in section 7 is one test in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Temporal worker and SDK in the recovery module

  Background:
    Given the worker is built with the Temporal Java SDK version pinned for RWB-E1-070
    Given rwb.p3.temporal is on and the parameters temporal.target, temporal.namespace and temporal.taskqueue.platform have values for SIT

  Scenario: AC1 Smoke workflow completes
    Given the Quartz smoke job runs at 06:00 on 16 November 2026
    When PlatformSmokeWorkflow "platform-smoke-20261116" starts on task queue rwb-platform
    Then the workflow runs one activity and ends COMPLETED within 60 seconds
    Then one decision_log_entry exists with decision code PLATFORM_SMOKE, actor SY-CASEWF and inputsRef "platform-smoke-20261116"
    Then no recovery_case row is created or changed

  Scenario: AC2 History holds encrypted payloads only
    Given the smoke activity input carries the synthetic national ID "1101700203456"
    When the workflow completes
    Then the raw history from the Temporal CLI shows the payload as binary ciphertext with codec metadata
    Then the string "1101700203456" appears nowhere in the history or the worker log
    Then decoding through PdpaPayloadCodec with the Key Vault key returns the input
    Then the worker log holds the workflow ID and no payload

  Scenario: AC3 Temporal unreachable
    Given the Temporal frontend is unreachable on port 7233
    When U-70 calls POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/workflows/smoke
    Then the response is 503 with MSG-P3-036
    Then no workflow execution exists and no decision_log_entry is written
    Then the metric workflow_start_failures_total increases by one

  Scenario: AC4 Duplicate workflow ID
    Given platform-smoke-20261116 is RUNNING
    When U-70 calls the smoke endpoint again with workflow ID platform-smoke-20261116
    Then the response is 200 with the same run ID and status RUNNING
    Then the history holds one WorkflowExecutionStarted event
    Then the activity runs once

  Scenario: AC5 Flag off
    Given rwb.p3.temporal is off in DEV
    When the application starts
    Then no worker is registered on rwb-platform and no poller connection is opened
    When U-70 calls POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/workflows/smoke
    Then the response is 404 and no workflow starts

  Scenario: AC6 Missing parameter at start-up
    Given temporal.target has no value for SIT
    When the application starts in SIT
    Then start-up fails with MSG-P3-032 naming temporal.target and SIT
    Then no worker polls and the health endpoint stays 503

  Scenario: AC7 Workflow class outside the package
    Given a branch adds the class recovery.casewf.smoke.SmokeWorkflowImpl outside recovery.casewf.workflow
    When the build runs WorkflowBoundaryTest
    Then the build fails naming the class and the package rule
    Then the merge is blocked
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Workflow code lives only in recovery.casewf.workflow; activities, gateways and I/O live in recovery.casewf.activities or the owning module, and the boundary test enforces it | D-RCV-36 T7; ADR-011 |
| BR2 | Workflow code is deterministic: no clock, random, I/O, parameter read or direct Drools call; time comes from Workflow.currentTimeMillis or a timer, and all I/O is an activity | D-RCV-36 T7 |
| BR3 | Every payload passes through PdpaPayloadCodec (AES-GCM, key in Azure Key Vault); no clear personal data in history, logs, tests or prompts | D-RCV-36 T1; NFR-045 |
| BR4 | Task queues are rwb-platform for smoke and health in Epic 1; rwb-case and rwb-integration are reserved for Epic 3 and no Epic 1 workflow uses them | D-RCV-36 T1 |
| BR5 | Workflow IDs are platform-smoke-{yyyymmdd} and, from Epic 3, case-{caseId}; a repeated start with the same ID returns the running execution and never starts a second run | D-RCV-36 T1; R-UNI-40 |
| BR6 | Every worker carries the build ID from the pipeline; a worker with an unknown build ID takes no new workflow | D-RCV-36 T1 |
| BR7 | With rwb.p3.temporal off, no worker is registered, no poller is opened and the smoke endpoint returns 404; nothing else changes | D-RCV-36 T1; RWB-E1-047 |
| BR8 | A required parameter with no value stops start-up with MSG-P3-032; the service never substitutes a default for temporal.target, temporal.namespace or temporal.taskqueue.platform | REQ-DRI-010; MSG-P3-032 |
| BR9 | The smoke activity writes its decision log entry through DecisionLogWriter before the workflow completes; a failed write fails the workflow | REQ-DRI-005; RWB-E1-027 |
| BR10 | The smoke workflow reads no case, no ACE view and no business table | D-RCV-35 U1; RWB-TE-001 |
| BR11 | A start that cannot reach the frontend fails with MSG-P3-036 and writes no workflow, no history and no decision log entry | D-RCV-36 T1; REQ-DRI-007 |

### 9. State transitions

None for a case. This story changes the status of the platform smoke workflow only.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Start | Workflow ID not known | RUNNING |
| RUNNING | Activity completes | The decision log entry is committed | COMPLETED |
| RUNNING | Activity fails after its retry policy | No decision log entry is written | FAILED |
| COMPLETED or FAILED | Retention 30 days | The workflow is closed | Removed from visibility; archive is RWB-E2-039 |

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-PLATADM | Runs the smoke workflow on demand, reads the worker health and the history (Platform administration, U) |
| RW-AUDIT | Reads the history and the decision log entry (Platform administration and Decision log, R) |
| RW-SECADM | Reads the codec configuration; decode through the codec server is RWB-E2-038, not this story |
| SY-CASEWF | The worker identity; connects with mTLS and writes the PLATFORM_SMOKE entry (Decision log C) |
| RW-COE | Reads the smoke result as a platform check (Platform administration, R) |
| RW-TRIBE | Builds and deploys the worker through the pipeline; has no PROD endpoint right |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A smoke run is not a credit decision |

### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry | all fields | Write |
| DF-DEC-030 | decision_log_entry | actor_user_id | Write |
| DF-DEC-031 | decision_log_entry | idempotency_key | Write, read |
| DF-REF-028 | lov_value | lov_code | Read |
| DF-REF-029 | lov_value | value_code | Read |

The PLATFORM_SMOKE entry has no case, no rule ID and no version group; it is a system event under the same exception that RWB-E1-027 applies to access events. Its idempotency key is the workflow ID. The parameters temporal.target, temporal.namespace and temporal.taskqueue.platform are read through ParameterService (RWB-E1-042) and add no field. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

### 12. Contract

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/workflows/smoke** (P3 endpoint)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Body optional: { workflowId: string }. Default platform-smoke-{yyyymmdd} in the server time zone |
| Response | 200 WorkflowRun: workflowId, runId, workflowType, status, taskQueue, startedAt |
| Errors | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Platform administration U (MSG-P4-002); 404 flag off; 409 the workflow ID already completed for the day (MSG-GEN-004); 503 Temporal unreachable (MSG-P3-036) |
| Authorization | Platform administration, right U |
| Idempotency | Workflow ID; a repeat while RUNNING returns the running execution, and a repeat after COMPLETED returns 409 with no second run |

**Published interface WorkflowGateway** (package recovery.casewf.workflow, Epic 1):

```java
public interface WorkflowGateway {
    String start(String workflowType, String workflowId, Object input); // returns the run ID; throws WorkflowUnavailableException (MSG-P3-036)
    void signal(String workflowId, String signal, Object payload);
}

public record WorkflowRun(String workflowId, String runId, String workflowType, String status,
                          String taskQueue, Instant startedAt) {}
```

The gateway is the only way a Workbench module starts or signals a workflow. It applies the PdpaPayloadCodec and the workflow ID convention, and it never exposes a Temporal type to a caller.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Worker, codec and gateway in `recovery/casewf/workflow` and `recovery/casewf/activities` (Java packages `recovery.casewf.workflow` and `recovery.casewf.activities`); the endpoint in `recovery/casewf/admin`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TemporalConfig | Configuration | Reads temporal.target, temporal.namespace and temporal.taskqueue.platform through ParameterService; fails start-up with MSG-P3-032 on a missing value |
| TemporalWorkerLifecycle | Service | Starts and stops the worker with rwb.p3.temporal; registers the workflow and activity classes and the build ID |
| PdpaPayloadCodec | Service | AES-GCM payload encryption with the Key Vault key; the only data converter on the client and the worker |
| WorkflowGatewayImpl | Service | Implements the published gateway: start and signal by workflow ID; maps an unreachable frontend to MSG-P3-036 |
| PlatformSmokeWorkflow | Workflow | One activity, then complete; deterministic and free of I/O |
| PlatformSmokeActivity | Activity | Writes the PLATFORM_SMOKE decision log entry and returns the build ID |
| SmokeScheduleJob | Job | Quartz, daily at 06:00, calls WorkflowGateway.start with platform-smoke-{yyyymmdd} |
| WorkerBuildIdProvider | Service | Reads the build ID from the pipeline manifest and refuses to start without it |
| WorkflowAdminController | Controller | POST /admin/workflows/smoke with the access check |
| WorkflowBoundaryTest | Test | Fails the build when a workflow class is outside recovery.casewf.workflow |

**Database.** No new table and no migration. The smoke activity writes decision_log_entry through DecisionLogWriter (RWB-E1-027), in the activity's transaction.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Parameters through RWB-E1-042: temporal.target (host and port), temporal.namespace = rwb-recovery, temporal.taskqueue.platform = rwb-platform, temporal.retention.days = 30.
- Feature flag rwb.p3.temporal through RWB-E1-047.
- Key Vault key name for the codec, one per environment; the key is never in a values file or a test.
- Build ID format `<git-sha>-<build-number>` from the pipeline manifest.

**Build steps**

1. Add the Temporal SDK at the pinned version and the Spring Boot starter; prove the dependency lock holds the version.
2. Build TemporalConfig with the parameter reads and the missing-value failure; test AC6.
3. Build PdpaPayloadCodec and register it on the client and the worker; test AC2 with a synthetic national ID.
4. Build WorkflowGatewayImpl with the ID convention and the unreachable mapping; tests AC3 and AC4.
5. Build PlatformSmokeWorkflow, PlatformSmokeActivity and the decision log write; test AC1.
6. Build SmokeScheduleJob on Quartz and add its job_catalog row through RWB-E1-056.
7. Build the worker lifecycle and the flag check; test AC5.
8. Build the endpoint with the access check; access test.
9. Build WorkflowBoundaryTest and prove it fails on a class outside the package; test AC7.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.temporal`. Off: no worker, no poller, the smoke endpoint returns 404, and no other behaviour changes.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the smoke workflow completes daily in SIT with one decision log entry, and the raw history holds no clear personal data.

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-036 | The workflow service is unreachable or refuses a start | The workflow service is not available. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P3-032 | A required parameter has no value at start-up | Parameter {name} has no value for {environment}. The service did not start. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Platform administration U calls the smoke endpoint | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

MSG-P3-036 is new and is added to Error and Message Standard v4. MSG-P3-032 exists and is reused unchanged.

The platform administrator calls the smoke endpoint and reads the Temporal Web UI; the job monitor of RWB-E1-056 shows the daily smoke job with its last run, status and duration. The smoke run has the states Not run, Running, Completed and Failed. SCR-44 Interface and job monitor shows the same data from Epic 2.
