### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the target, namespace, task queue, retention and flag are parameters.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts: every payload is encrypted; the test national ID is synthetic.
- No read of another module's tables; ACE data only through recovery.v_ace_* views: the smoke workflow reads no case and no ACE row.
- Workflow code is deterministic: no clock, random, I/O or Drools call in workflow code; all I/O is an activity.
- The codec is the only payload path; no clear personal data is written to history, even in DEV.
- No worker without a build ID and no start with a missing parameter.
- No Temporal Schedule and no case wait on Quartz; the smoke job is the only Epic 1 workflow and it has no business wait.

## RWB-E1-072 Drools runtime and rule package store

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-072 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-DRI-07 Run the Drools evaluator on versioned rule packages |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-016, REQ-DRI-001, REQ-DRI-004, REQ-DRI-011 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.3 and 5.7 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | D-RCV-36 (T3, T5, T6, T7); ADR-012 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-044, RWB-E1-043, RWB-E1-027 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the recovery module to evaluate rules with embedded Drools from versioned rule packages held in the database**, so that **every engine uses one evaluator and every decision names the rule and the package version that made it**.

### 2. Business rationale

ADR-012 replaces ADR-004 and keeps its principle that rules are versioned data. The home-built decision-table component has no standard compile check, no first-match guarantee that a reviewer can see and no single place where the version in force is chosen. A rule change in one engine can therefore behave differently from the same rows in another engine, and a decision cannot always name the row and version behind it.

This story adds the Drools runtime and the rule package store to the recovery module: two tables, the three rule_row columns, the rule_test_case link, one KieBase per package version built from the stored DRL, one evaluator that picks the version in force on the evaluation date, one catalog for action text, owner role, timer spec and outputs, and one agenda listener that names the fired rule. It meets REQ-CWC-016 (every event logged with rule ID and version), REQ-DRI-001 (one record per decision), REQ-DRI-004 (Epic 1 records use versioned rules) and REQ-DRI-011 (versioned data with an author and an approver). It follows D-RCV-36 T3 (embedded KIE runtime only), T5 (first match), T6 (rule_row is the catalog) and T7 (a Temporal workflow calls Drools only inside an activity, and the version is chosen at evaluation time). The measure is that every decision log entry in SIT names the rule ID and the package version that made it, with no engine reading the package source.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-044 is done: migrations run with parameterized schema names in every environment.
- RWB-E1-043 is done: the reference data service and the lists the rule rows use are loaded and versioned.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: DecisionLogWriter writes rule ID and rule version, and refuses a rule ID with no version.
- The five Epic 1 package codes are agreed (DL24): ENTRY, EXCLUSION, ALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT and TRANSFER; each has an owner role of RW-COE.
- SCB IT approved the KIE runtime libraries on 16 November 2026: drools-engine, drools-mvel, drools-decisiontables and drools-xml-support. No KIE Server, no Business Central and no KJAR is used.
- Physical Schema v6 is baselined with rule_package and rule_package_version and without payment_match_rule; the table count is 93.
- The parameter drools.kiebase.cache.max = 20 is in the catalog through RWB-E1-042.
- The caller passes facts built from its own module; this story reads no case table.

### 4. Flow

1. Deployment: Flyway migration V072_1__rule_package.sql creates rule_package and rule_package_version, adds DF-REF-296 to DF-REF-298 to rule_row and DF-REF-299 to rule_test_case, and seeds the five Epic 1 package codes.
2. Caller (for example the allocation engine): builds the facts object from its own data and calls RuleEvaluator.evaluate("ALLOCATION", facts, businessDate).
3. RuleEvaluatorImpl: reads the versions of ALLOCATION and selects the one with status IN_FORCE and valid_from <= businessDate <= valid_to.
4. RuleEvaluatorImpl: asks KieBaseRegistry for the KieBase of that package version.
5. KieBaseRegistry: on a cache miss, recomputes the SHA-256 of drl_source, compares it with rule_package_version.checksum and compiles the DRL into a KieBase; on a mismatch it refuses the version, raises an incident and does not cache it.
6. RuleEvaluatorImpl: inserts the facts, fires the package, and the agenda listener records the Drools rule name of the one rule that fired.
7. RuleEvaluatorImpl: returns one RuleResult with packageCode, packageVersion, ruleId and outputs.
8. Caller: writes the decision log entry through DecisionLogWriter with ruleId and ruleVersion from the result, then applies the action.
9. RuleCatalog: serves action_text, owner_role, timer_spec and outputs of a row by rule ID and package version from rule_row, for callers that need the catalog text rather than an evaluation.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No version of the package is IN_FORCE on the evaluation date | NoPackageInForce is thrown; the caller refuses the action and writes no decision log entry | MSG-P3-027 | AC3 |
| X2 | The recomputed SHA-256 of drl_source differs from rule_package_version.checksum | The version is refused at load into the cache; an incident is raised; the previous version continues to serve | MSG-P3-027 | AC6 |
| X3 | A role without Rules and parameters R calls GET /admin/rule-packages | The call is refused with 403; no package data is returned | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-072-08 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the schema of RWB-E1-044, the lists of RWB-E1-043 and the writer of RWB-E1-027; it holds the runtime and the store only |
| Negotiable | The cache size, the seed titles and the incident route are configuration; the first-match rule and the checksum rule are fixed |
| Valuable | Every engine and the test runner decide by the same evaluator and name the same rule and package version |
| Estimable | Two tables, three rule_row columns, one registry, one evaluator, one catalog and one endpoint |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion in section 7 is one test in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Drools runtime and rule package store

  Background:
    Given package ALLOCATION version "ALLOC-2026.12" is in force with 26 rows
    Given the parameter drools.kiebase.cache.max is 20

  Scenario: AC1 Evaluation returns the rule and the package version
    Given a mortgage case in region BKK with exposure band 3
    When SY-RULES calls RuleEvaluator.evaluate("ALLOCATION", facts, 2026-12-15)
    Then the result holds packageCode "ALLOCATION", packageVersion "ALLOC-2026.12" and ruleId "ALLOC-031"
    Then the outputs hold targetQueueCode "MTG-BKK-CO"
    Then the decision log entry carries rule ID "ALLOC-031" and rule version "ALLOC-2026.12"

  Scenario: AC2 The date picks the right version
    Given version "ALLOC-2026.11" is valid from 2026-11-01 to 2026-12-14
    Given version "ALLOC-2026.12" is valid from 2026-12-15
    When the same facts are evaluated on 2026-12-14
    Then the result carries packageVersion "ALLOC-2026.11"
    When the same facts are evaluated on 2026-12-15
    Then the result carries packageVersion "ALLOC-2026.12"
    Then the evaluation date comes from the caller and not from the system clock

  Scenario: AC3 No version in force
    Given no ALLOCATION version is IN_FORCE on 2026-12-20
    When SY-RULES evaluates a case for that date
    Then NoPackageInForce is thrown with MSG-P3-027 for the package in force check
    Then no decision log entry is written and the case is not moved

  Scenario: AC4 Exactly one rule fires
    Given rows "ALLOC-031" and "ALLOC-032" both match the facts
    Given both rows share the activation-group ALLOCATION
    When the package fires
    Then exactly one rule fires, "ALLOC-031", with the salience from its row order
    Then the result holds one rule ID and no output of "ALLOC-032"
    When the same facts are evaluated 100 times
    Then "ALLOC-031" is the only rule that fires every time

  Scenario: AC5 The cache is reused
    Given version "ALLOC-2026.12" is not in the cache
    When the evaluator runs twice with the same package version
    Then the KieBase is built once and the second call reads the cache
    Then the counter drools_kiebase_builds_total increases by one only
    Then the cache holds no more than 20 KieBases

  Scenario: AC6 Checksum mismatch
    Given the recomputed SHA-256 of drl_source for "ALLOC-2026.13" differs from its checksum
    When the cache builds that version
    Then the version is refused at load into the cache with MSG-P3-027 for the checksum check
    Then no evaluation uses the version and an incident is raised to RW-PLATADM
    Then version "ALLOC-2026.12" stays in force and serves every evaluation

  Scenario: AC7 The catalog returns the row fields
    Given row "ALLOC-031" of version "ALLOC-2026.12" has action_text "Assign to MTG-BKK-CO", owner_role "RW-CASEOWN", timer_spec "3d" and outputs {"targetQueueCode":"MTG-BKK-CO"}
    When RuleCatalog.row("ALLOC-031", "ALLOC-2026.12") is called
    Then it returns action_text, owner_role, timer_spec and outputs
    Then the read touches rule_row only and not the workbook or drl_source
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One evaluator, RuleEvaluator, serves every engine and the test runner; no engine reads drl_source, the workbook or rule_row directly | D-RCV-36 T3, T6; ADR-012 |
| BR2 | First match (T5): the RuleSet of a decision table is the package code, each row is one rule whose NAME is the rule ID, all rows share one activation-group, salience comes from row order and the default row is last; exactly one row decides | D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR3 | The package version is chosen at evaluation time from the caller's date and the valid_from and valid_to dates, returned in the result and written to the decision log | D-RCV-36 T7 |
| BR4 | A rule package version is never edited in place; every change is a new version row, and rollback moves the pointer | D-RCV-36 T4; R-UNI-38 |
| BR5 | Open cases keep the version they were decided under; a later evaluation may use the version then in force | R-UNI-38 |
| BR6 | rule_row is the rule catalog: action_text, owner_role, timer_spec and outputs are read by rule ID and package version, and no caller reads the package source | D-RCV-36 T6 |
| BR7 | A KieBase is built once per package version and cached; the cache is bounded by drools.kiebase.cache.max and evicts the least recently used version | D-RCV-36 T3; REQ-DRI-010 |
| BR8 | A checksum mismatch refuses the version and raises an incident; the evaluator never falls back to an earlier version without a decision | D-RCV-36 T4 |
| BR9 | No package in force is a refusal (NoPackageInForce), never a default decision | R-UNI-41; REQ-CWC-008 |
| BR10 | The decision log records rule ID = Drools rule name and rule version = package version label, with no schema change to decision_log_entry | D-RCV-36 T5; REQ-CWC-016 |
| BR11 | Temporal workflow code never calls RuleEvaluator; a workflow reaches Drools only through an activity | D-RCV-36 T7 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status and no rule package version status; it reads IN_FORCE versions and serves them. The status domain is shared with RWB-E1-073:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Load | Every check passes | LOADED; RWB-E1-073 |
| None | Load | Any check fails | REFUSED; RWB-E1-073 |
| LOADED | Approve | Approver is not the author | APPROVED; RWB-E1-073 |
| APPROVED | RULE_PACKAGE_EFFECTIVE | Valid from reached | IN_FORCE; previous SUPERSEDED |
| IN_FORCE | Rollback | Earlier version exists | ROLLED_BACK; previous IN_FORCE; RWB-E1-073 |

| RW-COE | Reads packages, versions and the catalog (Rules and parameters R) |

| RW-REFADM | Reads the package list; may not change a version |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A rule evaluation is not a credit decision |

| DF-REF-299 | rule_test_case | package_version_id | Create (migration), read |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 | rule_row | all rule fields | Read |
| DF-REF-052 to DF-REF-054 | rule_row | rule_table, row_order, target_queue_code | Read |

The migration creates the two tables and the four columns and seeds five rule_package rows; it writes no rule_package_version and no rule_row at run time. rule_row is read only through RuleCatalog. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model, Data Dictionary and Physical Schema v6.

### 12. Contract

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-packages** (P3/P4 endpoint; the tables are P4, the evaluator is P3)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query: packageCode (optional), status (optional; IN_FORCE by default) |
| Response | 200 RulePackage[]: packageCode, title, ownerRole, hitPolicy and versionInForce with versionId, versionLabel, validFrom, checksum; versionInForce is null when no version is in force |
| Errors | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Rules and parameters R (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown packageCode; 503 |
| Authorization | Rules and parameters, right R |
| Idempotency | Read only |

**Published interfaces** (package recovery.casewf.rules):

```java
public interface RuleEvaluator {
    RuleResult evaluate(String packageCode, Object facts, LocalDate onDate); // throws NoPackageInForce
}

public record RuleResult(String packageCode, String packageVersion, String ruleId, Map<String, Object> outputs) {}

public interface RuleCatalog {
    RuleRow row(String ruleId, String packageVersion);
}

public record RuleRow(String ruleId, String packageVersion, String actionText, String ownerRole,
                      String timerSpec, Map<String, Object> outputs) {}
```

`NoPackageInForce` is a checked exception with messageId MSG-P3-027 and the package code. RuleRow is the catalog projection of DF-REF-008, DF-REF-010, DF-REF-011 and DF-REF-298. No caller receives a KieBase, a KieSession or a Drools type.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Runtime, evaluator and catalog in `recovery/casewf/rules` (Java package `recovery.casewf.rules`); the tables are owned by the P4 package `recovery.accessadmin.rulepackages` and exposed through the published interfaces.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RulePackageRepository | Repository | Reads rule_package and rule_package_version; selects the version in force for a package and a date |
| KieBaseRegistry | Service | Builds a KieBase from drl_source once per version, verifies the checksum, caches up to drools.kiebase.cache.max and evicts the least recently used |
| RuleEvaluatorImpl | Service | Implements the published evaluator: version selection, fact insertion, fire, one RuleResult; maps no version to NoPackageInForce |
| RuleCatalogImpl | Service | Implements the published catalog: reads rule_row only and returns the catalog projection |
| DecisionLogAgendaListener | Listener | Captures the Drools rule name of the fired rule and hands it to the evaluator |
| NoPackageInForce | Exception | The checked refusal with messageId MSG-P3-027 |
| RulePackageController | Controller | GET /admin/rule-packages with the access check |
| V072_1__rule_package.sql | Migration | Creates the tables, adds the four columns and seeds the five package codes |

**Database**

- V072_1__rule_package.sql creates rule_package (id, package_code unique, title, owner_role, hit_policy, standard columns) and rule_package_version (id, package_id, version_label, status, source_blob_ref, drl_source, checksum, valid_from, valid_to, author, approver, loaded_at, approved_at, test_result, dry_run_counts jsonb, rollback_of, change_checklist jsonb, standard columns; unique (package_id, version_label); index (status, valid_from)).
- The same migration adds package_version_id, drools_rule_name and outputs jsonb to rule_row, and package_version_id to rule_test_case.
- It seeds ENTRY, EXCLUSION, ALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT and TRANSFER with owner_role RW-COE and hit_policy FIRST_MATCH, and changes nothing on a second run.
- Physical Schema v6 counts 93 tables: 92 + rule_package + rule_package_version - payment_match_rule. Temporal's own tables are not in the Physical Schema.

**Configuration and reference data**

- drools.kiebase.cache.max = 20 through RWB-E1-042.
- The five package codes and their titles, seeded by the migration and owned by RW-COE.
- The KIE runtime dependency lock: drools-engine, drools-mvel, drools-decisiontables and drools-xml-support only.

**Build steps**

1. Write V072_1 and the entities and repositories; test the table count, the unique constraint and the seed idempotence.
2. Build KieBaseRegistry with checksum verification and the bounded cache; tests AC5 and AC6.
3. Build RuleEvaluatorImpl with version selection by date; tests AC1, AC2 and AC3.
4. Add the agenda listener; test AC4 with two matching rows.
5. Build RuleCatalogImpl over rule_row; test AC7.
6. Wire DecisionLogWriter into the caller path; test that the entry carries the rule ID and package version.
7. Build GET /admin/rule-packages with the access check; access test.
8. Measure the first and the cached evaluation in SIT and record the result in the release evidence.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.drools`. Off: GET /admin/rule-packages returns 404 and the module builds no KieBase; the Epic 1 engines are not enabled in that environment. The flag is on in SIT, UAT and PROD.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and the five Epic 1 packages evaluate in SIT with the rule ID and package version on every decision log entry.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-027 | No version is in force or a checksum mismatch refuses a version | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Rules and parameters R calls the package list | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

For a checksum mismatch, {check} is "checksum" and {detail} names the package code and version label only, never the DRL or a payload.

### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. Packages and versions are read through GET /admin/rule-packages; SCR-39 Rules and parameters shows the same data from Epic 8. The operability view is the service metric drools_kiebase_builds_total and the incident for a checksum mismatch.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: packages, rows, salience, conditions and outputs are data in the database and the workbook.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts: facts are codes and numbers, and the result holds codes only.
- No read of another module's tables; ACE data only through recovery.v_ace_* views: the evaluator receives facts from the caller and reads no case or ACE table.
- A Temporal workflow calls Drools only inside an activity; no workflow class calls RuleEvaluator (T7).
- No cache of a version whose checksum fails, and no silent fallback to an earlier version.
- No second evaluator: every engine and the test runner calls RuleEvaluator, and no engine reads drl_source.
- No edit of a package version in place; a correction is a new version.

## RWB-E1-073 Rule authoring, validation, test scenarios, approval and rollback in Drools

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-073 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-14 Load a rule package version with validation; FEAT-CWC-15 Roll back a rule package version; FEAT-DRI-07 Run the Drools evaluator on versioned rule packages |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-013, REQ-CWC-014, REQ-DRI-004, REQ-CWC-008 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.3 and 5.7 |
| L3 process | 14 Set strategy, policy and decision rules; All recovery processes |
| Decision | D-RCV-36 (T3, T4, T5, T8, T10); ADR-012 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-072, RWB-E1-042 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **an Excel template in Drools decision-table format for each rule package, checks and scenarios on upload, approval by Risk, a dated start and rollback by one call**, so that **a rule change goes from template to production without a code release**.

### 2. Business rationale

Collection and recovery rules live in procedure documents today, and audit found the procedure not followed because the rules were not in the system (CTL-08). RWB-E1-029 proved the pattern for a home-built table component; this story carries the same control to Drools, where the workbook is the source of the decision table and the engine compiles it. A bad row can move every case that reaches it, so a load must be refused whole, a scenario must fail the build, and a rollback must take one call.

This story meets REQ-CWC-013 (validated load with a version, no release, rollback by one call), REQ-CWC-014 (schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row and scenario checks), REQ-DRI-004 (Epic 1 records use versioned rules) and REQ-CWC-008 (the allocation package always has a default row). It follows D-RCV-36 T3 (embedded KIE runtime only), T4 (workbook to KieBase to approved version in force, rollback by one call), T5 (first match) and T8 (this key replaces RWB-E1-029 and RWB-TE-005). The measure is that every version in force has a passing scenario set and a checksum, and that a wrong version leaves production in one call.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-072 is done: rule_package, rule_package_version, the rule_row and rule_test_case columns, RuleEvaluator, RuleCatalog and the KieBase cache exist.
- RWB-E1-042 is done: rules.testcases.min = 50 (assumed) and drools.kiebase.cache.max = 20 are in the catalog; the values are served through ParameterService as at 16 November 2026.
- The Drools XLS template is agreed on 16 November 2026: one workbook per package, a Rows tab and a Tests tab, RuleSet = package code, one row per rule with NAME = rule ID, and the default row last.
- Each Epic 1 package has at least 50 scenarios with expected queue or outcome, prepared by RW-COE in the Tests tab.
- RW-COE holds Rules and parameters C; RW-RISK holds Rules and parameters A; one person may not hold both (separation of duty).
- Open cases exist for the dry run, created by RWB-E1-018 in SIT and UAT.
- The Blob container rule-packages exists, and the recovery module identity has write and read rights on that container only.
- The build pipeline can run RuleScenarioBuildGate after the unit tests, and the release manifest `config/rule-packages.lock` lists the package code and version label in force for each environment.
- A job_catalog row for RulePackageEffectiveDateJob exists through RWB-E1-056, with owner RW-COE and schedule 00:01.

### 4. Flow

1. RW-COE: fills the package workbook (Rows and Tests tabs) for package ALLOCATION, version "ALLOC-2026.12", valid from 2026-12-15.
2. RW-COE: calls POST /admin/rule-packages/ALLOCATION/versions with the file and valid from.
3. RuleWorkbookParser: reads the Rows and Tests tabs, keeps row numbers and the version label, and generates the DRL.
4. DroolsCompileCheck: compiles the generated DRL; a compile error refuses the load and names the row and cell.
5. RuleLoadValidator: runs the schema check against the lists, then overlap, unreachable rows and the default row for ALLOCATION.
6. RuleScenarioRunner: runs at least rules.testcases.min scenarios (50) from the Tests tab through RuleEvaluator and compares each result with the expected queue or outcome.
7. RuleDryRun: evaluates the draft against every open case and counts the cases whose result would change, by product, queue and rule.
8. RulePackageVersionService: on any failed check, refuses the load whole and names every failed row, cell or scenario; on success stores the version LOADED with the workbook in Blob (source_blob_ref), the DRL, the checksum, the test result and the dry run counts, and writes the change log entry.
9. RW-RISK: approves through POST /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve; the call is refused if the approver is the author.
10. RulePackageEffectiveDateJob: at 00:01 on the valid from date moves the APPROVED version to IN_FORCE and the previous version to SUPERSEDED in one transaction; new decisions use it and open cases keep the version they were decided under (R-UNI-38).
11. RW-COE: if the version is wrong, calls POST /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/rollback; the previous version is in force again in one transaction and the change log records the rollback.
12. Build: RuleScenarioBuildGate runs every in-force package's scenarios from the release manifest on every build and fails the build when a scenario fails.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Two rows match the same case at the same row order | Load refused; both row IDs named | MSG-P3-027 | AC2 |
| X2 | A scenario result differs from the expected result | Load refused; failing scenario IDs named | MSG-P3-027 | AC3 |
| X3 | A required column is missing or a value is outside its list | Load refused; row and column named | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X4 | A row can never match because an earlier row covers it | Load refused; row named | MSG-P3-027 | AC6 |
| X5 | The allocation package has no default row | Load refused | MSG-P3-027 | AC7 |
| X6 | The approver is the author | Approval refused; the version stays LOADED | MSG-P7-002 | AC8 |
| X7 | Rollback with no earlier version | Refused; the version stays in force | MSG-P3-015 | AC9 |
| X8 | The same package code and version label are loaded twice | Refused with 409 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC10 |
| X9 | Valid from before today | Refused with 422 | MSG-GEN-003 | AC11 |
| X10 | An empty file | Refused with 422 | MSG-GEN-001 | AC12 |
| X11 | A role without Rules and parameters C loads a file | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-073-16 |
| X12 | The generated DRL does not compile | Load refused; row and cell named; no version row and no Blob object | MSG-P3-027 | AC13 |
| X13 | A scenario of an in-force package fails in the pipeline | The build fails; the merge is blocked | MSG-P3-027 | AC14 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Works on the package tables of RWB-E1-072 and the parameters of RWB-E1-042; it adds the authoring path and does not change the evaluator |
| Negotiable | The checks are fixed; the rows, scenarios, package codes and version labels are data |
| Valuable | A rule change takes a load, an approval and a dated start instead of a release, and a wrong version leaves in one call |
| Estimable | One parser, one compile check, one validator, one scenario runner, one dry run, one service, five endpoints and one build gate |
| Small | Fits three weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 is one test in section 16 |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Rule authoring, validation, scenarios, approval and rollback in Drools

  Background:
    Given the loader U-41 holds RW-COE and the approver U-51 holds RW-RISK
    Given package ALLOCATION version "ALLOC-2026.11" is in force with 24 rows

  Scenario: AC1 Valid load
    Given a workbook for package ALLOCATION version "ALLOC-2026.12" with 26 rows and 50 scenarios that pass every check
    When U-41 loads it with valid from 2026-12-15 and U-51 approves it
    Then version "ALLOC-2026.12" is in force from 2026-12-15
    Then the change log records author U-41, approver U-51, the load and approval times, the workbook checksum, "50 of 50 scenarios passed" and the dry run count

  Scenario: AC2 Overlap refused
    Given rows "ALLOC-031" and "ALLOC-032" both match product group "MORTGAGE" and region "BKK" at row order 12
    When validation runs
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 for the overlap check naming "ALLOC-031" and "ALLOC-032"
    Then version "ALLOC-2026.11" stays in force

  Scenario: AC3 Scenarios
    Given the 50 scenarios with expected queues
    Given scenarios "TA-07" and "TA-19" expect queue "MTG-BKK-CO" and the new rows return "MTG-CEN-CO"
    When validation runs
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 for the scenario check naming "TA-07" and "TA-19"

  Scenario: AC4 Rollback
    Given version 7, "ALLOC-2026.13", is in force and version 6, "ALLOC-2026.12", was in force before it
    When U-41 calls rollback once for version 7
    Then version 6 is in force
    Then the change log holds the rollback with U-41, the time and the reason
    Then a case allocated under version 7 keeps rule version "ALLOC-2026.13" on its decision log entry

  Scenario: AC5 Schema error
    Given row 9 has assignment reason "QUICK" that is not in its list
    When validation runs
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 for the schema check naming row 9 and its column

  Scenario: AC6 Unreachable row
    Given row "ALLOC-040" matches product group "SSME" in any region at row order 5
    Given row "ALLOC-041" matches product group "SSME" and region "NE3" at row order 6
    When validation runs
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 for the unreachable row check naming "ALLOC-041"

  Scenario: AC7 Missing default
    Given the allocation rows have no last row that matches every case
    When validation runs
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 for the default row check

  Scenario: AC8 Author cannot approve
    Given U-41 loaded version "ALLOC-2026.12"
    When U-41 calls approve
    Then the system refuses the call with MSG-P7-002
    Then the version stays LOADED

  Scenario: AC9 Rollback with no earlier version
    Given package TRANSFER has only version "TRF-2026.11"
    When rollback is called for "TRF-2026.11"
    Then the system refuses the call with MSG-P3-015
    Then "TRF-2026.11" stays in force

  Scenario: AC10 Same version loaded twice
    Given version "ALLOC-2026.12" of package ALLOCATION is loaded
    When a file with version label "ALLOC-2026.12" for package ALLOCATION is loaded again
    Then the system refuses the load with 409 and MSG-GEN-004

  Scenario: AC11 Valid from in the past
    When U-41 loads version "ALLOC-2026.14" with valid from 2026-11-01 on 2026-12-10
    Then the system refuses the load with 422 and MSG-GEN-003 for valid from

  Scenario: AC12 Empty file
    When U-41 loads a template with no rows
    Then the system refuses the load with 422 and MSG-GEN-001 for rows

  Scenario: AC13 Compile error
    Given the workbook for package ALLOCATION version "ALLOC-2026.14" has the condition cell "exposure_band >= " with no value at row 14
    When U-41 loads it
    Then DroolsCompileCheck fails and the load is refused with MSG-P3-027 for the compile check naming row 14 and the cell
    Then no rule_package_version row is written and no Blob object is stored
    Then version "ALLOC-2026.13" stays in force

  Scenario: AC14 Build gate fails on a scenario
    Given package ALLOCATION version "ALLOC-2026.13" is in force with 50 scenarios
    Given a build changes the case fact mapping so that scenario "TA-07" returns "MTG-CEN-CO" instead of "MTG-BKK-CO"
    When RuleScenarioBuildGate runs in the pipeline
    Then the build fails with MSG-P3-027 for the scenario check naming "TA-07" and version "ALLOC-2026.13"
    Then the merge is blocked

  Scenario: AC15 Change log records the checksum
    Given the workbook file "ALLOCATION-2026.12.xlsx" for package ALLOCATION version "ALLOC-2026.12"
    When U-41 loads it and the load succeeds
    Then the change log entry holds the SHA-256 checksum "9f2c...e1b4" of the workbook
    Then the same checksum is on rule_package_version.checksum and in the Blob object metadata
    Then a later download of the workbook gives the same checksum
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A package version passes the Drools compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row and scenario checks before it is stored; the dry run is recorded for the approver | REQ-CWC-014; D-RCV-36 T4 |
| BR2 | A load with any failed check is refused in full | Reference data change process, step 3; CTL-08 |
| BR3 | First match: RuleSet = package code, each row is one rule with NAME = rule ID, rows share one activation-group, salience comes from row order and the default row is last; exactly one row decides | D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR4 | The allocation package always has a default row | REQ-CWC-008 |
| BR5 | A version takes effect on its valid from date after approval; open cases keep the version they were decided under | R-UNI-38 |
| BR6 | The author cannot approve; RW-RISK signs rule package changes | Separation of duty table; CTL-08 |
| BR7 | Rollback returns the previous version in one call and one transaction | REQ-CWC-013; FEAT-CWC-15 |
| BR8 | Every load, approval and rollback is in the change log with author, approver, time, checksum and test result | REQ-CWC-013; FSD A2.14 |
| BR9 | The template is the Drools XLS decision-table format, one workbook per package, with Rows and Tests tabs; the generated DRL is stored with the workbook | D-RCV-36 T3, T4 |
| BR10 | A load carries at least rules.testcases.min scenarios (50, assumed) from the Tests tab, and every scenario runs through the same RuleEvaluator as production | REQ-CWC-014; D-RCV-36 T4 |
| BR11 | Every in-force package's scenarios run in every build through RuleScenarioBuildGate, and a failing scenario fails the build | D-RCV-36 T4; REQ-CWC-014 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status. It changes the status of a rule package version: LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Load | Every check passes | LOADED |
| None | Load | Any check fails, including the compile | REFUSED |
| LOADED | Approve | Approver is not the author | APPROVED |
| APPROVED | RULE_PACKAGE_EFFECTIVE (00:01 job) | Valid from reached | IN_FORCE; previous SUPERSEDED |
| IN_FORCE | Rollback | Earlier version exists | ROLLED_BACK; previous IN_FORCE |

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-COE | Loads a package version and calls rollback (Rules and parameters CRUD) |
| RW-RISK | Approves a version (Rules and parameters A); may not hold RW-COE |
| RW-AUDIT | Reads versions, scenarios, dry run counts and the change log (Rules and parameters R) |
| RW-REFADM | Prepares load files; may not approve |
| SY-RULES | Evaluates the draft and the version in force for scenarios and the dry run |
| SY-CASEWF | Applies the approved decision; no endpoint right |
| RW-TRIBE | Builds and runs RuleScenarioBuildGate; no PROD data in the build |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A rule package version is not a credit decision |

| DF-CAS-015 | recovery_case | exposure_band | Read |
| DF-CAS-019 | recovery_case | deviation_open | Read |

The load writes rule_row and rule_test_case through the package version id, and the case fields are read only through the P3 repository for the dry run. The change log of a version is its rule_package_version header; RWB-E2-041 reports it for audit. Lists used by the schema check are read through the P4 list interface. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

### 12. Contract

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions** (P4 endpoint)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: file (xlsx workbook with Rows and Tests), validFrom (date). The version label is a cell in the workbook |
| Response | 201 RulePackageVersion: versionId, packageCode, versionLabel, status LOADED, validFrom, validTo, author, checksum, testResult {total, passed, failed, failedScenarioIds}, dryRunCounts {openCases, changedCases, byProduct, byQueue} |
| Errors | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Rules and parameters C (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown package code; 409 version label exists (MSG-GEN-004); 422 a check failed (MSG-P3-027, with the check, rows, cells and scenario IDs in Problem.detail), empty file (MSG-GEN-001), date order (MSG-GEN-003); 503 |
| Authorization | Rules and parameters, right C |
| Idempotency | Package code and version label; a repeat is refused with 409 |

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query: status (optional) |
| Response | 200 RulePackageVersion[] with versionId, versionLabel, status, validFrom, validTo, author, approver, checksum, testResult, dryRunCounts |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Rules and parameters R; 404 unknown package code; 503 |
| Authorization | Rules and parameters, right R |
| Idempotency | Read only |

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | None |
| Response | 200 RulePackageVersion with status APPROVED, approver and approvedAt |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Rules and parameters A (MSG-P4-002); 404; 409 approver is the author (MSG-P7-002) or version not LOADED (MSG-GEN-004); 503 |
| Authorization | Rules and parameters, right A |
| Idempotency | Version ID; a repeat is refused with 409 and no second approval |

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/rollback**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Body { reason: string, required } |
| Response | 200 RulePackageVersion of the version now in force |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Rules and parameters U (MSG-P4-002); 404; 409 no earlier version (MSG-P3-015) or version not IN_FORCE; 422 no reason (MSG-GEN-001); 503 |
| Authorization | Rules and parameters, right U |
| Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header |

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/dry-run**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query: onDate (optional; default today) |
| Response | 200 DryRunReport: packageCode, versionLabel, evaluatedAt, openCases, changedCases, byProduct, byQueue, byRule |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Rules and parameters R; 404; 409 the version is REFUSED or a check failed and no report exists; 503 |
| Authorization | Rules and parameters, right R |
| Idempotency | Read only |

The load path, the scenario runner and the dry run call the published RuleEvaluator and RuleCatalog of RWB-E1-072. This story adds no published interface and no Drools type to a caller.

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Authoring, checks and scenarios in `recovery/casewf/rules` (Java package `recovery.casewf.rules`); endpoints and the package version writes in the P4 package `recovery.accessadmin.rulepackages`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RuleWorkbookParser | Service | Reads the Rows and Tests tabs, keeps row numbers, reads the version label and generates the DRL |
| DroolsCompileCheck | Service | Compiles the generated DRL and reports the row and cell of a compile error |
| RuleLoadValidator | Service | Schema, overlap, unreachable row and default row checks |
| RuleScenarioRunner | Service | Runs at least rules.testcases.min scenarios through RuleEvaluator and compares each expected result |
| RuleDryRun | Service | Counts open cases whose result changes, by product, queue and rule; reads case fields through the P3 repository |
| RulePackageVersionService | Service | Stores the version LOADED with the Blob workbook, DRL, checksum, test result and dry run counts; approval check; effective date; rollback in one transaction; change log |
| RulePackageController | Controller | The five endpoints of section 12 |
| RulePackageEffectiveDateJob | Job | Quartz at 00:01 moves APPROVED versions with today's valid from to IN_FORCE and the previous to SUPERSEDED |
| RuleScenarioBuildGate | Build gate | Loads the in-force package versions from `config/rule-packages.lock` into a Testcontainers database and runs every scenario through RuleEvaluator |

**Database and Blob**

- No new table and no migration: V072_1 of RWB-E1-072 created rule_package, rule_package_version and the four columns.
- The load writes rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case in one transaction; the rollback updates two version rows in one transaction.
- Blob container rule-packages, path `{packageCode}/{versionLabel}.xlsx`, versioning on; the object is write-once and the checksum is in the object metadata and DF-REF-285.

**Configuration and reference data**

- rules.testcases.min = 50 (assumed) through RWB-E1-042.
- drools.kiebase.cache.max = 20 through RWB-E1-042.
- The Drools XLS template, owned by RW-COE, with Rows and Tests tabs.
- `config/rule-packages.lock`, generated at release, lists package code and version label in force per environment for the build gate.

**Build steps**

1. RuleWorkbookParser; unit tests with a valid file, an empty file and a missing Tests tab (AC1, AC12).
2. DroolsCompileCheck; test a condition cell with no value (AC13).
3. Schema check against the lists; test AC5.
4. Overlap and unreachable row checks on the condition columns; tests AC2 and AC6.
5. Default row check for ALLOCATION; test AC7.
6. RuleScenarioRunner through RuleEvaluator; test AC3.
7. RuleDryRun with counts by product, queue and rule in the change log.
8. RulePackageVersionService: store, Blob, checksum, approve with the author check, effective date job, rollback; tests AC1, AC4, AC8, AC9, AC10, AC11 and AC15.
9. Endpoints with access checks; access tests TC-E1-073-16 to TC-E1-073-20.
10. RuleScenarioBuildGate and the lock manifest; test AC14.
11. Run the five Epic 1 packages through load, approval, effective date and rollback in SIT.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.drools`. Off: the five endpoints return 404 and RulePackageEffectiveDateJob does not run; no version changes state and nothing else changes.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the five Epic 1 packages load, approve, take effect and roll back in SIT, and the build gate runs 250 scenarios (five packages of 50).

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-027 | A package version check fails | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P3-015 | Rollback with no earlier version | There is no earlier version of {table} to return to. |
| MSG-P7-002 | Approver is the author | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Empty file or no rollback reason | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Valid from before today | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Version label already loaded, or version not LOADED | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value is compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row or scenario. The {detail} names the row IDs, cells or scenario IDs only, never a case fact or a person. For MSG-P3-015 the {table} value is the package code in this story.

### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. Rule packages are loaded by file and read through GET /admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions; SCR-39 Rules and parameters comes in Epic 8 ("by file load before"). The version states LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK and REFUSED are shown in the version list. The rule change audit report is RWB-E2-041.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: rows, conditions, target queues, scenarios and the test count are data.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts: scenarios use synthetic case facts and the dry run reports counts only.
- No read of another module's tables; ACE data only through recovery.v_ace_* views: the dry run reads case fields through the P3 repository.
- One evaluator for the load checks, the scenarios, the dry run and production; no check uses a second engine.
- The approver is never the author; the service checks it, not only the screen.
- An in-force package version is never edited; rollback moves the pointer and writes the reason.
- The build gate reads a release manifest and a Testcontainers database; it never connects to SIT, UAT or PROD and never writes a live database.

## RWB-TE-001 Recovery module folder and boundary test

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-TE-001 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P2 Integration |
| Feature | None |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-006 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Program, section 7 (constraint Modular monolith) and section 5.2 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | DL05 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | None |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **the recovery module folder and packages in the ACE repository with a build-time boundary test**, so that **no module calls the inside of another module and no recovery code calls a system of record directly**.

### 2. Business rationale

Three teams build in one ACE service. Without a checked boundary, a change in one team's code breaks another's, and a direct call to a core system could bypass the COLLINS and file load path. The skeleton gives each Workbench module one package with a published part and an internal part, and a test in every build refuses a call into another module's internal part, a cross-module table read and a direct system call outside the integration adapters. It meets REQ-DRI-006 and applies DT08, ADR-002 and DL05 (option B from 2 November: TechX creates the recovery module in its own package). The measure is the count of boundary violations merged to main, which must stay at zero.

### 3. Preconditions

- Access to the ACE repository for the TechX squads (DL36).
- DL05 is applied as option B from 2 November 2026: TechX creates the recovery module in its own package; the ACE team applies the module boundaries for the common and collection modules later.
- The common module's published packages are named in the module map. Until the ACE team names them, the map lists `..common.api..` (assumed; DL05).
- The ACE build runs the unit test phase on every pull request.

### 4. Flow

1. Squad member: creates the recovery folders and packages for the 19 Workbench modules, each with an `api` package and an `internal` package.
2. Squad member: writes the module map `architecture/recovery-modules.yaml` with each module code, its package and its published packages.
3. Squad member: writes RecoveryBoundaryTest with the rules BR1 to BR5, reading the module map.
4. Squad member: writes the front end boundary rules for `src/modules/recovery`.
5. Squad member: wires the common module access check for `/api/recovery/v1/**` through RecoveryAccessGuard.
6. Pipeline: on each pull request runs the back end tests, including RecoveryBoundaryTest, and the front end dependency check.
7. Pipeline: fails the build when a rule is broken and prints the rule, the class and the class it depends on.
8. Squad member: fixes the call by going through the other module's `api` package or an application event, and the build passes.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A recovery class imports a collection module internal class | Build fails with the rule and both class names | Build log: boundary rule BND-1 broken | AC1 |
| X2 | A recovery module class imports another recovery module's internal class | Build fails | Build log: boundary rule BND-3 broken | AC3 |
| X3 | A class uses another module's entity or repository | Build fails | Build log: boundary rule BND-4 broken | AC4 |
| X4 | A class outside the integration adapters uses an HTTP or SFTP client | Build fails | Build log: boundary rule BND-5 broken | AC5 |
| X5 | A recovery screen imports a collection screen | Front end build fails | Build log: rule no-collection-import broken | AC6 |
| X6 | A new package is not in the module map | Build fails | Build log: package not in module map | AC7 |
| X7 | A request reaches a recovery endpoint from a role without the right | 403 through the common module access check | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-TE-001-08 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only repository access; every later story builds inside these folders |
| Negotiable | Module names and published packages are in the module map file, not in the test code |
| Valuable | The three teams can change their own module without breaking another |
| Estimable | Folders, one map file, one ArchUnit test class, one front end rule file |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each rule has a test fixture class that breaks it |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Recovery module folder and boundary test

  Background:
    Given the module map lists modules P1 to P10 and S1 to S9 with their packages
    Given the published packages are "<module>.api" and any other package the module map lists for each recovery module, and "..common.api.." for the common module

  Scenario: AC1 Boundary enforced
    Given a class "recovery.casewf.internal.SampleService" that imports "collection.internal.CollectorRepository"
    When the pipeline runs
    Then the boundary test fails the build
    Then the build log names boundary rule BND-1, "SampleService" and "CollectorRepository"

  Scenario: AC2 Published interface allowed
    Given a class "recovery.casewf.internal.SampleService" that calls an interface in "common.api"
    When the pipeline runs
    Then the build passes

  Scenario: AC3 Recovery modules meet only through their api package
    Given a class in "recovery.integration.internal" that imports "recovery.decision.internal.DecisionLogRepository"
    When the pipeline runs
    Then the build fails with boundary rule BND-3
    When the class imports the published "recovery.decision.writer.DecisionLogWriter" instead
    Then the build passes

  Scenario: AC4 A module uses only its own tables
    Given a class in "recovery.integration.internal" that uses the entity "recovery.casewf.internal.RecoveryCaseEntity"
    When the pipeline runs
    Then the build fails with boundary rule BND-4

  Scenario: AC5 No direct call to a system of record
    Given a class in "recovery.casewf.internal" that uses "java.net.http.HttpClient"
    When the pipeline runs
    Then the build fails with boundary rule BND-5
    Then the same use in "recovery.integration.adapter" passes

  Scenario: AC6 Front end boundary
    Given a component in "src/modules/recovery/caselist" that imports "src/modules/collection/worklist/WorkList"
    When the front end build runs
    Then it fails with rule no-collection-import

  Scenario: AC7 A package missing from the module map
    Given a new package "recovery.vendorx" not in the module map
    When the pipeline runs
    Then the build fails with "package recovery.vendorx is not in the module map"
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | boundary rule BND-1: recovery classes depend on the collection module only through its published packages | DT08; ADR-002 |
| BR2 | boundary rule BND-2: recovery classes depend on the common module only through its published packages | DT07; DT08 |
| BR3 | boundary rule BND-3: a recovery module depends on another recovery module only through a package the module map lists as published for it, or an application event | Settled architecture; ADR-002 |
| BR4 | boundary rule BND-4: entities and repositories of a module are used only inside that module | Settled architecture: a module reads only its own tables |
| BR5 | boundary rule BND-5: only the packages the module map allows for client libraries use HTTP, SFTP or file transfer clients: `recovery.integration.adapter` (RWB-E1-007) for files, and the agent runtime client for the enterprise model endpoint INT-23 (RWB-TE-013); no recovery class calls a system of record | REQ-DRI-006; ADR-005 |
| BR6 | Module names, packages and published packages are read from the module map file, not written in the test | Principle 1 applied to build configuration |

The R-BND codes are the names of the boundary test rules in this story. They are not routing rules.

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the build result of a pull request from passed to failed when a rule is broken.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-TRIBE, tribe lead and squad members | Create the folders, the module map and the boundary test |
| TechX tech leads (code owners, RWB-TE-002) | Approve a change to the module map or to the boundary rules |
| ACE team | Names the common and collection published packages (DL05) |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Runs the pipeline |
| No approval level from the delegation of authority applies | The story takes no business decision |

### 11. Data

No business field is read or written. The boundary test reads source and compiled classes only.

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

### 12. Contract

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Every pull request build and every build of main |
| Back end check | RecoveryBoundaryTest, run in the unit test phase |
| Front end check | The dependency rules for `src/modules/recovery`, run in the front end lint step |
| Output | Pass, or fail with the rule code, the class or file and the dependency that broke it |
| Idempotency | The same commit always gives the same result |
| Restart | Rerun the pipeline; the check holds no state |

**Recovery side of the published access check**

```java
// Wired for /api/recovery/v1/**; calls the common module access check (published interface, INT-34)
void RecoveryAccessGuard.require(String capabilityArea, Right right, ScopeTarget target);
//   throws AccessDeniedException mapped to 403 Problem with messageCode MSG-P4-002
```

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Back end folder `ace-service/src/main/java/<ACE base package>/recovery/`, with one package per module: `dataengine` (P1), `integration` (P2), `casewf` (P3), `access` (P4), `dochub` (P5), `comms` (P6), `decision` (P7), `payments` (P8), `reporting` (P9), `agent` (P10), `valuation` (S1), `treatment` (S2), `guarantee` (S3), `litigation` (S4), `asset` (S5), `debtsale` (S6), `writeoff` (S7), `deviation` (S8), `partner` (S9). Each holds `api` for its published interfaces and `internal` for the rest; a story that publishes from another package, for example `recovery.casewf.allocation` (RWB-E1-020) or `recovery.decision.writer` (RWB-E1-027), lists that package as published in the module map. Front end folder `src/modules/recovery/` (ADR-006, DL07).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| recovery-modules.yaml | Rule table | Module code, package, published packages, allowed client libraries |
| RecoveryBoundaryTest | Service | ArchUnit rules boundary rule BND-1 to boundary rule BND-5 built from the module map |
| ModuleMapLoader | Service | Reads the map; fails when a recovery package is not listed (AC7) |
| Boundary fixtures | Service | Test-only classes under `src/test` that break each rule, run with the rule in expect-failure mode |
| RecoveryAccessGuard | Service | Calls the common module access check for every recovery endpoint |
| dependency rule file | Rule table | Front end rules: no import from `src/modules/collection`, imports from `src/common` only through its public index |

**Database.** None.

**Configuration and reference data.** The module map file, owned by the TechX tech leads through code owners (RWB-TE-002). The common module published package names come from the ACE team (DL05).

**Build steps**

1. Create the 19 module packages with `api` and `internal`, a package-info file each, and the front end folder.
2. Write recovery-modules.yaml and ModuleMapLoader with a test for AC7.
3. Write RecoveryBoundaryTest rules boundary rule BND-1 to boundary rule BND-5 with one breaking fixture per rule (AC1, AC3 to AC5).
4. Write the passing fixture that calls a common module published interface (AC2).
5. Add the front end dependency rules and a breaking fixture (AC6).
6. Wire RecoveryAccessGuard with a test-only controller declared Case record R and the access test.
7. Add both checks to the pull request pipeline and confirm a failing fixture blocks a merge.

**Feature flag.** None. A build check has no runtime path to switch off.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, and the pipeline of main shows the boundary test in its unit test report.

### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| Build log | A boundary rule is broken | Rule {code} broken: {class} depends on {dependency}. Use {module}.api or an application event. |
| Build log | A package is not in the module map | package {package} is not in the module map |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right calls a recovery endpoint | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

Build log text is for developers and is not part of the message standard.

### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. A developer reads the result in the pull request checks and the build log.

### 16. Test cases

| ID | Covers | Level | Data |

| TC-TE-001-01 | AC1, BR1 | System | Fixture importing a collection internal class |
| TC-TE-001-02 | AC2, BR2 | System | Fixture calling a common module published interface |

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code; module names and packages are in the module map.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts; fixtures hold class names only.
- No read of another module's tables; this story builds the check that enforces it.
- The breaking fixtures stay in `src/test` and never ship.

## RWB-TE-002 Code owners for the recovery module

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-TE-002 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P2 Integration |
| Feature | None |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-006 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Program, section 7 (constraints Built on ACE and Modular monolith) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | DL37 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-TE-001 |
| Status | Ready for build |

### 1. Story

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a code owners entry that maps every recovery folder to the TechX tech leads and the common module to the ACE team, with review by a code owner required before merge**, so that **every change in the recovery module is reviewed by its owners**.

### 2. Business rationale

The recovery and collection squads and the ACE team merge into one repository and one monthly release. Without named owners per folder, a change to the recovery module or to the common module can merge without the team that answers for it. The code owners file names the reviewing team per folder and the branch rule on main blocks a merge until that team approves. It supports REQ-DRI-006, because the integration adapter folder, the only place allowed to reach other systems, cannot change without a TechX tech lead, and it applies DL04 option A and DL37. The measure is the share of merged pull requests on recovery folders approved by a code owner, which must be 100 percent.

### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-TE-001 is done: the recovery folders and the module map exist.
- The repository host supports a code owners file (GitHub format assumed, as ACE uses GitHub Copilot under DL32).
- The teams exist in the repository host: TechX recovery tech leads and the ACE team. Names assumed until DL37 and DL36 are answered: `@scb-ace/techx-recovery-tech-leads` and `@scb-ace/ace-team`.
- The repository administrator of the ACE team can set the branch rule on main.

### 4. Flow

1. Squad member: writes `.github/CODEOWNERS` with the entries in BR1 to BR5, ordered so that the most specific path is last.
2. Squad member: adds the code owners validation step to the pull request pipeline.
3. ACE team repository administrator: sets the branch rule on main: one approval from a code owner required, stale approvals dismissed on a new commit.
4. Developer: opens a pull request that changes a recovery folder.
5. Repository host: requests review from the owning team named for each changed path.
6. Pipeline: runs the validation step; an owner that does not exist or a path that matches no file fails the check.
7. Code owner: approves; the merge is allowed once every owning team of the changed paths has approved.

### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A pull request changes a recovery folder and only a non owner approves | Merge stays blocked | Repository host: review required from code owners | AC1 |
| X2 | A pull request changes the common module | ACE team review required | Repository host: review required from code owners | AC2 |
| X3 | A pull request changes both recovery and common folders | Both teams must approve | Repository host: review required from code owners | AC3 |
| X4 | The author is a code owner and approves their own change | The author's approval does not count | Repository host: review required from code owners | AC5 |
| X5 | A new commit is pushed after approval | The approval is dismissed; review needed again | Repository host: review required from code owners | AC6 |
| X6 | The code owners file names an owner that does not exist | The validation step fails the build | Build log: owner not found | AC7 |
| X7 | A squad member who is not a code owner tries to satisfy the review | Merge refused | Repository host: review required from code owners | Access test TC-TE-002-08 |

### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the folders from RWB-TE-001 |
| Negotiable | Team names are values in one file (DL37) |
| Valuable | No change to the recovery or common module merges without its owner |
| Estimable | One file, one pipeline step, one branch rule |
| Small | 1 point |
| Testable | Each criterion below is a pull request in a test branch |

### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Code owners for the recovery module

  Background:
    Given the code owners file maps the recovery folders to "@scb-ace/techx-recovery-tech-leads" and the common module folder to "@scb-ace/ace-team"
    Given main requires one code owner approval and dismisses stale approvals

  Scenario: AC1 Review required
    Given a pull request that changes "ace-service/src/main/java/<ACE base path>/recovery/casewf/internal/AllocationService.java"
    When it is opened
    Then a TechX tech lead is required as reviewer
    Then an approval from a squad member outside the team leaves the merge blocked

  Scenario: AC2 A common module change needs the ACE team
    Given a pull request that changes a file under "ace-service/src/main/java/<ACE base path>/common/"
    When it is opened
    Then "@scb-ace/ace-team" is required as reviewer

  Scenario: AC3 A change across both modules needs both teams
    Given a pull request that changes one recovery file and one common module file
    When a TechX tech lead approves
    Then the merge stays blocked until a member of "@scb-ace/ace-team" also approves

  Scenario: AC4 Front end, migrations and the module map are covered
    Given a pull request that changes "ace-web/src/modules/recovery/caselist/CaseListPage.tsx", a file under "ace-service/src/main/resources/db/migration/recovery/" and "architecture/recovery-modules.yaml"
    When it is opened
    Then "@scb-ace/techx-recovery-tech-leads" is required for all three

  Scenario: AC5 An author cannot approve their own change
    Given a TechX tech lead opens a pull request on a recovery folder
    When the same tech lead approves it
    Then the merge stays blocked until a second member of the team approves

  Scenario: AC6 A new commit needs a new approval
    Given an approved pull request on a recovery folder
    When a new commit is pushed to it
    Then the system dismisses the approval and code owner review is required again

  Scenario: AC7 An owner that does not exist fails the check
    Given the code owners file names "@scb-ace/recovery-leads-typo" for a recovery path
    When the pipeline runs
    Then the code owners validation step fails and names the owner not found
```

### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every path under the recovery back end, test and migration folders is owned by the TechX recovery tech leads | DL04 option A; DL37 |
| BR2 | The recovery front end folder and the module map file are owned by the TechX recovery tech leads | ADR-006; DL07 |
| BR3 | The common module folder is owned by the ACE team | DL04 option A; DT07 |
| BR4 | The code owners file itself is owned by both teams | DL04 |
| BR5 | The last matching pattern in the file decides the owner, so specific paths come after general ones | Repository host rule |
| BR6 | A merge to main needs one approval from a code owner of every changed path; an author's own approval does not count; a new commit dismisses approvals | ADR-008; DT11 |
| BR7 | Team names are values in the file; a change of team is a change to the file, reviewed by both teams | DL37 |

### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It sets the review state of a pull request: review required, approved, or dismissed on a new commit.

### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| TechX recovery tech leads | Approve changes to recovery folders and the module map |
| ACE team | Approves changes to the common module and the code owners file; sets the branch rule on main |
| RW-TRIBE, tribe lead and squad members | Open pull requests; cannot satisfy a code owner review unless in the owning team |
| No Workbench capability area applies | Access is a repository right, not a Workbench role right |

### 11. Data

No business field is read or written.

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

### 12. Contract

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| File | `.github/CODEOWNERS` at the repository root |
| Entries | `/ace-service/src/main/java/**/common/ @scb-ace/ace-team`; `/ace-service/src/main/java/**/recovery/ @scb-ace/techx-recovery-tech-leads`; `/ace-service/src/test/java/**/recovery/ @scb-ace/techx-recovery-tech-leads`; `/ace-service/src/main/resources/db/migration/recovery/ @scb-ace/techx-recovery-tech-leads`; `/ace-web/src/modules/recovery/ @scb-ace/techx-recovery-tech-leads`; `/architecture/recovery-modules.yaml @scb-ace/techx-recovery-tech-leads`; `/.github/CODEOWNERS @scb-ace/ace-team @scb-ace/techx-recovery-tech-leads` |
| Branch rule on main | Require a pull request; require review from code owners; 1 approval; dismiss stale approvals; the author's approval does not count |
| Pipeline step | Code owners validation: syntax, every owner exists and has write access, every pattern matches at least one file |
| Trigger | Every pull request that changes any file |
| Idempotency | The same file and the same changed paths always request the same owners |

### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Repository root: `.github/CODEOWNERS` and the pipeline definition of the ACE repository. No Java package.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CODEOWNERS | Rule table | Path to owning team, in the order of BR5 |
| CodeOwnersValidation | Job | Pipeline step that fails on a missing owner or a pattern with no match |
| Branch rule on main | Rule table | Code owner review, one approval, stale approvals dismissed |

**Database.** None.

**Configuration and reference data.** Team names (assumed until DL37 and DL36); the folder paths from RWB-TE-001.

**Build steps**

1. Write the CODEOWNERS file with the entries in section 12, general paths first.
2. Add the validation step to the pull request pipeline and prove it fails on a misspelt team (AC7).
3. Ask the ACE team repository administrator to set the branch rule on main (BR6).
4. Run the six test pull requests in a test branch protected by the same rule (AC1 to AC6) and record the result in the pull request history.

**Feature flag.** None. The file and the branch rule have no runtime path.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and the branch rule on main shows code owner review as required.
